name: The eight precepts
method_summary: On the uposatha, abstaining also from all sexual activity, eating after midday, entertainments and adornment, and high beds (AN 8.41).

name: The invocation gestures (āvāhanī and the rest)
method_summary: The series by which a deity is invited and settled in worship: āvāhanī (the añjali filled with flowers), sthāpanī (the same turned downward), sannidhāpanī (the fists joined, thumbs raised), sannirodhanī (the same with thumbs inside), sammukhīkaraṇī (the fists turned up), with sakalīkaraṇa (placing the six limbs on the deity), avaguṇṭhana (the right fist with the index finger extended, turned around), dhenu (amṛtīkaraṇa) and mahāmudrā (paramīkaraṇa) (ŚT 23.106-114).

name: Calling on the name of Avalokiteśvara
method_summary: Single-mindedly calling the bodhisattva's name in danger or need (Lotus 25).

name: Eating less (ūnodarī)
method_summary: Eating less than one's fill, as external austerity.

name: Analysis of the three states (avasthā-traya-viveka)
method_summary: Observing that waking, dream and sleep and their objects come and go while the consciousness that knows them is uniform and continuous, and identifying with that consciousness.

name: Senseless speech (avitadbhāṣaṇa)
method_summary: He utters meaningless, repetitive or contradictory words.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Senseless acts (avitatkaraṇa)
method_summary: He handles sticks, clods and the like as one who cannot tell pure from impure or fit from unfit, without breaking the restraints.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Worship of the imperishable unmanifest (akṣara / avyakta upāsanā)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Worshipping the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, constant — while restraining the whole group of the senses, being even in understanding everywhere and delighting in the welfare of all beings; such worshippers also reach the Lord (12.3–4).
prerequisites: restraint of the whole group of the senses (12.4)
evenness of understanding everywhere (12.4)
delight in the welfare of all beings (12.4)

warnings.text: Greater is the hardship of those whose awareness (cetas) is attached to the unmanifest; for the unmanifest goal is reached with difficulty by the embodied.

notes: New practice for 12.3–5, combining extractor A's prc:avyakta-upasana and extractor B's prc:worship-of-the-imperishable-unmanifest. Commentators identify the object differently: Śaṅkara as brahman beyond all attributes, Rāmānuja as the individual self's own nature (recalled; see dsp:bhagavad-gita-lord-or-unmanifest); the text names it only akṣara and avyakta.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch10-12): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

signs_of_progress: They too reach the Lord (12.4).

name: Awareness of arising thoughts
method_summary: 'When a thought arises, be aware of it; when aware of it, it vanishes'; 'do not fear thoughts arising, only fear being slow to notice'.

warnings.text: Wumen lists 'being aware of thoughts as they arise' among Chan faults ('toying with spirits') when taken as an end.

name: Āyambil (plain-food fast)
method_summary: A day with one meal of plain boiled grain or pulses without salt, oil, spices, milk or sweets, eaten once; repeated during the Navapada Olī.

name: Dwelling in the temple (āyatanavāsa)
method_summary: The first-stage practitioner lives in a temple built by another, under his teacher, as one lives on a riverbank.

name: Rites for long life (āyuṣya)
method_summary: Recitations and rites to hold back death and restore life-breath, keeping the person 'in the world of the living' (AVŚ 8.1).

name: Baddhapadmāsana (the bound lotus)
method_summary: Padmāsana with the arms crossed behind the back holding the big toes (HYP 1.44; GS 2.8); named as the seat for purifying the channels (HYP 2.7; GŚ 41, 43) and in Dattātreya's own posture (DYŚ 5).
prerequisites: padmāsana
notes: The Triśikhibrāhmaṇa lists baddhapadma separately from padma.

name: Bahiṣkṛta-dhauti (the outward washing)
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: described as filling the belly with air by kākī mudrā and holding it, then, standing in navel-deep water, drawing out and washing the 'śakti-nāḍī' (the lower bowel) and returning it (GS 1.22-25). Procedure and durations are not reproduced.

warnings.text: This washing is secret and hard to attain even for the gods.
The great bahiṣkṛta-dhauti does not arise until one can hold (the air) for a long period.

name: The meditation taught to Bālāki
method_summary: Pass beyond venerating the persons in the sun, moon and other phenomena as brahman to the self into which the sleeper withdraws and from which all breaths, worlds and gods come forth.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

queries: prepared segments: BĀU 2.1, KauU 4
checks.note: All 2 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (BĀU 2.1; KauU 4). It rests on 5 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Blood offering to the Goddess (bali)
method_summary: The offering of animal victims to the Goddess taught in the Kālikā Purāṇa's offering chapter and practised at Kāmākhyā and in Bengal. Restricted: summary only — no victims' lists, durations or procedure.

warnings.text: A brāhmaṇa who offers a lion, tiger or man goes to hell; offering one's own blood is self-slaughter; by offering wine a brāhmaṇa falls from his class.
A human offering without the king's permission is sin.
Pumpkin, sugarcane and spirits are declared equal to a victim.

name: The three locks together (bandha-traya)
method_summary: Mūla, uḍḍīyāna and jālandhara applied together: contracting the base, drawing back the belly and binding iḍā and piṅgalā, the breath is made to flow in the back (central) path and dissolves (HYP 3.74-76); in breath-control they are timed to inhalation, retention and exhalation (HYP 2.45-47). The texts say they arise spontaneously in a mastered siddhāsana (HYP 1.42) and that siṃhāsana brings them about (HYP 1.52).

queries: e-text refs of prc:bandha-traya
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 3 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

signs_of_progress: then there is no death, old age or disease (HYP 3.75)
the means in all the haṭha teachings (HYP 3.76)
alt_method_summary: Root, abdominal and throat locks applied with breath-practice to turn the breaths upward and keep them in the suṣumnā.

name: Training for the bardos
method_summary: Practising in life the recognitions to be made after death: resting in the clear light, seeing appearances as self-display, dream yoga, the peaceful and wrathful deities, the root verses of the six bardos.

name: Intermediate-state yoga (bar do)
method_summary: Training in the three bardos: inner heat and illusory body in life, dream yoga in sleep, and at death recognizing the clear light in the dissolution; failing that, arising as illusory body in the bardo, or blocking or choosing rebirth.
alt_method_summary: At death, recognizing the withdrawal of senses and elements and the gathering of winds at the heart, the yogin meditates deity yoga or rests in reality; when turning toward rebirth, meditates all appearance as the deity, thereby 'blocking' the intermediate state (Tilopa, from Sukhasiddhi).

name: Singing bargīts
method_summary: The rāga songs of Śaṅkaradeva and Mādhavadeva are sung, often at dawn and at the opening of sattra services, with prescribed rāga and tāla.

name: Basti / jala-basti (the water enema)
method_summary: Squatting in utkaṭāsana in water up to the navel with a tube in the anus, one contracts the base (ādhāra) and washes (HYP 2.26-28); the Gheraṇḍa's water-basti is done likewise in navel-deep water with contraction and expansion of the anus (GS 1.45-47).
signs_of_progress: gulma, spleen disorders, dropsy and diseases of vāta, pitta and kapha are destroyed; clarity of tissues, senses and mind; lustre; kindled fire (HYP 2.27-28)
removes urinary disorders, gudāvarta and harsh wind (GS 1.47)

warnings.text: One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.
Some teachers hold that all impurities are dried up by breath-control alone and do not approve of the other acts.
The six acts, which purify the body, are to be kept secret.

name: Bāul body practice (deha-sādhanā) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. A secret, guru-given practice of the couple and of the body's substances and breath, aimed at reversing the downward current and 'catching' the Man of the Heart in the body; recorded here only as its aim and the tradition's warnings — no method is given.

sources.ref: songs of the uncatchable Man and the tide

warnings.text: Only under a guru and after long preparation; without mastery of desire it leads to ruin and to the downward fall.
The practice is secret and must not be revealed to the unqualified.

name: Bāul initiation and instruction (dīkṣā and śikṣā)
method_summary: A first initiation (dīkṣā) by a guru with a mantra, and later instruction (śikṣā), often from a second guru, into the body practice; the teaching is given individually and kept secret.

warnings.text: The practice is not to be learned from books or songs without a guru.

name: Song as practice (gān)
method_summary: Singing with the ektārā and dotārā as devotion, as teaching of the doctrine and as coded transmission of practice; the singer loses himself in the song of the Man.

name: Nenbutsu at special times (betsuji nenbutsu)
method_summary: Intensive nenbutsu for fixed periods (a day to ninety days), and the deathbed practice, as taught in the Ōjōyōshū's sixth chapter.

name: Bhadrāsana (the auspicious seat)
method_summary: The ankles under the scrotum at the sides of the perineum, the sides of the feet held firmly with the hands (HYP 1.53-54); in the Gheraṇḍa the ankles are crossed, the big toes held from behind, jālandhara applied and the gaze on the nose-tip (GS 2.9-10).
signs_of_progress: destroys all diseases (HYP 1.54; GS 2.10)

names.name: gorakṣāsana (so called by the siddha yogins, HYP 1.54)

equivalents.note: HYP 1.54 says the siddhas call bhadrāsana gorakṣāsana; GS 2.24-25 describes a distinct gorakṣāsana.

notes: Listed in the Yoga-bhāṣya on YS 2.46. U10's paraphrase of that list omits vīrāsana; the unit recalls 'padmāsanaṃ vīrāsanaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ svastikaṃ …' — check the bhāṣya.

name: Meditation on the self seated in the yoni (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: an opponent's one-line report that the Kāpālas attain nirvāṇa by meditating on the self as seated in the yoni. No further description is recorded here.
notes: Sexual rite category: restricted, summary only.

name: Meditation on the Lord in the heart-lotus (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Seated evenly with gaze at the nose-tip, after breath purification with Oṃ, visualize the eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the four-armed Lord in the fire; meditate on each limb, then on the smiling face, then fix the mind in space and finally think of nothing, seeing the self in the Lord as light in light.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:bhagavata-heart-lotus-dhyana
checks.note: Rests on tea:uddhava-gita:11.14.32-46; each was located in the local text and matches this entry's statement.

signs_of_progress: the delusion of object, knowledge and act ceases (11.14.46)

name: Service to devotees (bhāgavata-kainkarya)
method_summary: Honouring and serving the Lord's devotees regardless of their birth, which the teachers rank above service to the Lord himself; avoiding any offence against them.

name: The seven-day hearing of the Bhāgavata (saptāha)
method_summary: A formal recital of the whole Bhāgavata over seven days, modelled on Śuka's teaching to Parīkṣit, with vows for the hearers; the Māhātmya praises it above sacrifice, vows, yoga and meditation and tells how it freed the preta Dhundhukārī.
duration: seven days

queries: rests_on teachings and cited refs located
checks.note: Bhāgavata Māhātmya chs. 1-6 (local) located. All teachings it rests on were located in the local e-texts (see their checks).

name: The twelve yamas and twelve niyamas (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Practising the twelve restraints and twelve observances listed in 11.19.33-35.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:bhagavata-yamas-niyamas
checks.note: Rests on tea:uddhava-gita:11.19.33-35; each was located in the local text and matches this entry's statement.

name: The circle worship (bhairavī-cakra, tattva-cakra)
method_summary: Collective Kaula worship in a circle of initiates in which caste distinctions are suspended for its duration. Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: The Tattva circle is truly performed only by those in whom 'all is Brahman' arises.
After the circle all castes are separate again.

The wilful, the uninitiated, one who drinks the unconsecrated substance, takes a woman by force or kills for his own pleasure, and the addict without Kaula instruction go to hell; the intoxicated Kaula knows neither meditation nor God nor guru and falls.

name: Atharvavedic healing rites (bhaiṣajya)
method_summary: Healing by recitation of the hymns with plants, water, amulets, fire and the sun, touching the patient, and sending the disease away to distant places or creatures (fever, jaundice, leprosy, worms, consumption).
notes: Summary only; the Kauśika Sūtra gives the rite details (U02).

name: Bhaiṣajyaguru rites for the sick and dying
method_summary: Keeping the Medicine Buddha's name, reciting the sūtra, lighting lamps and hanging banners to prolong life and heal.
notes: The number of lamps and days of the rite are given in the Chinese versions; not recorded here.

name: Bhajan (listening to the sound current)
method_summary: Listening within to the inner sound (with the ears closed in some lines), selecting the sound from the right side and letting it draw the attention upward.

name: Devotional singing (bhajana, bhajan)
method_summary: Singing devotional songs and names of the deity, usually in a group led by a lead singer, with simple rhythm instruments; in the South Indian bhajana tradition an ordered sequence of songs and names to many deities culminating in the Lord's name; in the Vārkarī tradition singing the abhaṅgas of the saints; in the Sant tradition singing the śabdas of Kabīr and others.
signs_of_progress: melting of the heart and tears (BhP 11.14.24)
alt_method_summary: Groups sing abhaṅgas, padas or dohās and the name together with cymbals and drum, in the evening, at festivals and on the road; in the Vārkarī form a leader sings and the group answers.

name: The devotee's conduct: non-violence, truth, purity, compassion, faith
method_summary: Carefully keeping non-violence, truthfulness, purity, compassion, faith and the other virtues (NBS 78); giving up pride and hypocrisy (NBS 64), since the Lord dislikes pride and loves humility (NBS 27).

name: Reflecting on the scriptures of devotion
method_summary: The scriptures of devotion are to be reflected upon and the acts that awaken devotion done (NBS 76); no half-moment wasted waiting for a better time (NBS 77); but disputation is avoided (NBS 74–75).

name: Bhakti-yoga: loving meditation (upāsana, dhruvānusmṛti)
method_summary: Daily, repeated meditation on the Lord (in one of the Upaniṣadic forms, the vidyās) as one's inner self, until it becomes unbroken, vivid as sight and full of love; supported by the seven aids and by duties done as worship, continued until death, with remembrance at the last moment.
stage: for those qualified by birth, learning and capacity (traivarṇika) after karma- and jñāna-yoga
prerequisites: the seven aids (sādhana-saptaka)
karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga leading to the vision of the self
duration: daily until death
signs_of_progress: vividness equal to seeing (darśana-samānākāra)
parabhakti, parajñāna, paramabhakti

warnings.text: It is long and difficult, obstructed by accumulated sins, and requires the last remembrance at death; hence prapatti is taught for those unable.

name: Devotional drama (bhāonā)
method_summary: An aṅkīyā nāṭ is staged in the nāmghar with the sūtradhāra singing and dancing, masks, music and song; performing and watching are acts of worship.

name: Bharanyāsa: the rite of laying down one's burden
method_summary: The formal performance of surrender, in which one places the burden of one's protection and its fruit on the Lord, with the sāttvika-tyāga; performed by oneself, by repeating after the teacher, or by the teacher on one's behalf.

name: Wearing the sacred ash and rudrākṣa
method_summary: Smearing tirunīṟu (in three horizontal lines) and wearing rudrākṣa beads as the marks of Śiva's devotee; praised as mantra and medicine.

name: Rejuvenation with metallic and mineral preparations
method_summary: Later Āyurveda and the rasa texts use calcined metals, minerals and mercurial compounds as rejuvenatives and medicines. RESTRICTED: summary only; no preparations or doses.

warnings.text: Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.
Impure minerals and metals destroy life (impure pyrite causes death without doubt; impure copper and iron destroy life, strength and lustre).
Mercury is not to be used where a vital point is injured or in burns from caustic or fire.

name: Ash-bath (bhasma-snāna)
method_summary: Bathing the body in ash with the five brahma-mantras — the 'fire-bath' ranked above water-baths and enjoined for ascetics.

queries: e-text refs of prc:bhasma-snana
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 5 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text. Some rest on teachings whose ref was corrected or only partly confirmed; the content is located, only the numbering changes: tea:jabali-upanisad:3-4 (partially-confirmed).

alt_method_summary: Smearing the whole body with ash prepared with mantras (Bṛhajjābāla; Bhasmajābāla; Atharvaśiras).

name: Lying in ash (bhasmaśayana)
method_summary: The practitioner sleeps and lies on ash.

name: Bathing in ash (bhasmasnāna)
method_summary: At each of the three junctures of the day the practitioner purifies himself, takes ash consecrated with the mantras and rubs it over the whole body while muttering, then enters the temple.
prerequisites: Pāśupata initiation

name: Bhastrikā ('the bellows')
method_summary: Seated in padmāsana, the breath is expelled and drawn in forcefully through the nose again and again like a blacksmith's bellows, sounding in heart, throat and skull; when tired, one fills through the right nostril, holds with the nostrils closed and releases through the left (HYP 2.59-67; GS 5.76-78). The numbers of strokes and rounds given in the Gheraṇḍa are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: removes vāta, pitta and kapha, increases the bodily fire, quickly awakens kuṇḍalinī, destroys the phlegm barring the mouth of the brahma-channel, pierces the three knots (HYP 2.65-67)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
When fatigue arises in the body the bellows-breathing is to give way to filling through the sun (right) nostril.

name: Inner worship with offerings of feeling (bhāva-pūjā)
method_summary: Worship of the inner liṅga of consciousness in the heart-shrine with inner offerings — forbearance as bath, discrimination as cloth, truth as ornament, dispassion as garland, samādhi as scent, freedom from ego as rice, faith as incense, knowledge as lamp, the world as food-offering, silence as bell.

equivalents.note: inner worship with mental offerings; here directed to the prāṇaliṅga and ranked above ritual worship

name: Contemplation of the body as the Śrīcakra (Bhāvanā Upaniṣad)
method_summary: Each part of the Śrīcakra and each deity is identified with a constituent of one's body and mind (channels, vital airs, fires, qualities, subtle elements, inner organ, lunar days); the offerings are made as inner acts; the worship is the contemplation of the non-difference of knower, knowing and known. Bhāskararāya wrote a procedure (prayoga) for it.
duration: three muhūrtas of absorption (as the Upaniṣad states)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā
signs_of_progress: identity with the deity; intentions fulfilled without effort; called a Śiva-yogin (Bhāvanā Upaniṣad)

name: Bheda-vijñāna (discriminating self from non-self)
method_summary: Repeatedly discerning that the knowing self is other than body, karma, passions and thoughts — 'I am one, pure, made of perception and knowledge; nothing else, not even an atom, is mine' — and resting in self-experience; the core practice of the Adhyātma path.
signs_of_progress: self-experience (svānubhūti)
calm of the passions

warnings.text: Taking the ultimate standpoint alone while abandoning conduct is itself a wrong view (niścayābhāsa).

equivalents.note: Discrimination of seer and seen in Yoga; the Jain knower is an agent with modes.

name: Taking the garb (bhek; among Fakirs khilāphat)
method_summary: Initiation into mendicant life with the robe (ālkhāllā) and begging bowl, performed with a symbolic funeral of the old self in some lines; the fakiri counterpart is khilāphat.
notes: The 'symbolic funeral' detail is recalled from ethnographic reports with low confidence.

name: The twelve special vows of the monk (bhikṣu-pratimā)
method_summary: A series of twelve progressively severe undertakings for qualified monks, restricting alms to one or a few 'portions' of food and drink for a month or more at a time and ending in intense night-long standing meditation (restricted: prolonged fasting — summary only).

warnings.text: Only for monks of sufficient bodily strength, scriptural learning and years of standing, with the teacher's permission.

name: Moderation in eating
method_summary: Eating with reflection, not for amusement, intoxication or beautification, but to sustain the body and support the holy life (MN 39; MN 107).

name: Bhrāmarī ('the bee')
method_summary: In the Haṭhapradīpikā, rapid inhalation with the sound of a male bee and very slow exhalation with the hum of a female bee (HYP 2.68). In the Gheraṇḍa, practised after midnight in silence with the ears closed, it becomes a practice of listening: the inner sounds are heard in the right ear, from crickets and flute to drums and vīṇā, and the mind dissolves in the light within the unstruck sound (GS 5.79-83); it is the Gheraṇḍa's means to nāda-samādhi (GS 7.5-6, 7.10-11).
signs_of_progress: a play of indescribable bliss in the minds of the best yogins (HYP 2.68)
the inner sounds, a light within the sound, dissolution of the mind — 'Viṣṇu's supreme state' (GS 5.80-83)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.

name: Gazing / meditating between the brows (bhrūmadhya-dṛṣṭi)
method_summary: The gaze and attention fixed at the point between the eyebrows: in siddhāsana and mahāmudrā (HYP 1.35; GS 2.7, 3.7), with khecarī (HYP 3.32; GS 3.27), in mūrcchā (GS 5.84), and as a practice of its own — 'unmanī is quickly attained by meditation between the brows; this is my view' (HYP 4.80); 'between the brows is the place of Śiva, where mind dissolves' (HYP 4.48). The Dattātreyayogaśāstra counts it among the laya signals (DYŚ 21).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch07-09): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.
Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

signs_of_progress: unmanī quickly; the laya born of nāda (HYP 4.80)
no fear of death while breath is held and gaze is between the brows (HYP 2.40)
alt_method_summary: Shutting out external contacts and fixing the gaze between the eyebrows while equalizing the breaths (5.27); at death setting the breath fully between the brows with devotion and yoga-power (8.10).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.10: at the time of departure the yogin, with steady mind, devotion and the power of yoga, makes the breath (prāṇa) enter fully between the brows and so reaches the supreme divine Person.

Having put external contacts outside, the gaze (cakṣus) is placed between the eyebrows, and prāṇa and apāna moving within the nostrils are made even; the sage so restrained, intent on liberation and free of desire, fear and anger is forever free (5.27–28). The text gives no further method.

Passing beyond the supports, the yogin gazes at the middle of eyes, nose and forehead and on the guru as a flame of grace (Tirumūla ñāṉam 5); Pattirakiriyār longs to see the light of bliss straight at the forehead (227).
notes: In 6.13 the Gītā instead prescribes gazing toward the tip of the nose; the text does not relate the two instructions.

name: Bhujaṅgāsana (the serpent)
method_summary: From the toes to the navel the body rests on the ground; supporting the ground with the palms one raises the head like a serpent (GS 2.42-43).
signs_of_progress: the bodily fire increases, all diseases are destroyed and the serpent goddess (kuṇḍalinī) awakens (GS 2.43)

name: Bhujaṅginī mudrā ('the serpentine')
method_summary: With the mouth slightly opened and the neck stretched, air is drunk in through the gullet like a serpent (GS 3.92-93).
signs_of_progress: destroys old age and death; quickly removes diseases of the belly, especially indigestion (GS 3.92-93)

name: The meditation on plenitude (bhūma-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate in ascending order name, speech, mind, intention, thought, meditation, understanding, strength, food, water, heat, space, memory, hope and breath as brahman, each greater than the one before; then seek to understand truth, understanding, thinking, faith, steadfastness, action and happiness, up to plenitude (bhūman), where one sees nothing else; then the teaching of 'I' and of the self.
signs_of_progress: freedom of movement as far as each object reaches; the self-ruled moves at will in all worlds (ChU 7.25.2)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

queries: prepared segments: ChU 7.25.2, ChU 7.1-7.26
checks.note: All 2 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ChU 7.25.2; ChU 7.1-7.26). It rests on 5 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūta-śuddhi)
method_summary: Named in the Devī Gītā as a preliminary of daily worship (procedure not described here).

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:bhuta-suddhi
checks.note: Rests on tea:devi-gita:7.40.1-7; each was located in the local text and matches this entry's statement.

notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.
alt_method_summary: In Gauḍīya deity worship (Haribhaktivilāsa, following Pāñcarātra and tantric manuals), the worshipper purifies the elements of the body by meditation and places mantras on the limbs (nyāsa) before worship.

name: Meditative cultivation of a real object (to yogic perception)
method_summary: A real object (above all the four truths) is cultivated until, at its culmination, it appears vividly and without conceptual construction — yogic perception.

warnings.text: Vividness alone does not make a cognition valid: those overcome by desire, grief, fear, madness or dream also see unreal things as if before them.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi)
method_summary: In the preliminaries to worship the practitioner mentally dissolves the elements of the body, from earth upward, into their sources, burns away the impure body, and re-creates a pure divine body with mantras before placing mantras on it. Summary only.
alt_method_summary: Purification of the elements of the body by meditation and mantra before worship.

name: Wall-gazing (biguan)
method_summary: Bodhidharma's 'abiding firmly in wall-gazing' in which self and other, ordinary and holy are one; in the tradition, his nine years sitting facing a wall at Shaolin.

name: Seed-syllables of the centres and elements
method_summary: Meditating on, or softly intoning, the seed-syllable of each centre with its element — laṃ (earth, root centre), vaṃ (water, svādhiṣṭhāna), raṃ (fire, maṇipūra), yaṃ (air, anāhata), haṃ (space, viśuddhi), oṃ (ājñā) — together with its shape, colour, deity and the letters on its petals; the same seeds are used in the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) before worship, where the elements of the body are dissolved upward into their sources and a divine body is re-created.
prerequisites: initiation and instruction by a guru

warnings.text: The rousing of kuṇḍalinī through the centres is to be done by the method learned from the guru.

equivalents.note: bhūtaśuddhi uses the element seeds
duplicate id of bhūtaśuddhi

name: Contemplation of oneself as the reflection of Nārāyaṇa
method_summary: Seated upright during the purifications before worship, one contemplates Nārāyaṇa in the lotus of the heart and one's own self before him as his reflection, and prays: 'You are the original, I am the reflection, though there is a difference between us; flawless Lord, separate my faults from me.'
prerequisites: dīkṣā
ritual purity
signs_of_progress: removal of sin, according to the text
notes: A step within daily worship rather than a free-standing meditation; ritual details omitted.

name: Libation into the bindu (bindu-tarpaṇa)
method_summary: Offering libations of the consecrated special water into the central point of the Śrīcakra to satisfy the Goddess (LSN 178); substances vary by mode (Kaula or with substitutes). Summary only.

name: Arousing the thought of awakening (bodhicittotpāda)
method_summary: Resolving to attain full buddhahood for the sake of all beings — the entry into the bodhisattva path, renewed throughout it; the Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha requires it even of the lowest aspirants.
signs_of_progress: irreversibility (Aṣṭa 17)
alt_method_summary: In the Jewel Ornament: generating aspiring and engaging bodhicitta in a ritual and training in its precepts.

name: Receiving the Brahmajāla bodhisattva precepts
method_summary: Receiving the ten major and forty-eight minor precepts, open to lay and ordained, and reciting them fortnightly; in Japanese Tendai (Saichō) the sole ordination precepts.

name: Taking the bodhisattva vows (praṇidhāna)
method_summary: Formulating vows for beings' welfare — Śrīmālā's ten vows and three aspirations, the Avataṃsaka's vows attached to every daily act, the great vows of Samantabhadra.
alt_method_summary: Atiśa: taken from a qualified teacher by the rite of the Bodhisattvabhūmi's ethics chapter, or, lacking a teacher, by Mañjuśrī's (Ambarāja's) rite before the buddhas; requires a prātimokṣa basis.

Before the Buddhas, following the Sugatas of old, one generates the awakening mind and undertakes to train in the bodhisattva trainings in due order; the Śikṣāsamuccaya sets out the vow (saṃvara) and the root downfalls to be avoided, drawn from the sūtras.
Taken in the Kagyu according to the Jewel Ornament's ritual of bodhicitta.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).
prerequisites: refuge
the sevenfold worship

warnings.text: One who promises happiness to the whole world and then deceives it faces a worse destiny than one who fails to give a trifle he intended to give.

name: Taking and keeping the bodhisattva vow (Yogācāra rite)
method_summary: The vow of the threefold discipline is taken before a teacher who holds it and is learned and capable (or, lacking one, before the buddhas); the four offences equivalent to defeat and the lesser faults are avoided; a lost vow may be retaken; lesser faults are confessed.

warnings.text: An offence committed with strong affliction destroys the vow.

equivalents.note: the Yogācāra ('vast conduct') form of the bodhisattva vow, distinct from the Madhyamaka form of the Śikṣāsamuccaya

name: Offering the body or its parts by fire (Lotus 23)
method_summary: The Lotus's Bhaiṣajyarāja chapter praises a past bodhisattva who burned his body as an offering and says burning a finger or toe at a stūpa exceeds offering kingdoms; East Asian ordination customs of burning incense marks derive from it. Summary only.

warnings.text: The same chapter ranks keeping even one four-line verse of the sūtra above all such bodily offerings.
The Vinaya forbids monks and nuns to harm their own bodies or seek death; Chinese critics (e.g. Yijing) opposed such offerings as contrary to the Vinaya.
warnings.ref: (Vinaya rules on self-harm; Yijing's account — from memory, unverified)

notes: Restricted category: no method recorded.

name: Contemplating the body's impurity
method_summary: Reflecting on the body as a compound of bones, flesh, blood and impurities to loosen attachment (Nāradaparivrājaka 3; Maitreya 2).

name: The body maṇḍala
method_summary: Meditating the deities and the twenty-four sites of the Heruka maṇḍala in the parts and channels of one's own body, associated especially with Ghaṇṭāpa's five-deity Cakrasaṃvara.
notes: The attribution of the body-maṇḍala system to Ghaṇṭāpa follows Tibetan presentations.

name: Body scanning (observation of sensations)
method_summary: Moving attention systematically through the body, part by part, from head to feet and back, observing whatever sensation is present — gross or subtle — with equanimity and the understanding of impermanence; later sweeping the body in free flow.
prerequisites: five precepts
three days of mindfulness of respiration

warnings.text: Practise only within a course under an authorized teacher; do not mix with other techniques (the tradition's own rule).

name: Bön preliminaries
method_summary: Preliminaries of the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü and other cycles: impermanence, refuge, bodhicitta, purification, maṇḍala, guru yoga, each accumulated.
notes: Optional (Bön).

name: Meditation on brahman under stated aspects (Taittirīya 3.10.2-3.10.4)
method_summary: Meditating on "that" (tat; not named in the passage, the vallī's subject being brahman) as support, as great, as mind, as homage, as brahman, as the "death-around" of brahman, each with its fruit; the text also lists aspects in speech, breath, hands, feet, excretory organ, rain, lightning, cattle, stars, generative organ and space. Summary only.

checks.note: Corrected by J: method_summary: the object "that" (tat) is not named in 3.10.2-3; "brahman" is now marked as the vallī's subject rather than the passage's word.

name: The Upaniṣadic meditations (brahma-vidyās)
method_summary: Specific forms of meditation on Brahman taught in the Upaniṣads (such as the Dahara, Śāṇḍilya, Madhu and Antarākṣi vidyās), traditionally counted as thirty-two; each is a form of bhakti-yoga, chosen and practised according to the rules of the Brahma Sūtras' third chapter.
notes: The count of thirty-two and the list are recalled with low confidence.

name: Practice of Brahman (brahmābhyāsa)
method_summary: Thinking of Brahman, speaking of it, awakening one another to it and being wholly devoted to it; spending nights in reflection on the teaching of the Self.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:brahmabhyasa
checks.note: Rests on tea:moksopaya:3.22.23-26; each was located in the local text and matches this entry's statement.

alt_method_summary: Thinking of Brahman, speaking of it, instructing one another in it, and being wholly devoted to it — the constant practice recommended after knowledge dawns (quoted in the Pañcadaśī from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha).

name: Continence (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Restraint of the generative organ in one whose senses are guarded (YBh 2.30). Restricted-adjacent (sexual topic): only the definition is recorded.

signs_of_progress: Vigour (vīrya) is gained (YS 2.38).

Restraint of the generative organ with the senses guarded (YBh 2.30).

Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): the third support of life, 'the best of paths'; required of the medical student and of the one taking rejuvenation; sexual activity only in measure and at permitted times and places.

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): what people call sacrifice, offering, the long session, silence, fasting and forest-life is really brahmacarya (ChU 8.5); the brahma-world belongs to those who find it by brahmacarya (8.4.3); living in the teacher's house (ChU 2.23.1; 8.15.1).

prerequisites: initiation (upanayana)
notes: U01 contribution: the Atharvavedic studentship. Other units contribute brahmacarya as celibacy (yama).
alt_notes: Named only as the discipline of those seeking the imperishable; no method given in this chunk.
The verse says only 'the vow of the brahmacārin' (brahmacāri-vrata); commentators gloss it as celibacy together with the Vedic student's other restraints.

name: Offering sacrifice by sacrifice into the fire of Brahman
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.25: others offer sacrifice by means of sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman. The verse gives no further detail (commentators read it as offering the self into Brahman, or the sacrificial act itself).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

name: Offering as Brahman (brahmārpaṇa)
method_summary: Performing the offering while seeing each factor as Brahman — the offering or ladle, the oblation, the fire, the offerer — with concentration on action as Brahman; Brahman is what such a one reaches (4.24). Related: acting having placed one's actions in Brahman and abandoned attachment, one is untouched by evil like a lotus leaf by water (5.10).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

signs_of_progress: Brahman alone is reached (4.24)

name: Brahmasambandha initiation
method_summary: The second initiation of the Puṣṭimārga, following the refuge mantra: the disciple, holding tulasī, dedicates body, senses, life, mind and possessions to Kṛṣṇa through a formula given privately by a Gosvāmī ācārya; thereafter everything is offered before use.

name: Development of the four divine abidings (brahmavihāra)
method_summary: Vism IX p. 318-319: the four divine abidings are loving-kindness, compassion, gladness and equanimity; the text gives each a mark, function, manifestation, proximate cause, success and failure, a common purpose (pleasant abiding in insight and success in existence) and a special purpose (loving-kindness against ill will, compassion against cruelty, gladness against discontent, equanimity against lust), and a near and a far enemy for each: for loving-kindness lust is near and ill will far; for compassion household-based displeasure near and cruelty far; for gladness household-based gladness near and discontent far; for equanimity the household-based equanimity of ignorance near, lust and resentment far. In Vism III they are listed among the forty: the first three bring three jhānas (fourfold count); for the fourth divine abiding the edition prints "catukkajjhānikā" (read by the extractor, in the notes of tea:visuddhimagga:3.p111/2, as the fourth jhāna; the page does not say so in those words); they suit the hating temperament.

alt_method_summary: Abiding pervading one direction, then the second, third and fourth, above, below, across and everywhere, with a mind of love, compassion, rejoicing and equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity (DN 13; MN 7; AN 3.65).
signs_of_progress: no limited deed remains (DN 13)
the four assurances (AN 3.65)

equivalents.note: YS 1.33 prescribes the four attitudes towards the happy, the suffering, the virtuous and the non-virtuous for clarity of mind

name: Riddle exchange (brahmodya)
method_summary: A ritual exchange of riddles about the cosmos between priests (e.g. at the horse sacrifice: 'who moves alone?' — 'the sun moves alone'), testing and displaying knowledge of hidden correspondences.

name: Service at the saints' brindāvanas
method_summary: Worship, circumambulation and vows at the tomb-shrines (brindāvanas) of Mādhva saints — above all Rāghavendra's at Mantrālaya and the Nava Brindāvana near Hampi — where the tradition holds the saints to remain present.
notes: Living practice described from general knowledge; no textual source checked.

name: Recollection of the Buddha's body and qualities
method_summary: Calling to mind the Tathāgata's golden body, marks and qualities until samādhi, knowing the buddha recollected to be neither form nor formless.

names.name: Genshin's particular, general and abbreviated contemplations

name: Recollection of the Buddha
method_summary: Recollecting 'the Blessed One is an arahant, fully awakened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, well-farer, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed trainer, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed' (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)
faith and gladness
access concentration
alt_method_summary: Recollecting the Buddha's special qualities ('accomplished, fully enlightened …') until the mind is filled with faith and gladness; reaches access.

name: Buddhiyoga, the yoga of understanding (BhG 2.39–53)
method_summary: Hold the understanding 'according to yoga' in acting (2.39): a single, resolute understanding (2.41); take refuge in understanding rather than making the fruit the motive (2.49); be the same in success and failure — equanimity is yoga, and yoga is skill in actions (2.48, 2.50); let the understanding cross the thicket of delusion and stand immovable in samādhi (2.52–53).

warnings.text: The understandings of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
For those attached to enjoyment and lordship, carried away by the flowery speech of the ritual-minded, resolute understanding is not established in samādhi.
Wretched are those whose motive is the fruit.

stage: all; culminates in understanding immovable in samādhi (2.53)
signs_of_progress: No effort is lost and even a little protects from great fear (2.40); casting off good and evil deeds (2.50); freedom from the bondage of birth (2.51); nirveda towards what is heard (2.52); attaining yoga (2.53).

name: Recitation of 'buddho'
method_summary: Silent repetition of 'buddho' — alone or 'bud-' with the in-breath and '-dho' with the out-breath — until the mind settles; then the word is dropped and the breath or body is contemplated.

equivalents.note: a form of recollection of the Buddha used as a concentration word

name: Recollection of one's generosity
method_summary: Recollecting one's own generosity, living at home with a mind free of the stain of avarice (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)
faith and gladness
access concentration
alt_method_summary: Recollecting one's own generosity, free from the stain of avarice; reaches access.

name: Veneration of the Jina (caityavandana)
method_summary: A liturgy of salutation before the image or a representation of the Jina, with prostrations, the Śakrastava ('namo'tthu ṇaṃ') and hymns; Haribhadra's Lalitavistarā comments on it.

name: Cakrasaṃvara practice
method_summary: Kagyu contribution: the principal Kagyu yidam; his empowerment (the sixty-two-deity maṇḍala) opens the six dharmas; generation-stage practice precedes the completion stage.
notes: U44 owns the Indian Cakrasaṃvara practice; shared id.

name: Cakrī (the 'wheel' act)
method_summary: One of the eight cleansing acts of the Haṭharatnāvalī, added to the Haṭhapradīpikā's six (with gajakaraṇī); it is a cleansing of the anus — the unit recalls it as done by rotating the finger there, like the Gheraṇḍa's mūlaśodhana.
notes: Method recalled with low confidence; check the Haṭharatnāvalī.

name: The Cākṣuṣmatī vidyā
method_summary: Praise of the Sun for health of the eyes; one who knows it has no eye disease and none in his family is blind (Akṣi 1).

checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 1 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

name: Calm abiding according to the lamrim
method_summary: Having gathered the prerequisites, one sits in the eight-featured posture, takes an object (often the visualised body of the Buddha), and progresses through the nine mental states by the six powers and four attentions, applying the eight antidotes to the five faults — above all recognising gross and subtle laxity and excitement with alertness — until pliancy of mind and body arises.
prerequisites: the six prerequisites (suitable place, few desires, contentment, few activities, pure ethics, abandoning desire-thoughts)
duration: months to years of continuous practice (the texts give no fixed measure)
signs_of_progress: the nine mental states in order
mental then physical pliancy with joy
the mind stays on its object at will

warnings.text: Subtle laxity is easily mistaken for faultless meditation; long meditation in it dulls the mind.
If the limbs of calm are lost, even thousands of years of effort will not produce concentration.

equivalents.note: same ninefold method from the Śrāvakabhūmi
Kamalaśīla's presentation, on which the lamrim draws

name: Inner heat (caṇḍālī)
method_summary: Summary only: meditation on the navel fire (caṇḍālī) in the central channel that melts the drop at the crown, giving rise to the four joys; taught in the Hevajra and first of Tilopa's six dharmas (from Caryāpa), with physical exercises. No method details are recorded here.
prerequisites: the higher consecrations
the generation stage
a qualified guru's oral instruction

warnings.text: To be received only from the guru after consecration; revealing it to the unripe is a root downfall.
Saraha mocks those who force the winds and 'call themselves yogins out of pride' (King Dohā v24) and those who take experiences for the ultimate (v25–26).
To be practised only after the common path, a complete empowerment and the generation stage, under a teacher; wind practices done wrongly cause wind disorders.

equivalents.note: A feminine inner power in the central channel in both; frames and goals differ.

alt_method_summary: Summary only: the completion-stage practice of kindling inner heat at the navel, which Tsongkhapa calls the foundation stone of the completion stage; taught in the Six Yogas and within the Lamdre's method continuum.

name: Recitation of the Devī Māhātmya (Caṇḍīpāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting the thirteen chapters of the Devī Māhātmya (with ancillary hymns in the recitation tradition), especially on the eighth, ninth and fourteenth lunar days and during the autumn Navarātra; the Goddess promises protection and prosperity to reciters and hearers (DM 12).

name: Cāndrāyaṇa (lunar penance)
method_summary: Summary only: an expiatory fast in which food follows the waning and waxing of the moon over a month (MDh 11.216).

warnings.text: To be performed only as prescribed expiation, with the observances and self-control the texts require.

notes: Restricted (prolonged fasting): no quantities recorded.

name: Walking meditation (caṅkama)
method_summary: Walking back and forth with the senses turned inward and the mind not going outward (AN 7.61); by day and night as part of wakefulness (MN 39).

name: Caraka's means to liberation
method_summary: Serving the good and avoiding the wicked; vows, fasts and restraints; study of the dharma treatises; delight in solitude and aversion to objects; approaching a teacher; renunciation of possessions (the renunciant's requisites); acting with mindfulness in all movements; bearing opposites; withdrawing the senses into the mind and the mind into the self; counting the body's parts by dhātus; contemplating all that is caused as suffering, not one's own and impermanent; all flowing from the recollection of truth (tattvasmṛti), culminating in the understanding 'this is not I, not mine' and final renunciation.
signs_of_progress: purified mind shining like a polished mirror or a lamp in a windless place (Śā 5.13-15)
the eight powers of yogins (Śā 1.140-141)

equivalents.note: mindfulness in all postures and activities and contemplation of the body's parts

name: Knowing the four moons (cāri candra bhed) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. A secret Bāul practice concerning four bodily substances ('moons'); recorded only by name, aim (reintegration of what the body emits) and the tradition's warnings — no method, substance handling or quantities.

warnings.text: Secret; never to be attempted without a guru; ruin follows otherwise.

name: Meditation objects that purify temperament
method_summary: The meditation object is prescribed by temperament: the unattractive for the lustful, loving-kindness for the hateful, dependent origination for the deluded, analysis of the elements for the proud, mindfulness of breathing for the discursive.
prerequisites: a teacher who can discern the practitioner's temperament

name: The non-dual caru rite
method_summary: Kaula consumption, in daily and occasional rites, of substances ordinarily held impure, as a discipline of non-duality; recorded only in summary.

warnings.text: No one may be made to take the caru by force, without their will.
One who, having taken up non-dual conduct, acts otherwise falls into terrible hells.
To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.

name: Defining the four elements (catudhātuvavatthāna)
method_summary: Discerning the body as earth, water, fire and air — briefly for the quick-witted, or by forty-two aspects; the perception of a being disappears; reaches access; in the Pa-Auk tradition by twelve characteristics, leading to the sight of material groups.

equivalents.note: the sutta contemplation of elements (MN 10) (U36)

name: The sixty-four services (catuḥṣaṣṭy-upacāra)
method_summary: The Goddess is served in imagination and act as a queen with sixty-four royal services — bath, anointing, garments, jewels, weapons, mounting the cakra, sitting on Kāmeśvara's lap, drink, betel, lights, parasol, fans, mirror and the rest (PKS 4.5; LSN 58); the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad interiorizes the services.

name: The fourfold purity of virtue (catupārisuddhi-sīla)
method_summary: Restraint by the Pātimokkha, restraint of the sense faculties, purification of livelihood, and use of the requisites with reflection.

name: The rainy-season retreat (cāturmāsa)
method_summary: Mendicants stop wandering for the four months of the rains and stay in one place chosen with the local community, to avoid harming the many beings that appear; it is a season of teaching, study and austerity.

equivalents.note: the Buddhist rains retreat

name: The seasonal rites (cāturmāsya)
method_summary: Offerings at the beginning of the three four-month seasons, including the Sākamedha with the Tryambaka offerings to Rudra.

name: The fourth prāṇāyāma (YS 2.51)
method_summary: Restricted-adjacent (breath retention): summary only. Vyāsa: the fourth goes beyond both the external and the internal; unlike the third, which is a single-effort stopping without attention to an object, it is a gradual stopping preceded by surpassing both, by mastery of the ground, after determining the object of inhalation and exhalation.

alt_method_summary: A breath-stilling that goes beyond the external and internal spheres, reached gradually after mastering the stages (2.51, YBh 2.51). Summary only.
prerequisites: mastery of the three kinds (2.50)
notes: Marked restricted as a form of breath suspension; no method given.

name: The caukā rite (Dharamdāsī Kabīr Panth)
method_summary: A ritual on a square ground with coconut, betel leaves and lamps, performed by the ācārya for initiation and for the dead, by which souls receive the Name and the 'passport' past Kāl.
notes: Details from secondary accounts; low confidence.

name: Long sitting without lying down (changzuo buwo / jangjwa bulwa)
method_summary: Sitting day and night without lying down for long periods; reported of Northern-school practice and kept by some Korean Seon practitioners.

warnings.text: 'Long sitting constrains the body — what benefit to the principle?' (Huineng); Jinul lists 'always sitting and never lying down' among austerities useless without knowing one's own mind.

name: Cheating death (mṛtyuvañcana)
method_summary: Summary only: reading omens of death and averting untimely death by Tārā practice (Vāgīśvarakīrti) or by drawing the life-wind into the central channel (Sekoddeśa). No technique recorded.

name: Rites to avert death ('chi bslu)
method_summary: When signs of untimely death appear, ransom rites, saving animals' lives, long-life practices and effigies are used to avert it.

name: Chöd: the visualized offering of the body (lus sbyin)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted). After refuge, bodhicitta and supplication to Machig and the lineage, the practitioner transfers consciousness into the sky as the wrathful ḍākinī, visualizes the body left behind as offered and transformed into nectar, and distributes it to the four guests, then rests in the view in which giver, gift and recipient are empty; sung liturgy with drum, bell and thighbone trumpet. Its purpose is to cut self-clinging, not to subdue spirits.
prerequisites: Chöd empowerment and reading transmission from a lineage holder
the common and uncommon preliminaries
some understanding of the view of emptiness
the teacher's permission before practice in frightening places
signs_of_progress: fear no longer arises in frightening places
clinging to the body diminishes
spirits are experienced as friendly
illness is pacified (tradition's account)

warnings.text: Practised without the view of emptiness and without compassion it becomes a mere rite that can provoke harm.
Do not go to frightening places before the teacher permits and before one has stability.
Pride at feeling powerful over spirits is itself the māra of conceit.
Spirits are guests to be fed with compassion, not enemies to be attacked or exorcised.

equivalents.note: the kusāli's accumulation of the Nyingma preliminaries is a short form of the same visualized body-offering
both practise in charnel grounds to overcome fear and clinging; their views, deities and aims differ

name: Chöd practice in charnel grounds and haunted places
method_summary: Summary only (restricted). Having trained in the liturgy, the practitioner goes to charnel grounds and places held to be haunted, practises Chöd there, especially at night, and meets the fear that arises by looking for the one who is afraid; wandering practitioners traditionally moved between many such places.
prerequisites: stable practice of the Chöd liturgy
the teacher's permission

warnings.text: Not to be undertaken before the teacher permits and before one has stability; practised with self-clinging it increases fear and harm.

name: Essence extraction (bcud len)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted where it restricts ordinary food). Rejuvenating regimens in which the practitioner, often in retreat, lives on or supplements food with prepared essences (of flowers, minerals and other substances) to restore vigour, prolong life and support meditation.

warnings.text: To be undertaken only with instruction from a qualified teacher and physician; unsuitable regimens harm health (tradition's general caution).

equivalents.note: rejuvenation therapy
rejuvenation in seclusion

name: Worship of Tārā in the Cīna mode
method_summary: The worship of Tārā/Nīlasarasvatī according to the Mahācīna mode taught to Vasiṣṭha by the Buddha (Rudrayāmala 17; Tārā Tantra; Bṛhannīla Tantra). Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: The Buddha's instruction begins with purity, the paśu disposition, solitude, restraint and breath-yoga.

name: Taming the mind (cittassa damatho)
method_summary: The verse states that taming the mind is good and that a tamed mind brings happiness (Dhp 35); the discerning one makes the quivering mind straight like a fletcher's arrow (33); the mind is restrained systematically (yoniso) as an elephant with the goad (326).

checks.note: Level not raised (entities are not promoted by the J check). By code: every rests_on teaching exists in final/ and links this id. J read the gloss against those verses and checked the id is not a homonym of an existing data/ entry with the Buddhist sense.

name: Guarding the mind (cittaṁ rakkhetha)
method_summary: The wise one should guard the very subtle mind that alights where it wishes; a guarded mind brings happiness (Dhp 36); guard one's own mind, lift oneself out of the mud (327).

checks.note: Level not raised (entities are not promoted by the J check). By code: every rests_on teaching exists in final/ and links this id. J read the gloss against those verses and checked the id is not a homonym of an existing data/ entry with the Buddhist sense.

name: Contemplation of mind (cittānupassanā)
method_summary: Knowing the mind in eight pairs: with/without lust, hatred, delusion; contracted/scattered; exalted/unexalted; surpassable/unsurpassable; concentrated/unconcentrated; liberated/unliberated (MN 10:34-35).

checks.note: Level not raised (entities are not promoted by the spot-check). By code: every linked id resolves in data/ or these shards; no restricted flag; no modern/psychological/health wording found. Content not read line by line by J.

alt_method_summary: Knowing the mind as with or without lust, hatred, delusion, contracted, scattered, exalted, concentrated, liberated (MN 10).

name: Clear-light yoga
method_summary: Summary: resting the mind in the central channel and steadying it in the drop at the heart, lights, rays, rainbows, dawn, sun and moon appear and fields become pure (Tilopa, from Nāgārjuna); in the Ārya scheme the fourth stage, full awakening in clear light.
signs_of_progress: the appearances listed by Tilopa (lights, rainbows, dawn, sun and moon, deities)
signs of lights, rainbows, dawn, sun and moon (Ṣaḍdharmopadeśa)
alt_method_summary: Recognizing the clear light in the gap between waking, sleep and dream and holding it through deep sleep ('awakening through deep sleep'), mixing day and night; its full form rests on restricted completion-stage wind practice.

name: Cultivating compassion (Kamalaśīla)
method_summary: Compassion is cultivated first, seeing all beings as tormented by the three kinds of suffering: first toward those dear, then toward the indifferent, then toward enemies, until it is equal toward all beings in the ten directions and arises spontaneously.
notes: Order (friends, neutral, enemies) from memory of Bhāvanākrama I.

name: Anuyoga completion stage (rdzogs rim)
method_summary: Work with the channels, winds and essences to bring the winds into the central channel and give rise to bliss-emptiness, emphasized in Anuyoga. Summary only.
prerequisites: empowerment
generation stage
a qualified teacher

warnings.text: Taught only after empowerment and under guidance; improper practice disturbs the winds.

name: Purification by the four opponent powers
method_summary: Confessing wrongdoing with regret, relying on refuge and bodhicitta, applying a remedy (recitation, prostration, meditation on emptiness) and resolving not to repeat it.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).
alt_method_summary: Recalling the evil done in beginningless saṃsāra and this life, natural and prescribed faults alike, one confesses them before the Buddhas with joined palms, in fear of their result, asks that they be accepted as faults, and resolves not to do them again.

name: Confession before the thirty-five buddhas
method_summary: Reciting the names of the thirty-five buddhas with prostrations, confessing wrongs, rejoicing and dedicating.

name: Slaying desire, the enemy
method_summary: First restrain the senses and slay desire, the destroyer of knowledge and discernment (3.41); knowing that which is beyond the understanding, steady the self by the self and slay the enemy in the form of desire (3.43). Desire's seat is the senses, mind and understanding (3.40).
prerequisites: restraint of the senses (3.41)
knowing what is beyond understanding (3.42–43)

warnings.text: Desire is an insatiable fire, the constant enemy of the knower, covering knowledge.
The enemy in the form of desire is hard to overcome (durāsada).

name: Seeing the conditioned as a dream (Diamond verse)
method_summary: Contemplating all conditioned dharmas as stars, a fault of vision, a lamp, an illusion, dew, a bubble, a dream, lightning, a cloud.

name: Contemplating death
method_summary: The lamrim's meditation on death by three roots, nine reasons and three decisions.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).
alt_method_summary: Recollecting that death may come soon, before one's evil is exhausted, that one will go alone leaving relatives and possessions, and that the lord of death rules all who are born, one turns from craving to refuge and the Dharma.

name: Courting dishonour (avamāna, paribhava)
method_summary: Hiding his sign and learning, the ascetic goes among people behaving so as to be despised and reviled; he regards censure as no censure. The text states that his demerit then passes to his revilers and their merit to him.
signs_of_progress: being thought mad or sinful by people (the intended result)

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Taking one's craft as the path (the siddhas' instruction)
method_summary: The guru turns the disciple's own trade or habit into the meditation: the weaver weaves phenomena into the dharmakāya, the cobbler tans the leather of concepts, the smith forges the three poisons in the fire of gnosis, the potter burns delusion in the kiln, the tailor stitches the three realms with compassion, the liar meditates all as a lie.

name: Cūḍākaraṇa (tonsure)
method_summary: Shaving the child's head, leaving the tuft, in the first or third year (MDh 2.35).

queries: local text at the cited refs

name: Cultivating patience
method_summary: Seeing that anger destroys the merit of aeons, one cultivates patience by reflection: if a thing can be remedied, why be unhappy, and if not, why be unhappy; suffering has virtues (humility, compassion, dread of evil); harm arises from causes and conditions, and the enemy is a helper in the practice of patience.

name: Cultivation of compassion over many lives
method_summary: Compassion, repeatedly cultivated, becomes the mind's nature and grows by its own momentum without limit, because mind continues across lives; perfected, it moves one to remove others' suffering and is the root of a buddha's authority.

name: Being still (cummā iruttal)
method_summary: The silent guru's instruction 'be still': resting without the mind's movement, which Tāyumāṉavar holds harder and higher than every power.

equivalents.note: inner stillness beyond outer silence

warnings.text: All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.

name: Cutting the root of mind (rtsad gcod)
method_summary: 'Cut the root of your own mind and leave awareness naked; let the muddy water of thought clear; neither stop nor create appearances, leave them in their own place' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā): decisive recognition that the thinking mind has no root, after which thoughts are no longer followed.
notes: Kagyu idiom; not to be confused with Dzogchen's trekchö (khregs chod, U45).

name: Meditation on the small space in the heart (dahara-vidyā)
method_summary: Seek and understand what is within the small space in the lotus of the heart, in this 'city of brahman': as large as outer space, containing heaven and earth; the self free from evil, old age, death, sorrow, hunger and thirst, whose desires and intentions are real.
signs_of_progress: freedom of movement in all worlds; whatever one desires arises by intention (ChU 8.1.6-8.2)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

queries: prepared segments: ChU 8.1.6-8.2, ChU 8.1.1-6

alt_method_summary: Meditation on Brahman within the small space of the heart-lotus (Chāndogya 8.1); for Śrīkaṇṭha, meditation on Śiva as the supreme ether, his cit-śakti.

name: Sacrifice to the gods (daiva yajña)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.25: some yogins attend to sacrifice to the gods alone; cf. 4.12, people desiring success of their actions sacrifice to the deities, and success born of action comes quickly in the human world.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

name: Therapy resting on the divine (daivavyapāśraya)
method_summary: Mantra, wearing of herbs and gems, auspicious rites, offerings, gifts, oblations, observances, expiation, fasting, benedictions, prostration and pilgrimage, used especially for karma-born and exogenous disorders. No mantras or rites recorded.

name: Breath practice (dam) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. Coded Bāul teaching on the breath as the vehicle of the Man ('catch the thief in the house of air'); summary and warnings only, no retentions or counts.

warnings.text: Without the guru the seeker catches only wind.

name: The three 'da': self-restraint, giving, compassion
method_summary: Practise the three that the thunder repeats — da, da, da: be restrained (dāmyata), give (datta), be compassionate (dayadhvam) (BAU 5.2).

queries: prepared segments: BĀU 5.2, BĀU 5.2.1-3

name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Give because it ought to be given, to one who makes no return, at the right place and time to a worthy person (17.20); the gleaner's gift of his last food to a guest (MBh 14.92–93).

queries: prepared segments: BĀU 5.2, TU 1.11.3, ChU 3.17.4, BĀU 5.2.1-3
checks.note: All 4 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (BĀU 5.2; TU 1.11.3; ChU 3.17.4; BĀU 5.2.1-3). It rests on 3 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.
