checks.note: Matsya 274-289 (local peterFreund colophons), GP 2.5.123-126 and MkP 10.68 located. All teachings it rests on were located in the local e-texts (see their checks).

notes: U05's contribution to a shared practice.
alt_method_summary: Giving food and wealth to the needy, the friend and the priest; the gift at the sacrifice (dakṣiṇā).
Giving to the virtuous, a dwelling for the Saṅgha of the four quarters, and regular gifts as sacrifices of great fruit (DN 5); the first perfection (Bv 2).
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'give' (datta, BAU 5.2); give with faith, grace, modesty, awe and understanding (TU 1.11.3); giving among the priestly gifts of the life-sacrifice (ChU 3.17.4).
Religious gifts - food, water, land, cows, gold, sesame and the sixteen great gifts - to worthy recipients at due times and places; gifts in life ease the road after death.

warnings.text: Who eats alone has only sin; the wealth of the non-giver finds no one to pity him.

name: Giving and the field of merit
method_summary: Giving whose merit depends on the giver (faith etc.), the thing and the field (destiny, suffering, benefit, qualities); the highest gift is from one liberated to one liberated, or the bodhisattva's gift. The schools differ on whether gifts to the Buddha or to the Saṅgha yield more fruit.

name: Giving (dāna) and sharing with ascetics
method_summary: Giving food, medicine, knowledge and fearlessness; above all offering pure food to wandering ascetics who arrive unannounced, with the proper manner, thing, giver and recipient.

name: Giving (dāna) in Vaiśeṣika ethics
method_summary: Giving and receiving as deliberate acts yielding merit, with rules regarding recipients who are superior, equal or inferior in merit.

name: Daṇḍa-dhauti (washing with a stick)
method_summary: A stalk of plantain, turmeric or cane is moved within the chest (gullet) and slowly withdrawn, expelling phlegm, bile and mucus upward (GS 1.37-38).
signs_of_progress: destroys heart disease (GS 1.38)

name: Daṇḍāsana (the staff seat)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Dantamūla-dhauti (cleansing the roots of the teeth)
method_summary: The roots of the teeth are rubbed with catechu juice or pure earth until the impurity is removed, daily at dawn (GS 1.27-28).
signs_of_progress: protects the teeth (GS 1.28)

name: Dark retreat (mun mtshams)
method_summary: Retreat in complete darkness for a prescribed period, in Nyingma Heart-essence (Yangti) and in the Bön Zhang Zhung Nyengyü, to bring forth the visions of spontaneous presence. Summary only.
prerequisites: preliminaries
stability in cutting through
a qualified master's guidance

warnings.text: Undertaken only with a master's instruction and supervision, after the foundations are complete; the traditions warn of disturbances of wind and mind when it is attempted without them.

notes: RESTRICTED: durations and methods not recorded.

name: New- and full-moon offerings (darśapūrṇamāsa)
method_summary: The fortnightly offerings of cakes and other substances at new and full moon, the model (prakṛti) of all iṣṭi rites; the White Yajurveda begins with its formulas.

queries: local text at the cited refs
checks.note: ŚB 1.1.1 (the vow of truth on entering the rite) and 1.6.3.35–36 were found. This rests on confirmed teaching checks: tea:satapatha-brahmana:1.1.1.4-5, tea:satapatha-brahmana:1.6.3.35-36.

alt_method_summary: The fortnightly Śrauta offerings of cakes and other oblations, entered with a vow of truth (ŚB 1.1.1.4–5), which heal the joints of the year-Prajāpati at the moon's phases (ŚB 1.6.3.36).
The archetypal iṣṭi (prakṛti), all of whose subsidiaries (e.g. the prayājas) are taught in its own context, from which ectypal offerings take their procedure; enjoined for one desiring heaven.
duration: each new and full moon

name: Das Lakṣaṇa Parva
method_summary: Ten days of the Digambara rains festival, each devoted to one of the ten dharmas (supreme forbearance, humility, straightforwardness, purity, truth, restraint, austerity, renunciation, non-possession, chastity), with readings of the Tattvārthasūtra, worship and fasting according to capacity, ending with forgiveness.
duration: ten days

name: The ten perceptions (Girimānanda)
method_summary: Impermanence, not-self, unattractiveness, danger, abandoning, dispassion, cessation, non-delight in the whole world, impermanence in all formations, mindfulness of breathing — recited to the sick (AN 10.60).

name: The ten precepts
method_summary: The novice's ten training rules, adding the refusal of gold and silver (Khp 2).

name: Dāsōha — sharing the fruit of work
method_summary: Giving what one earns by kāyaka to the jaṅgamas and the community in the spirit 'I am your servant'; in the modern maṭhas, free feeding and schooling.

name: Servitude to the Lord (dāsya)
method_summary: Relating to the Lord as his servant and serving him. Seventh of the Bhāgavata's nine forms. For the Āḻvārs servitude (aṭimai) is the soul's nature: 'at all times without break we must do faultless service' (TVM 3.3.1); the drum the girls ask is service for seven times seven births (TP 29); the Āḻvārs ask to serve the Lord's servants. The Nārada Sūtra: love as an eternal servant (NBS 66).

equivalents.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava kaiṅkarya is service as the soul's goal, grounded in the Āḻvārs' aṭimai
service to the Lord's devotees

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Hanumān.

name: Supporting the dying with wholesome objects
method_summary: Relatives and monks help the dying recollect their good deeds, chant, and bring offerings or Buddha-images into view, so that a wholesome kamma or sign becomes the object of the last cognitive process, which conditions rebirth.
notes: Popular practice resting on the Abhidhamma account of death; text support is the doctrine, not an injunction.

name: Deathbed rites for birth (linzhong xingyi / rinjū gyōgi)
method_summary: The dying person faces west (or is moved to a separate hall) before an image of Amitābha, holding a five-coloured cord tied to its hand; attendants burn incense, recite with him, ask what he sees and help him repent evil signs, so that he completes the ten recitations in right mindfulness; those who have taken wine, meat or pungent roots stay away.
signs_of_progress: visions of the lotus-dais and holy assembly (to be recorded)

warnings.text: If relatives who have eaten meat or drunk wine approach, the sick one loses right mindfulness and may die deranged and fall into the evil paths.
Do not wait for the deathbed to begin practising; build the habit now.

notes: Shinshū does not rely on deathbed rites (Mattōshō 1).

name: Deathless body and mind (Shangpa)
method_summary: The 'fruit' practices of the Shangpa, joining deity and wind yogas for the undying mind; summary only.

name: Dedicating merit (pariṇāmanā)
method_summary: Turning all merit toward awakening for all beings, ideally without apprehending merit, dedicator or goal.

warnings.text: For Shinshū the practitioner has no merit of his own to transfer; the nenbutsu is not said as a memorial for one's parents.
Dedication made with apprehension of signs is 'poisoned, with a thorn'.

alt_method_summary: The merit of practice is dedicated to the relief of all beings' sufferings and their awakening, with the aspiration to remain as long as space and the world remain and to take the world's suffering on oneself.

name: Mental worship of the body-liṅga with eight flowers
method_summary: Instead of an external liṅga, the practitioner worships the liṅga within the body mentally, offering the eight inner flowers — non-harming, sense-restraint, compassion, feeling, patience, conquest of anger, meditation and knowledge — and, in the Yogaviṣaya, bathing the inner Lord with the moon's nectar and offering the flower of the mind.
signs_of_progress: enjoyment and liberation (KJN 3.27)

name: Transformation of the body (dehavedha)
method_summary: The application of perfected mercury to the body to make it stable, ageless and 'divine' as the basis for yoga and liberation in life — first tested on metal. RESTRICTED: summary and warnings only.

warnings.text: As in metal, so in the body: first test on metal, afterward apply to the body.
Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.
Impure minerals and metals destroy life (impure pyrite causes death without doubt; impure copper and iron destroy life, strength and lustre).
Mercury is not to be used where a vital point is injured or in burns from caustic or fire.
Without the guru's grace and permission the work is fruitless; the unfit gain nothing and lose their wealth.

signs_of_progress: in the texts' claims: freedom from disease, agelessness, sky-going, the powers (Rasahṛdaya 1.3, 1.26) — claims, not endorsements

name: Deity yoga (generation-stage sādhana)
method_summary: After refuge, bodhicitta and the protection circle, the practitioner dissolves ordinary appearance into emptiness, generates the maṇḍala and himself as the deity from seed syllables on sun and moon discs, invites the gnosis beings to merge with the visualized pledge beings, receives consecration and the seal of the family lord, maintains the deity's clarity and pride while reciting mantra, and finally dissolves and re-arises for activity.
prerequisites: vase consecration (trm:kalasabhiseka)
the pledges (samaya)
signs_of_progress: stable clarity of the deity and the maṇḍala
pride of the deity
readiness for the completion stage ('the staircase', Pañcakrama 1.2)

warnings.text: There is no meditator and nothing meditated, no mantra and no deity: they abide in the nature free of elaboration — the deity is not to be reified.
Saraha criticizes those who meditate on maṇḍala circles without the innate (People Dohā v10–13).

alt_method_summary: Generating oneself as the deity from emptiness, maintaining divine pride and clear appearance; for the Gelug, the wisdom realising emptiness itself appears as the deity.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).

name: The reasoning of dependent origination
method_summary: Because a thing arises in dependence it is empty of own-nature, and because it is empty it can arise: reflecting that nothing is not dependently arisen and so nothing is non-empty, one avoids both eternalism and annihilationism.

name: Recollection of the deities
method_summary: Recollecting that the faith, virtue, learning, generosity and wisdom by which deities were reborn are present in oneself (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)
faith and gladness
access concentration
alt_method_summary: Recollecting one's own faith, virtue, learning, generosity and understanding with the deities as witnesses; reaches access.

name: Kuṇḍalinī yoga of the Devī Gītā
method_summary: Summary only: after the eight limbs, the Goddess describes breath control, the channels and six centres, and the rousing of kuṇḍalinī from the root centre to union with the supreme at the crown; procedures, counts and retentions are not recorded here.

warnings.text: The Devī Gītā places this yoga after the yamas and niyamas and within devotion to the Goddess; the text is to be taught only to the qualified.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:devi-gita-kundalini-dhyana
checks.note: Restricted practice: the entry stays summary-only, with no procedures, counts or retentions, and the warnings are the text's own (7.40.34 restricts the teaching). Location DBhP 7.35 verified (Gītāsaṅgraha ch. 4, closing 'iti yogavidhiḥ kṛtsnaḥ').

prerequisites: the ten yamas and ten niyamas
a qualified teacher

name: The ten yamas and ten niyamas (Devī Gītā)
method_summary: Practising the ten restraints and ten observances listed by the Goddess as the first limbs of yoga.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:devi-gita-yamas-niyamas

name: Dhammakāya meditation (Wat Paknam method)
method_summary: The mind is brought down through a series of bases (nostril, eye-corner, centre of the head, palate, throat, navel level) to the seventh base at the centre of the body, while visualizing a clear crystal sphere and repeating 'sammā arahaṃ', until a bright sphere and then successive inner bodies appear.
notes: From secondary knowledge; exact list of bases not verified.

name: Contemplation of dhammas (dhammānupassanā)
method_summary: Five sections: the five hindrances, five aggregates of clinging, six sense bases, seven awakening factors, four noble truths (MN 10:36-45). For hindrances, fetters and awakening factors the monk knows each as present or absent and how the unarisen arises, the arisen is abandoned (or fulfilled, for the factors) and the abandoned does not arise again.

alt_method_summary: Contemplating the hindrances, the aggregates, the sense bases and their fetters, the factors of awakening and the four truths (MN 10; DN 22).

name: Recollection of the Dhamma
method_summary: Recollecting 'the Dhamma is well proclaimed, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise' (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)
faith and gladness
access concentration
alt_method_summary: Recollecting the qualities of the Dhamma ('well proclaimed, visible here and now, timeless …'); reaches access.

name: Dhanurāsana (the bow)
method_summary: In the Haṭhapradīpikā the big toes are held with the hands and drawn up to the ear like a drawn bow (HYP 1.25); in the Gheraṇḍa the legs are stretched on the ground, the feet held from behind and the body curved like a bow (GS 2.18).
notes: The two texts describe different forms under one name.

name: Dhāraṇā (concentration)
method_summary: The binding of the mind to a place (3.1); the bhāṣya names as places the navel wheel, the lotus of the heart, the light in the head, the tip of the nose, the tip of the tongue, or an external object, the mind being bound by its activity alone.

alt_method_summary: Binding the mind to one place — navel wheel, heart-lotus, light in the head, tip of the nose or tongue, or an external object (3.1, YBh 3.1).
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): yoga as 'the firm holding (dhāraṇā) of the senses' (KU 2.3.11); fourth limb in MaiU 6.18; 'its further concentration' at the palate (MaiU 6.20).
Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: 'Established in yoga-dhāraṇā': restraining all the gates, confining the mind in the heart and placing the breath in the head at departure (8.12).
Sāṃkhya contribution: concentration, with posture and one's own duty, accomplishes meditation (SS 3.32); with meditation, practice and dispassion it stops the coloring of puruṣa (SS 6.29).
prerequisites: fitness from prāṇāyāma (2.53)

name: Dhāraṇī recitation
method_summary: Reciting protective dhāraṇīs given in the sūtras (Lotus 26; the Great Compassion and Uṣṇīṣavijayā dhāraṇīs).

name: Dharma-dhyāna (virtuous meditation)
method_summary: Fixing the mind on one of four objects: the Jina's command (the realities as taught), the harm and misery of wrong ways, the fruition of karma, and the structure of the universe; supported by the reflections, the four attitudes and equanimity; also practised through the four objects (piṇḍastha …).
stage: guṇasthānas 4–7 (Digambara); up to 12 in some Śvetāmbara accounts
prerequisites: right view
equanimity
a qualified meditator and suitable place (Jñānārṇava)
duration: up to one muhūrta at a time

name: Inquiry into dharma (dharma-jijñāsā, vedārtha-vicāra)
method_summary: Systematic investigation of the Vedic sentences by the adhikaraṇa method — subject, doubt, connection, prima facie view, conclusion — undertaken after Vedic study, before the student returns home, to know dharma for performance.
prerequisites: completed study of one's Vedic recension

name: Preaching the dharma (dharmabhāṇaka practice)
method_summary: Teaching the sūtra seated on the Tathāgata's seat (emptiness), wearing his robe (patience), in his room (compassion); the four peaceful practices for the latter age.

name: Attention to the elements (dhātumanasikāra)
method_summary: Reviewing the body, however placed, as earth, water, fire and air, like a butcher at a crossroads with the divided carcass (MN 10:12-13).

alt_method_summary: Reviewing the body as earth, water, fire and air (and space), internal and external, like a butcher's carcass cut into pieces, seen as 'not mine, not I, not my self'; meditating like the earth that is unaffected by what is thrown on it (MN 10; MN 28; MN 62; MN 140).

name: Analysis of the elements (dhātuprabheda)
method_summary: For the proud: analysing the body into the six elements (earth, water, fire, air, space, consciousness), which dissolves the perception of the body as a solid lump.

name: Dhauti (washing) — the class of cleansing acts
method_summary: The first of the six acts. In the Haṭhapradīpikā dhauti is the swallowing and withdrawing of a moistened cloth (HYP 2.24-25). In the Gheraṇḍa dhauti is fourfold — inner (antar-dhauti: vātasāra, vārisāra, vahnisāra, bahiṣkṛta), of the teeth (danta-dhauti: tooth-roots, tongue, ears, the forehead hollow), of the heart/chest (hṛd-dhauti: with a stick, by vomiting, with a cloth) and of the root (mūlaśodhana) — and it cleans the body (GS 1.13-44). The Gheraṇḍa also counts dhauti as the nirmanu way of purifying the channels (GS 5.36).

warnings.text: One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.
Some teachers hold that all impurities are dried up by breath-control alone and do not approve of the other acts.
The six acts, which purify the body, are to be kept secret.
The Śivasaṃhitā counts washing by dhauti (with sitting in gomukha, stirring the belly and the like) among the obstacles that take the form of knowledge.

name: Dhenu mudrā (the cow gesture)
method_summary: The little and ring fingers, and the index and middle fingers, of the two hands interlaced and joined facing each other; with it the officiant turns the offering-water into nectar (amṛtīkaraṇa) (ŚT 23.112-113, with the commentary's fuller description).

name: Tending the sacred fire (dhūnī)
method_summary: Keeping the yogī's fire burning at the seat or camp, offering to it and distributing its ash (vibhūti) as blessing.

name: The ascetic practices (dhutaguṇa)
method_summary: Optional austerities: rag-robes, only three robes, alms-round without skipping houses, one meal, living in the forest, at a tree's root, in the open, in a charnel ground, the sitter's practice (not lying down), and others; twelve in the Sanskrit lists, thirteen in the Pali.
notes: Common to all the Vinayas; details and counts differ by school.

warnings.text: They are optional; the Vinaya accounts show the Buddha refusing to make forest-dwelling and similar austerities compulsory (Devadatta's demands).

equivalents.note: Twelve in the Sanskrit lists, thirteen in the Pali.

name: The thirteen ascetic practices (dhutaṅga)
method_summary: Voluntary austerities undertaken for effacement: refuse-rag robes, three robes only, alms-food, house-to-house alms, one session, bowl-food, refusing later food, forest dwelling, tree-root, open air, charnel ground, any bed, the sitter's practice; each has strict, medium and mild grades.

warnings.text: They suit the greedy and deluded temperaments; undertaken with the wish to be admired they become a basis of evil desire.
The Buddha refused Devadatta's demand to make forest dwelling, alms-food, rag robes, tree-root dwelling and abstaining from fish and meat compulsory for life; each is allowed only for those who wish.

notes: Second warning from memory.
alt_method_summary: Voluntary austerities such as forest dwelling, living on alms-food only, wearing rag robes, living at the root of a tree — praised in Mahākassapa (Thag 18.1) and allowed as optional; the thirteen dhutaṅgas are listed in the commentaries (U37).

name: Dhyān (contemplation of the master's form)
method_summary: Holding the attention at the eye centre by contemplating the living master's form, which later appears within as the radiant form.

name: Meditation (dhyāna) as the means of abandoning the afflictions' activities
method_summary: The gross activities of the afflictions, thinned by kriyā-yoga, are abandoned by meditation as discerning insight (prasaṃkhyāna), until they are subtle, like burnt seeds (YS 2.11, YBh 2.11).

alt_method_summary: One-pointedness of cognition in that place (3.2); the bhāṣya adds: a like flow, untouched by any other cognition.
The continuous flow of a single cognition on the place of concentration (3.2); it removes the gross activities of the afflictions (2.11).

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): venerate meditation as brahman (ChU 7.6); by the yoga of meditation the sages saw God's power (ŚU 1.3); the friction of meditation with Om (ŚU 1.14); 'meditating, one sees him' (MuU 3.1.8); a limb in MaiU 6.18.

name: Dhyāna: visualization in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through meditative visualization, e.g. of the circle of the powers of consciousness in the heart (TĀ 5).

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: In solitude, alone, with mind and body controlled and without possessions, sit on a firm seat in a clean place; with body, head and neck erect and still and the gaze as if at the tip of the nose, serene and fearless, keeping the vow of celibacy, make the mind one-pointed, fixed on the self or on the Lord; gradually still the mind by a steady intellect and think of nothing else; whenever the restless mind wanders, bring it back; be moderate in food, sleep and effort.
stage: the one who has ascended (6.3–4); practised with determination and without despair (6.23)
prerequisites: renunciation of intention (6.2); self-control; moderation (6.16–17)
signs_of_progress: the mind steady like a lamp in a windless place (6.19); contentment in the self and happiness beyond the senses (6.20–21); the happiness of contact with Brahman (6.28); seeing the self in all and all in the self (6.29)

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or not at all, sleeps too much or too little.
The mind is restless; it is restrained by practice and dispassion.
Yoga is not for one who eats too much or nothing at all, nor for one who sleeps too much or keeps awake (6.16).
The mind is restless, turbulent and as hard to restrain as the wind (6.34); it is held only by practice and dispassion (6.35).
Yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is unrestrained (6.36).

Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

alt_method_summary: The yogin constantly yokes himself in a secluded place, alone, restrained in thought (citta) and in himself, without expectation or possessions (6.10); on a firm seat in a clean place (6.11), he makes the mind one-pointed, restrains the activity of thought and senses and practises for self-purification (6.12); holding body, head and neck in line and motionless, gazing toward the tip of his nose, not looking about (6.13), tranquil, fearless, in the vow of the brahmacārin, with the mind (manas) restrained, thought (citta) on the Lord and intent on him (6.14). Abandoning all desires born of intention and restraining the senses with the mind (6.24), he comes to rest little by little by an intellect held firm, makes the mind abide in the self and thinks of nothing (6.25); wherever the restless mind wanders he brings it back into the self (6.26).
Bhagavad Gītā 13.25: some see the self in themselves by themselves through meditation (dhyāna); no technique is given here.
duration: constantly (satatam 6.10; sadā 6.15, 6.28); perfection may take many births (6.45)
notes: Yoga is defined here as 'the unyoking from union with sorrow', to be practised with resolve and an undejected mind (6.23). One who falls away is not lost: he is reborn and resumes (6.40–45).

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) in the Kaula way
method_summary: After mutual testing, the guru initiates by touch, sight or piercing; Śākta initiation is held the highest (Kulārṇava 12.12; 14.53-66).
prerequisites: testing of the disciple for a year, six months or three

warnings.text: Guru and disciple who give and receive without mutual testing both become piśācas.
For the capable the observances remain binding; knowingly breaking them is a great fault.

queries: local text at the cited refs
checks.note: AB 1.3 (the consecrated sacrificer made an embryo) was found. This rests on confirmed teaching checks: tea:aitareya-brahmana:1.3.

alt_method_summary: Before a Soma sacrifice the sacrificer is consecrated in a hut with vows of fasting and restraint; the priests make him an embryo again (AB 1.3); he is born anew at the final bath.

The guru, after preliminary purifications and worship of the deity on a maṇḍala and in the fire, performs on the disciple a rite that acts on the soul (not caste or body): in the Śaiva form it binds the disciple to the observances (samaya-dīkṣā) and, in the liberating initiation (nirvāṇa-dīkṣā), purifies the six paths and destroys the bonds through mantra-power; consecrations of sādhaka and ācārya may follow. Pāñcarātra initiation admits to Bhagavān's mantras and worship.

The guru, having become Śiva by ritual identification, removes or burns the disciple's bonds by mantra-power (Sanskrit manuals), or initiates by look, touch, word, thought, scripture, yoga or fire (Tamil).

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) into Hari's worship
method_summary: The ācārya initiates a qualified devotee who has undergone the saṃskāras: the disciple sips the Lord's foot-water, receives mantra and vows, and thereafter worships; the Kṛṣṇāmṛtamahārṇava calls those without Hari's initiation 'beasts among men'.
prerequisites: devotion
saṃskāras
a qualified ācārya
notes: Ritual particulars (maṇḍala, fasting days) deliberately summarized, not listed.

name: Jain initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The candidate, having received the teacher's permission (and, for Śvetāmbaras, the family's), renounces household life, plucks out the hair, receives the great vows and the ascetic's requisites (Śvetāmbara: white robes, broom, bowls, mouth-cloth; Digambara monks: nudity, peacock-feather whisk, water-gourd) and a new name.

name: Consecration of the sacrificer (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The consecration before the soma rite: the sacrificer is shaved, bathed, clothed anew, restricted in food and speech and kept apart, and so 'reborn' fit for the gods; 'here I go from untruth to truth' (VS 1.5) is the vow-taker's formula.

warnings.text: The dietary restrictions of the consecration are ritual observances within the rite; they are not recorded here in detail.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) in the Trika
method_summary: Initiation in its many forms - samaya, putraka, abbreviated, by the balance, of the absent and the dead - purifying the paths (adhvan) and removing the bonds; the teacher observes signs of immersion in the disciple (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇi; MVT 11.35). For one who knows the Heart, initiation needs no oblation (Parātrīśikā 25).

name: Daily routine (dinacaryā)
method_summary: Rise at the brāhma muhūrta (before dawn) to protect life; attend to the body and cleanliness; clean the teeth with a twig suited to season and doṣa; apply collyrium to the eyes; nasal oil, gargling and (for some) medicated smoke; daily oil-massage, especially of head, ears and feet; exercise to half one's strength; bathing; clean clothes, fragrance; eat in measure when the previous meal is digested; follow good conduct through the day; at night, after a watch has passed, sleep remembering the gods, sages and teachers.

warnings.text: Tooth-twig, massage and bathing each have conditions in which they are to be avoided (indigestion, fever, eye and ear disease, kapha affliction, just after purification).

signs_of_progress: life, health, power and fame (AHS Sū 2.49)

name: Direct introduction to awareness (ngo sprod)
method_summary: The master points out awareness directly — by word, gesture, symbol or a sudden 'phaṭ' — and the disciple recognizes the nature of mind; the first of Garab Dorje's three statements.
prerequisites: preliminaries
devotion to the teacher

name: Discerning the field and its knower (kṣetra-kṣetrajña)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Knowing the field (the body and its constituents, 13.2, 13.6-13.7) and its knower is called knowledge (13.3). Whoever knows puruṣa and prakṛti with the guṇas thus is not born again (13.24). The one who truly sees sees the supreme lord abiding equally in all beings (13.28), actions as done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer (13.30), and the separate existence of beings as resting in the one (13.31). Those who know the difference between field and knower with the eye of knowledge go to the highest (13.35).
prerequisites: The dispositions called knowledge (13.8-13.12).
signs_of_progress: Not born again (13.24); reaching brahman (13.31); going to the highest (13.35).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

equivalents.note: The Mokṣadharma's practice of enumerating the twenty-four principles and knowing the twenty-fifth as other than them corresponds to knowing the difference between the field (13.6–7, whose items can be counted as twenty-four) and its knower (13.35); the Gītā gives no number and speaks of field and knower, not of principles.

notes: New practice (extractor B) in the Gītā's own terms.

name: Dīvālī as Mahāvīra's nirvāṇa
method_summary: Jains keep Dīvālī as the night of Mahāvīra's nirvāṇa at Pāvā, when the eighteen kings lit lamps 'since the light of knowledge is gone'; the next morning Gautama's omniscience is celebrated and the Jain new year (Vīra era) begins.

name: Pilgrimage to the divine sites and maṅgaḷāśāsana
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): the Āḻvārs travelled to the Lord's temples and sang each one — Tirumaṅkai some eighty — longing to be born even as a fish or a step at Tiruvēṅkaṭam, seeing the Lord at Śrīraṅgam from feet to face, calling the reclining Lord at Kuṭantai to rise and speak; the sites they sang became the 108 divya-deśas.
alt_method_summary: Visiting the temples sung by the Āḻvārs and praying for the Lord's welfare there, as the Āḻvārs and teachers did.

name: Recitation of the Divya Prabandham
method_summary: Recitation of the Āḻvārs' hymns in temples and homes — daily selections (nityānusandhānam), the annual festival of recitation (adhyayana-utsava) and the sung and enacted araiyar service — as the Tamil Veda.

name: Dokusan / sanzen (private interview)
method_summary: Private meeting with the teacher to present one's understanding of the kōan or to receive guidance.

name: Seeing the faults (doṣa-darśana)
method_summary: Reflecting on the faults in acquiring, guarding and losing objects, in attachment, and in the harm enjoyment does to beings, so that passion subsides; passion is not quieted by enjoyment but by seeing the faults of both.

warnings.text: Abstaining from objects for these faults is only a contentment, not liberation, without knowledge of the principles.

name: Sacrifice with material things (dravya-yajña)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.28: sacrifice with material things, one of the forms of sacrifice; 4.33: the sacrifice of knowledge is better than sacrifice made of material things.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

name: Dream yoga (rmi lam)
method_summary: Setting the intention before sleep and watching with mindfulness, the practitioner recognizes dreams as dreams, then trains in them — increasing, transforming, emanating, travelling to pure lands — knows them as illusion, abandons fear, and meditates on suchness; recognition in dream prepares recognition in the bardo.

equivalents.note: the sūtra contemplation of phenomena as dreamlike is the waking basis of dream yoga

prerequisites: stable mindfulness
illusory-body contemplation
signs_of_progress: recognizing dreams while dreaming
fearlessness and lightness in dreams (Ājñāsamyakpramāṇa)
travelling to pure lands; riding sun and moon (Karṇatantravajrapada)

warnings.text: Miracles in dreams, if taken as real, become obstacles; known as illusion, they become path.

notes: U46 owns this id; U45 contributes the Nyingma/Bön forms.
alt_method_summary: Recognizing the dream as dream and meditating on the profound meaning; focusing on nāda, bindu and the seed syllables of the five families, one sees buddha-fields and buddhas — 'the means of great bliss in sleep' (Tilopa, from Lavapa).

Recognizing dreams as dreams, transforming and mastering them, and training in the bardo of dream as preparation for the bardos after death; with the yoga of luminous sleep. In Bön from the Mother Tantra.
alt_notes: Also one of the Six Yogas of Nāropa (other units).

name: Discrimination of seer and seen (dṛg-dṛśya-viveka)
method_summary: Tracing the chain of seer and seen — object seen by eye, eye by mind, mind by witness — to the seer that is never seen.

name: Thangtong Gyalpo's Avalokiteśvara practice
method_summary: Refuge and bodhicitta; Avalokiteśvara visualized above oneself and all beings; light purifies; the six-syllable mantra; dissolution and resting with body, speech and mind as the deity's.

name: Meditation on the drop at the nose tip
method_summary: Visualizing a tiny drop or mustard seed (a five-coloured jewel) at the tip of the nose and resting the mind on it until the object dissolves into emptiness (Ajogi; Pañcakrama 1.10–11).
signs_of_progress: the mustard-seed object is lost in emptiness (Ajogi's song)

name: Great accomplishment and sacred-medicine accomplishment
method_summary: Collective, uninterrupted sādhana over several days, often producing consecrated medicine pills.

name: Shunning bad company (duḥsaṅga-tyāga)
method_summary: Avoiding in every way the company that breeds desire, anger, delusion, loss of memory and of understanding and utter ruin — small ripples that become an ocean through association (NBS 43–45); likewise not listening to talk of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies (NBS 63).

name: The bull-sound (ḍuṇḍuṅkāra / huḍukkāra)
method_summary: A holy sound like a bull's bellow produced by touching the tongue-tip to the palate, made as part of the offering.

name: The autumn worship of Durgā (Bengal)
method_summary: The great autumn worship of Durgā with her children, including the worship of a kumārī and the 'junction' worship (sandhi-pūjā), framed by the āgamanī and vijayā songs of Umā's homecoming and departure.
notes: Detailed rites (and offerings in some households) not recorded; the Kālikā Purāṇa's autumn-worship chapters not checked in Phase B.

name: Constant recollection of the dvaya
method_summary: Reciting the dvaya with its meaning — refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī, and prayer for service — throughout life, as the Lord bade Rāmānuja in the Śaraṇāgati Gadya.

name: Dividing thoughts into two classes
method_summary: Noting whether a thought is of sensuality, ill will or cruelty (to be abandoned) or of renunciation, good will or harmlessness (to be developed), since what one frequently thinks becomes the mind's inclination (MN 19).

name: The eight spheres of mastery (abhibhvāyatana)
method_summary: Mastering visual objects, small and great, beautiful and ugly, and the four colours, as extensions of the first, second and third deliverances.

name: The eight antidotal formations
method_summary: Against laziness: desire-to-act, effort, faith and pliancy; against forgetting the instruction: mindfulness; against sinking and agitation: awareness that notices them; against non-application: the intention that applies the remedy; against over-application: equanimity that lets the mind flow when they have ceased.
alt_method_summary: Faith, aspiration, effort and pliancy against laziness; mindfulness against forgetting the instruction; alertness to notice laxity and excitement; application of the remedy against non-application; equanimity against over-application.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).

name: The eight deliverances (vimokṣa)
method_summary: Two deliverances with the unlovely as object (in the first two dhyānas), the deliverance of the beautiful (fourth dhyāna), the four formless, and cessation.

name: Solitary living (ekacariya)

name: Concentrations (dhāraṇā) in the Mokṣadharma's yoga
method_summary: The Mokṣadharma's yoga teaches fixing the mind in concentrations (dhāraṇā) — on the elements and within the body — with the steadiness of an arrow-maker intent on his arrow, by which the yogin gains yoga-power (MBh 12.289; 12.298–306).

name: The five element-concentrations (pañca-dhāraṇā) in the haṭha texts
method_summary: The breath is held with the mind for a set period (not reproduced) in the place of each element, contemplated with its colour, shape, seed-syllable and deity: earth (yellow, square, la, Brahmā), water (white, crescent, va, Viṣṇu), fire (red, triangle, ra, Rudra), air (smoky/black, ya, Īśvara) and space (clear, ha, Sadāśiva) (GS 3.68-81; GŚ 68-75). The texts place them differently: in the heart, throat, palate, between the brows and in the brahmarandhra (GŚ 69-73); at the anus-region, navel, above the navel, between navel and brows and above the brows (DYŚ 100-110; ŚS 3.63-65); from feet to knees, knees to anus, anus to heart, heart to brows and brows to crown (Yogatattva). The Gorakṣaśataka names them the stabilising, liquefying, burning, whirling and drying concentrations (GŚ 74). The Gheraṇḍa counts them as five of its twenty-five mudrās.

name: Entry into cognition-only (vijñaptimātratā-praveśa)
method_summary: Having gathered merit and knowledge and reflected on the teachings, the bodhisattva in concentration sees objects as nothing but mental speech, rests in mind-only that appears as them, then no longer apprehends the object (the grasped is abandoned), then abandons the apprehension of mind-only itself (the grasper), and non-conceptual wisdom free of duality arises: 'where there is nothing grasped there is no grasping'.

name: Making prāṇa and apāna even (prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā)
method_summary: Having made even (sama) the prāṇa and apāna that move within the nostrils — together with putting external contacts outside and placing the gaze between the brows (5.27) — the sage with senses, mind and intellect restrained, intent on liberation, is forever free (5.28). name: Equalizing self and other
method_summary: Reflecting that oneself and all others equally want happiness and do not want suffering, so there is no ground for cherishing oneself above them; the first step of Śāntideva's method as taught in the lamrim.

alt_method_summary: One first reflects that others want happiness and fear suffering exactly as oneself, so there is no reason to protect oneself alone; the world is to be protected as one's own body with its many limbs.

name: Examining the teacher (and the disciple)

name: Exchanging self and other

method_summary: Requiting enmity (accepting suffering as past karma), according with conditions, seeking nothing, and according with the Dharma.

name: The Four-Session Guru Yoga of the 8th Karmapa
method_summary: A guru yoga recited in four sessions daily, supplicating the Karmapa as the union of all lineage gurus.

name: The four thoughts that turn the mind (blo ldog rnam bzhi)
method_summary: Repeated contemplation of the precious human birth, impermanence and death, the defects of saṃsāra and cause and effect, until the mind turns from worldly aims; practised at the start of every session.

name: The four yogic stages of the Laṅkāvatāra
method_summary: Mount to mind-only and stop imagining external objects; rest in suchness and pass beyond mind-only; pass beyond the imageless (even non-dual awareness as an image); abiding in the imageless, see the Mahāyāna.

name: Bhīṣma's fourfold meditation (dhyāna-yoga)

Recitation of the Sāvitrī verse preceded by Oṃ and the three utterances, especially at the twilights (MDh 2.76–78; YS 1.22–25).
alt_notes: The rules of who may recite it and how often belong to the gṛhya and dharma literature (U02).

name: Meditation on the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Venerate the Gāyatrī as all this — speech, earth, body, heart — whose four feet are the worlds, the Vedas, the breaths and the sun; and the space within the heart as identical with the space outside (ChU 3.12; BAU 5.14).

queries: prepared segments: ChU 3.12, BĀU 5.14
checks.note: Located: ChU 3.12.1-9 (the Gāyatrī is all this — speech, earth, body, heart; 3.12.6 = RV 10.90.3; 3.12.7-9 on the three spaces) and BĀU 5.14.1-8 (its four feet, the fourth 'darśataṃ padaṃ parorajāḥ'). All 2 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ChU 3.12; BĀU 5.14). It rests on 2 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Gelug Mahāmudrā meditation on the mind
method_summary: After preliminaries and guru yoga, one takes the mind itself — its mere clarity and knowing — as the object of calm abiding; then, with that calm, investigates the mind's way of existing to realise its emptiness; alternately in the mantra approach through the clear light.

equivalents.note: the Kagyu Mahāmudrā practice; the Gelug root text says both converge in one intent

name: Generating the awakening mind
method_summary: In the Nyingma preliminaries: training in the four boundless attitudes, taking the vow of aspiring and applying bodhicitta, equalizing and exchanging self and others, and taking on others' suffering.
alt_method_summary: Preceded by love, contemplating beings' sufferings and resolving irreversibly to free them; then taking the aspiring mind by ritual and repeating it.

After worship, refuge and confession, one rejoices in the virtue of all beings, requests the Buddhas to teach and not to pass away, dedicates merit, and then generates the awakening mind for the good of the world, afterwards rejoicing and inviting all beings as guests to happiness.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).

name: Mahāyoga generation stage (bskyed rim)
method_summary: From the three samādhis (suchness, all-illuminating compassion, the seed syllable) the practitioner generates the maṇḍala and deity, with clear appearance, vajra pride and recollection of purity, purifying the habits of birth, and recites the mantra; everything is seen as deity, sound as mantra, thought as wisdom.
prerequisites: empowerment
preliminaries

name: Dense recitation (ghanapāṭha)
method_summary: The most elaborate commonly practised recitation (ab ba abc cba abc, bc cb bcd dcb bcd …), whose master is called ghanapāṭhin.

name: The sevenfold yoga of the pot (ghaṭastha-yoga)
method_summary: The Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā's whole course: cleansing acts, postures, mudrās, withdrawal, breath-control, meditation and samādhi, each producing one quality of the 'pot' (purity, firmness, steadiness, calm, lightness, perception of the self, non-attachment).

name: Gross, luminous and subtle meditation (Gheraṇḍa)
method_summary: Gross: visualize a jewel island in an ocean of nectar in the heart with the chosen deity (or the guru in the lotus of the crown); luminous: meditate on kuṇḍalinī as a flame at the root, the navel sun, or the praṇava-light between the brows; subtle: by śāmbhavī, on awakened kuṇḍalinī (GS 6.1–22).

warnings.text: Subtle meditation is secret, hard even for the gods to obtain (a warning of secrecy).

name: The Dol festival at Ghoshpara
method_summary: At Dol Pūrṇimā (Holi) devotees gather at Ghoshpara at Satī Mā's shrine, bathe in the Himsāgar tank, tie threads at the pomegranate tree for healing and boons, and sing; many are possessed by bhāva.

name: Caring for the sick
method_summary: Nursing sick fellow monks, as the Buddha did: 'whoever would attend on me should attend on the sick' (Vin Mv 8.26).

name: The meditation seat and posture of the Gītā
method_summary: A firm seat of one's own in a clean place, neither too high nor too low, spread with kuśa grass, a deerskin and cloth; sitting there, hold body, head and neck erect, motionless and steady.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

notes: The order of the layers (cloth, skin, grass) is read differently by commentators.
alt_method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 6.11–13: in a clean place, a firm seat of one's own, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass; sitting on it with body, head and neck held in line and motionless, steady, gaze toward the tip of the nose, not looking about.
alt_notes: Commentators take the layering as kuśa grass beneath, skin above it, cloth on top.

name: Study and hearing of the Gītā
method_summary: Studying the dialogue is worship of the Lord by the sacrifice of knowledge; hearing it with faith and without cavil brings the worlds of the righteous; teaching it to devotees is the dearest service (18.68–71).

warnings.text: It is not to be told to one without austerity or devotion, who does not wish to hear, or who speaks ill of the Lord.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

alt_method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 15.20: understanding (buddhvā) this most secret teaching one becomes wise and one who has done what is to be done.

name: Song as offering (gīta)
method_summary: Singing of the Lord's qualities and deeds, following the rules of music.

name: Giving body, enjoyments and merit
method_summary: The bodhisattva mentally gives away his body, possessions and the merit of the three times to all beings, and then protects, purifies and increases them for beings' use; physical giving of the body is a matter only for those whose compassion is pure — summary only.

warnings.text: The body, which serves the true Dharma, should not be harmed for a lesser purpose; life should not be given up while the intention of compassion is impure.
If body and possessions are not protected, how can they be enjoyed by beings? What is given but cannot be used is no gift.

notes: Marked restricted because it touches on giving the body; only the texts' summary and warnings are recorded.

name: The alms-round (gocarī)
method_summary: The mendicant goes from house to house taking a little food 'like a bee from flowers', accepting only what was not prepared for him and is free of the faults of alms; Śvetāmbara mendicants collect in bowls and eat in their lodging; the Digambara monk eats once a day, standing, from his cupped hands, at a house where he is ceremonially received.

name: The gift of the Vaitaraṇī cow
method_summary: Giving a (dark) cow to a brahmin at or before death so that the dead may cross the Vaitaraṇī by boat.

queries: rests_on teachings and cited refs located
checks.note: All teachings it rests on were located in the local e-texts (see their checks).

name: The fivefold transmission rite (gojū sōden)
method_summary: Jōdo-shū's multi-day rite transmitting the teaching of the school in five stages to monks and lay people, ending in the entrustment of the nenbutsu.
notes: Outline only; details not recalled with confidence.

name: The Golden Light confession
method_summary: Confessing all evil done in ignorance before the buddhas, as heard from the golden drum; rejoicing and dedication; used in East Asian repentance rites.

name: Gomukhāsana (the cow-face seat)
method_summary: The right ankle set beside the left buttock and the left beside the right, so that the legs resemble a cow's face (HYP 1.20); in the Gheraṇḍa the feet are on the ground with the heels by the sides of the back and the body steady (GS 2.16).
notes: Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra. The Śivasaṃhitā (5.5) counts 'sitting in gomukha' among the obstacles that take the form of knowledge.

name: Recitation of the Gopāla mantra
method_summary: Worship and recitation of Kṛṣṇa's five-part mantra with meditation on his form (Gopālapūrvatāpanī).

queries: e-text refs of prc:gopala-mantra-japa
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 1 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

name: Gorakṣāsana (Gorakṣa's seat)
method_summary: The feet turned up between the knees and thighs, the heels covered with the upturned hands, the throat contracted and the gaze on the nose-tip (GS 2.24-25). In HYP 1.54 'gorakṣāsana' is the siddhas' name for bhadrāsana.
signs_of_progress: a cause of success for yogins (GS 2.25)

name: Gifts for the planets (graha-dāna)
method_summary: Giving to brahmins the gift proper to the afflicting planet — objects, grains, cloth, metals or animals of its colour and nature — as part of the planetary sacrifice or on its own; also great gifts of gold, food, cows and land to pacify heavenly portents.

name: Pacification of the planets (grahayajña, navagraha-homa)
method_summary: The nine planets are installed as images of their prescribed materials or drawn in their colours in their directions, worshipped with their own Vedic mantras, and offered oblations in the fire with each planet's fuel-stick, followed by food offerings and gifts to brahmins; performed for peace, prosperity, rain, long life and nourishment, when a planet is badly placed in transit or period, and before great undertakings.
prerequisites: a qualified priest for the fire-rite

warnings.text: Rites alone — mantra, consecration, amulets, pacification, oblation, fasting, worship, recitation — do not bring success, or the king's priest would be king.
The one whom a planet afflicts at a given time should worship that planet with special care.

name: Vows and fasts for the planets
method_summary: Keeping a fast or restricted diet and worship on the weekday of an afflicting planet (Sunday for the Sun, Saturday for Saturn and so on), or on related lunar days, often for a set number of weeks, with its colour, food and gift.
notes: Later practice; classical source not checked. Not a prolonged fast.

name: Observances at an eclipse
method_summary: From the onset of the restricted period before an eclipse no food is cooked or eaten; at the eclipse one bathes, recites mantras, makes oblations and gifts (whose offering Rāhu receives by Brahmā's boon), and bathes again at its end; mantra-recitation then is held especially fruitful.

warnings.text: A child born during an eclipse faces disease and danger and requires pacification.

notes: The fast is limited to the eclipse period; not a prolonged fast.

name: Recitation of the tradition's scripture (pārāyaṇa)
method_summary: Reading or chanting a whole scripture in a set period: the Jñāneśvarī or Gāthā (Vārkarī), the Rāmcaritmānas in nine days (navāhna) or a month (māsa-pārāyaṇa) (Rāmānandī and wider Hindi-speaking devotion), the Kīrtana-ghoṣā and Bhāgavata in the nāmghar (Ekaśaraṇa).

name: Breath-control through moon and sun (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: In the bound lotus, filling through the left (moon) and releasing through the right (sun) while meditating on the moon-disc, then the reverse while meditating on the sun-disc at the navel; this purifies the channels and manifests the inner sound.

warnings.text: Draw in and release the breath slowly; do not hold it beyond measure nor release it hastily.
Avoid pungent, sour and salty food; take milk.

signs_of_progress: sweat, then trembling, then rising up (GŚ 49); purified channels, kindled fire, inner sound, health (GŚ-Briggs 101)
notes: Measures of retention given in the text are not reproduced.

name: The five seals and locks of the Gorakṣaśataka
method_summary: Mahāmudrā, nabhomudrā (khecarī), uḍḍiyāna, jālandhara and mūlabandha: one who knows them is fit for success; uḍḍiyāna conquers death, jālandhara stops the nectar falling into the fire, mūlabandha draws apāna upward.

warnings.text: The reversed practice is to be obtained from the guru's mouth.

name: The five element-concentrations (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: Holding the mind with the breath on earth (heart, yellow, square, la), water (throat, white crescent, va), fire (palate, red triangle, ra), air (between the brows, smoky circle, ya) and space (brahmarandhra, clear, ha, with Sadāśiva); they stabilise, dissolve, burn, whirl and dry, and the space-concentration opens the door of liberation.
notes: The fixed durations in the text are not reproduced.

name: Meditation with and without qualities (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: With the gaze at the nose-tip, meditating on the centres in their colours (with qualities) and on the attributeless Śiva in the sky and the all-pervading self (without qualities); adjuncts are removed by practice.

name: Guarding the mind with mindfulness and alertness
method_summary: Guarding the doors of the senses with mindfulness, alertness and conscientiousness; examining the mind-stream three times each day and night.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).
alt_method_summary: Because the training cannot be kept without guarding the mind, the mind is bound with the rope of mindfulness and its states of body and mind are repeatedly examined by introspection, before acting, speaking or thinking.

name: Keeping the vow hidden (gūḍhavrata)
method_summary: He keeps his knowledge, austerity, vow and mantras concealed.

name: Worship of Hari with qualities according to fitness
method_summary: Meditative worship (upāsanā) of Hari under the qualities fit for the worshipper: Brahmā with all qualities, humans as bliss (ānanda), knower (jña) and the ever-existing Self (sadātmā); the gods are liberated when Hari becomes directly perceived through such worship.

warnings.text: A person who desires what he is unfit for surely falls; serve Viṣṇu according to your fitness.

name: Seeing that the guṇas act: non-doership
method_summary: Knowing that the guṇas act upon the guṇas (3.28) and that the senses move among their objects, the knower of truth thinks 'I do nothing at all' (5.8–9); he sits as one indifferent, knowing 'the guṇas are acting' (14.23), and sees prakṛti as the doer and the self as non-doer (13.29).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.
Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

alt_method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 5.8–9: the yoked knower of reality thinks 'I do nothing at all' while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing, speaking, releasing, grasping and blinking, holding that it is the senses that move among the objects of the senses.

Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Whoever sees actions done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer sees truly (13.30); the seer who sees no doer other than the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains the Lord's state (14.19); the one beyond the guṇas sits as one indifferent, unshaken, knowing only that 'the guṇas are operating' (14.23).
notes: In 5.8–9 the text says that the senses move among the objects of the senses (indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartante), not, as in 3.28, that the guṇas move among the guṇas; the knower's thought 'I do nothing' is the same.
signs_of_progress: Neither hating illumination, activity and delusion when present nor longing for them when gone (14.22).

name: Guptāsana (the hidden seat)
method_summary: The feet hidden between the knees and thighs and the anus placed on the feet (GS 2.20); HYP 1.37 gives guptāsana as another name of siddhāsana.

name: The controls and carefulnesses
method_summary: Restraining mind, speech and body, and moving, speaking, begging, handling objects and excreting with constant care not to injure living beings — looking ahead while walking, sweeping with the broom (rajoharaṇa/picchī), speaking gently.

name: Devotion to the teacher (guru-bhakti)
method_summary: Hold the highest devotion to God and to one's teacher as to God (ŚU 6.23); honour the teacher as a god (TU 1.11.2); the pupils worship Pippalāda as the father who takes them across (PrU 6.8).

queries: prepared segments: ŚU 6.23, TU 1.11.2, PrU 6.8
checks.note: All 3 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ŚU 6.23; TU 1.11.2; PrU 6.8). It rests on 3 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

alt_method_summary: Treating the guru as father, mother and Maheśvara, never slandering or disobeying him; the disciple first tests the guru, then serves him.

Honouring the true guru as the giver of the Name, above or equal to God: surrender, service and remembrance of the guru; among Bāuls and Kartābhajās worship of the living guru as the human form of the Lord.

Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs; Bhakti Sūtras): Madhurakavi's devotion to Nammāḻvār — his teacher's name sweeter than Kṛṣṇa, 'I know no other god', the teacher as mother and father; the Nārada Sūtra: devotion comes chiefly by the grace of great souls, who are not different from the Lord.

warnings.text: Disciples who break the guru's command and slander him become 'dead while living'.
Kāl sends false teachers in the true guru's name.

name: Devotion to the vajra master
method_summary: After mutual examination, the disciple regards the guru as inseparable from Vajradhara, bows three times a day, offers gifts, follows instructions and observes the etiquette of the Gurupañcāśikā (not stepping on his shadow, rising when he arrives, speaking softly); Saraha's songs praise the guru as boat, physician and sun.

warnings.text: The disciple who despises his master despises all buddhas and meets only suffering.

name: Meditation on the guru's form
method_summary: Meditating on the guru's form, the root of meditation, often visualized in the lotus of the head at dawn (Devī Gītā 7.40.1).

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:guru-dhyana
checks.note: Guru Gītā 79 ('dhyānamūlaṃ gurormūrtiḥ') and DBhP 7.40.1 (at dawn, the guru in the lotus of the head) verified.

name: Recitation of the Guru Gītā
method_summary: Reciting or chanting the Guru Gītā, prescribed in the text for success, protection and liberation at death; in recent times chanted daily in Muktananda's ashrams.

warnings.text: Not to be taught to the faithless, the deceiver or the hypocrite.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:guru-gita-recitation
checks.note: Rests on tea:guru-gita:173-181; each was located in the local text and matches this entry's statement.

name: Worship of the guru's feet (pādukā) and the circle of gurus
method_summary: Daily contemplation of the guru's feet in the crown with nectar flowing from them (PKS 2.2), recitation of the pādukā given at initiation, and worship of the lineage of gurus in their divine, perfected and human streams.

name: Worship of the guru's sandals (pādukā)
method_summary: Worship of the guru's sandals and recitation of the lineage's pādukā-mantra — 'no mantra beyond the pādukā, no god beyond the guru' (Kulārṇava 12.12).

name: Service of the teacher
method_summary: Serving and worshipping the teacher as the Lord in body, speech and mind; in the Guru Gītā the guru's satisfaction fulfils all practices.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:guru-seva
checks.note: AR 3.4.32 ('manovākkāyasadbhaktyā sadguroḥ parisevanam'), AR 3.10.24 ('ācāryopāsanaṃ ... madbuddhyā') and Guru Gītā 36-38, 70-80 verified.

alt_method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.8: attendance on the teacher (ācāryopāsana) is listed among the twenty dispositions called knowledge; no procedure is given.
Voluntary service to the Master and community (Sant Mat: physical, financial and mental sevā at the Dera); among Bāuls feeding and serving sādhus (sādhu-sevā).

name: Approaching a teacher with fuel in hand
method_summary: Having become disgusted with the worlds won by action, go 'fuel in hand' to a teacher learned in the Veda and established in brahman (MuU 1.2.12); live with the teacher a set time in austerity, celibacy and faith before asking (PrU 1.2); serve the teacher (ChU 4.4-9, 8.7-12, 8.15).

checks.note: All 10 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (MuU 1.2.12; PrU 1.2; ChU 4.4-9; ChU 8.7-12; ChU 8.15; MuU 1.2.12-13; PrU 1.1-2; ChU 4.4-4.9; ChU 8.7-8.12; KauU 1.1). It rests on 5 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Approaching the teacher (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: Approaching, 'fuel in hand', a teacher learned in scripture and established in Brahman, with humility, service and questioning, and receiving the teaching repeatedly until it is grasped.

name: Guru yoga
method_summary: Visualizing the guru as Vajradhara (in the Karma Kagyu, the Karmapa), supplicating with devotion, receiving the four empowerments as lights, and merging one's mind with the guru's; the most important of the preliminaries because realization comes through blessing.

equivalents.note: devotion to the teacher is common; guru yoga adds visualization, empowerment and mixing of minds

notes: Shared id with U45.
alt_method_summary: Visualizing one's teacher as Padmasambhava (or in Bön as Tapihritsa or Shenrab), making the seven-branch offering, supplicating with the Seven-line prayer and Vajra Guru mantra, receiving the four empowerments by lights from the guru's three places, and mingling one's mind with the guru's wisdom mind, then resting in that state; the root of blessing and realization in Dzogchen.

Visualising the teacher as inseparable from the Buddha — Tsongkhapa with his two sons in the Hundred Deities of Tuṣita, or Lobsang Thubwang Dorje Chang in the Offering to the Spiritual Master — offering the seven limbs and maṇḍala, making requests, receiving blessings and dissolving the teacher into oneself.
alt_notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).

name: Surrender to the guru (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: The fifth means of the Nimbārka school: complete dependence on the guru, who then performs the means on the disciple's behalf.

name: Worship of Hanumān
method_summary: Recitation of the Hanumān Cālīsā (often on Tuesdays and Saturdays) and worship at Hanumān/Māruti shrines as Rāma's servant and remover of obstacles; the Samartha sampradāya joins it to the cultivation of bodily strength.

name: The Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra
method_summary: The sixteen names 'hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare / hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare' (the Kalisantaraṇa gives the Hare Rāma half first), chanted in japa or sung in kīrtana; the Upaniṣad states there are no rules of time, place or purity for it.

name: Recitation of the sixteen names
method_summary: Repeating 'hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare, hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare'; the Kalisantaraṇa says no rule binds it, and that three and a half crore repetitions free from the gravest sins.
notes: Gauḍīya practice recites it with the 'hare kṛṣṇa' half first; the Upaniṣad gives the 'hare rāma' half first.

queries: e-text refs of prc:hare-krsna-mahamantra-japa
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 2 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

name: Remembering Hari as the doer; action as worship
method_summary: Doing the prescribed duties and avoiding the forbidden, without desire for results, while remembering that Hari within moves one's limbs and that all acts of mind, speech and body are his worship — the Yogadīpikā's definition of yoga.

name: Week of the name (harināma saptāh)
method_summary: A village holds seven days of continuous singing of the name and reading of the Jñāneśvarī or the Gāthā, with nightly kīrtan, ending with a common meal.
duration: seven days

name: Loud laughter as offering (hasita, aṭṭahāsa)
method_summary: Loud laughter ('a-ha-ha'), opening throat and lips, offered to the Lord while absorbed in meditation on Śiva.

name: Hasti-niṣadana (sitting like an elephant)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: The restraints and observances of the haṭha texts
method_summary: The ten yamas (non-harming, truth, non-stealing, continence, forbearance, fortitude, compassion, straightforwardness, moderate diet, purity) and ten niyamas of the interpolated HYP verses and the Yoga Yājñavalkya; the SS's list of things to avoid (3.33) and to follow (3.35); in the HYP the ethical frame is chiefly celibacy, moderate diet and renunciation (1.57).

name: The postures of the Haṭhābhyāsapaddhati (group entry)
method_summary: A prose haṭha manual that describes more than a hundred postures (about 112 are counted), set in a sequence after the yamas, niyamas and cleansing acts and before breath-control and mudrā; many are dynamic or repeated movements and some use a rope. Its postures reappear, illustrated, in the Mysore Śrītattvanidhi. The individual names are not recalled with enough confidence to be entered here (see REPORT).
notes: Group entry standing in for the individual postures the unit could not responsibly name.

name: The eighty-four postures of the Haṭharatnāvalī (group entry)
method_summary: The Haṭharatnāvalī (ch. 3) names eighty-four postures and describes a selection, repeating the Haṭhapradīpikā's descriptions for several (siddha, padma, siṃha, bhadra and others) and adding many variants; the full list is not entered here because the unit could not recall it reliably (see REPORT for candidate names to check).

name: Havelī kīrtan
method_summary: Temple singing of the aṣṭachāp poets' songs in classical rāgas matched to each period of the day and season, as part of the Lord's service.

name: Hearing, reflection and cultivation
method_summary: Wisdom arises in three stages — from hearing the teaching, from reflecting on it with reasoning, and from meditative cultivation — which are three of the seventeen stages of the Yogācārabhūmi; for the pramāṇa school, reasoning (cintā) establishes what cultivation then makes vivid.

name: Meditation in the heart lotus
method_summary: Seated in solitude, body straight, meditating on the Lord (with Umā; or as the thumb-sized Oṃ; or as the flame) in the heart lotus (Kaivalya 5–7; Dhyānabindu 19; Vāsudeva).

queries: e-text refs of prc:heart-lotus-meditation
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 1 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

name: Reciting the Heart Sūtra and its mantra
method_summary: Recitation of the Heart Sūtra and 'gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā', daily in East Asian monasteries and, in Tibet, to avert obstacles.

name: Hevajra practice in the Sakya
method_summary: After receiving the Hevajra empowerment of the Lamdre, the practitioner daily performs the Hevajra sādhana of the generation stage and, under instruction, the completion-stage practices of the method continuum; the daily practice is a commitment of those empowered.
prerequisites: Hevajra empowerment
the Lamdre Tsokshé or Lobshé instruction

warnings.text: Completion-stage practices of the body-method continuum are restricted; the Vajra Verses list obstacles and their protections.

notes: Summary only; restricted completion-stage content not recorded.

name: Pilgrimage to Hiṅglāj
method_summary: Pilgrimage to the Goddess at Hiṅglāj (Balochistan), made by Kīnārām according to tradition and honoured by Aghora and Nāth ascetics.

name: Tantric fire offering (homa)
method_summary: Offerings into the fire for the four activities (pacifying, increasing, subjugating, destroying) as part of sādhana and consecration rites (Vajrāvalī); the siddhas deride it when done without knowledge.

warnings.text: Pointless fire offerings only hurt the eyes with smoke.

name: Hōonkō, the memorial assembly for Shinran
method_summary: The annual assembly of gratitude on the anniversary of Shinran's death, with the reading of Kakunyo's Godenshō and sermons, the central event of the Shinshū year.

name: Casting and reading the horoscope
method_summary: From the moment and place of birth the astrologer computes the rising sign, the planets, the divisional charts, strengths and the running periods, then judges the houses, yogas and periods to declare the ripening of past karma, with remedies where evil is shown; the Kerala practice begins with the astrologer's own worship and the omens at the time of consultation.
prerequisites: mastery of computation and horā (BS 2)
the qualities of a daivajña (BPHS 1.7–8)

warnings.text: One who predicts by trickery, feigned possession or eavesdropping is no knower of fate and is not to be consulted.

name: Meditation in the heart-lotus (Uddhava's instruction)
method_summary: Seated evenly, gaze at the nose-tip, purify the breath-channels, raise Oṃ in the heart like a bell; visualise the upturned eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the Lord's form in the fire; meditate on all its limbs, then on the smile, then fix the mind in space, then think of nothing; the self is seen in the Lord, light in light (BhP 11.14.32-46).

warnings.text: Keep far from the company of the attached; meditate in a secluded, safe place.

name: Huatou / hwadu (observing the critical phrase)
method_summary: Pressing down all discriminating mind and holding the key word of a case (e.g. 'wu') with doubt at every moment and in every posture, without interpreting it, until the doubt shatters.

warnings.text: Eight things to avoid: understanding it as being or non-being, by reasoning, by deliberation, in gestures, in words, sinking into no-concern, accepting it where raised, seeking proof in texts (Dahui).
Do not wait for awakening: 'if you keep your mind on the breaking, it will never break' (Dahui).

prerequisites: great faith, great doubt, great determination (Gaofeng)

name: Turning the light around (huiguang fanzhao / hoegwang banjo)
method_summary: Turning awareness back from its objects to its source — asking who it is that sees, hears and asks, or listening back to the hearing-nature — so as to recognise the empty and calm numinous awareness.

name: Illusory-body yoga
method_summary: Training to see oneself, the deity and the whole world as illusion, dream, mirror-image and painted Vajrasattva (Tilopa, from Nāgārjuna); in the Ārya completion stage, the arising of the self-consecration body of wind and mind after the empties, 'the vision of conventional truth', obtained by the guru's grace.
prerequisites: consecration
mind isolation (for the completion-stage form)

warnings.text: Without the self-consecration stage, obtained only by the guru's grace, labour in sūtra and tantra is in vain.

name: Illusory body yoga (sgyu lus)
method_summary: Seeing one's body, appearances and all beings as illusory — like a mirror image, a rainbow, the moon in water — first by contemplation and in daily life, then (in the completion stage) arising as the pure illusory body of the deity.
signs_of_progress: the eight worldly concerns self-liberated
attachment and aversion subside
notes: The contemplative portion is not restricted; the completion-stage 'pure illusory body' depends on restricted wind practices.

name: Loathing practice: contemplating the body's impurity (Jingtu shiyi lun)
method_summary: To turn from the five desires, the aspirant contemplates the body as impure in seven ways (seed, conception, dwelling in the womb, nourishment, birth, the body's contents, death), gradually, even if he cannot yet leave his family; paired with joyful aspiration for the Pure Land.

name: Closing the doors of the senses with the intellect
method_summary: With the intellect he shuts all the doors (senses), so that outwardly their working seems deranged.

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses
method_summary: Withdraw the senses from their objects as a tortoise draws in its limbs (2.58); restrain them first and so slay desire (3.41); move among objects with senses free of attraction and aversion (2.64); Alarka learns the senses are conquered not by force but by yoga (Anugītā 14.30).

warnings.text: The turbulent senses carry off the mind even of a wise man who strives.
Abstaining from objects removes them but not the taste, which ceases only on seeing the supreme.

alt_method_summary: Offering the senses into the fires of restraint (4.26) and the actions of senses and breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint kindled by knowledge (4.27); restraint of the senses is a condition for gaining knowledge (4.39); in meditation the whole troop of senses is restrained on every side by the mind (6.24); external contacts are put outside (5.27).

name: Sense restraint (indriyasaṃvara)
method_summary: Seeing a form with the eye (and so for each sense) one does not grasp at its signs and features, through which covetousness and grief might invade, but guards the faculty (DN 2; MN 27; MN 39); not blindness but quick equanimity (MN 152).

equivalents.note: Yoga's withdrawal of the senses; the Buddhist practice guards the senses while they function

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses (indriya-saṃyama)
method_summary: Withdraw the senses from their objects on all sides as a tortoise draws in its limbs (2.58); restraining them all, sit yoked, intent on Kṛṣṇa (2.61); keep the senses withheld from their objects on all sides (2.68); move among objects with senses free of attraction and aversion and under the self's control (2.64); control the senses by the mind while acting (3.7); restrain the senses first in order to slay desire (3.41).
signs_of_progress: wisdom firmly established (2.58, 2.61, 2.68)
serenity (prasāda), the end of all sorrows and steady understanding (2.64–65)
even the inner taste for objects turns away on seeing the highest (2.59)

warnings.text: For one who abstains, the objects turn away but the taste (rasa) remains; it turns away only on seeing the highest.

The mind that follows the roving senses carries off wisdom as the wind a ship on the water.
Restraining the organs of action while dwelling on objects in the mind is hypocrisy (mithyācāra).
Beings follow their nature; 'what will restraint accomplish?'
Attraction and aversion lie in the object of each sense; do not come under their sway, for they are waylayers.

name: Offering sense objects into the fires of the senses
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.26: offering the sense objects, beginning with sound, into the fires of the senses — the senses' taking of their objects described as a fire-offering.

name: The inner sacrifice of the senses (Anugītā)
method_summary: Contemplating the senses, mind and intellect as the seven tongues of the fire Vaiśvānara within, their objects as fuel-sticks, and the knower-functions as priests, one offers the objects into the fires within (Anugītā 14.20–24).
notes: Related to the prāṇāgnihotra of the Āraṇyakas (U02).

name: Inner worship: japa, meditation, pūjā, homa as acts of consciousness
method_summary: Outer ritual is for the gross; japa is the repeated contemplation of the supreme state, meditation the formless steady understanding, worship the firm mind in the great void, oblation the offering of elements, senses and objects with the mind into the fire of consciousness, bathing the entry into one's own nature (VBT 144-153; Paramārthasāra 74-80).

equivalents.note: inner worship (antaryāga) of other Śākta and Śaiva systems

name: Contemplation of the postures (iriyāpatha)
method_summary: The monk knows 'I am walking', 'standing', 'sitting', 'lying down', and knows the body however it is disposed (MN 10:6-7).

name: Gazing on the iṣṭaliṅga (liṅga-yoga)
method_summary: Holding the liṅga on the palm at eye level and gazing on it steadily, then turning the gaze inward to the liṅga within; taught in modern Śivayoga training and associated in legend with the 'unblinking' (animiṣa) yogi.

name: Worship of the iṣṭaliṅga on the palm
method_summary: Daily worship of one's own liṅga held on the left palm (karapīṭha) with water, ash, flowers and the like, without invocation or dismissal because Śiva already abides in it; the palm-worship is ranked above worship on an outer pedestal.

warnings.text: Never abandon liṅga-worship, even at the loss of possessions or life.

Through it the obstacles do not arise and the yogin sees his own form (YS 1.29); it brings the perfection of samādhi (YS 2.45).

name: Worship of the Lord (Nyāya)
method_summary: Worship (upāsti) of the Lord, declared by the wise to be the path to heaven and liberation; for the Naiyāyika it includes the reasoned contemplation of Him.

name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)
method_summary: Renouncing all actions in Kṛṣṇa, with a mind directed to the self, free of expectation and of 'mine', and with the fever gone, act (fight) (3.30); those who follow this teaching constantly, with faith and without carping, are freed from actions (3.31).

warnings.text: Those who cavil at this teaching and do not follow it are deluded in all knowledge and lost.
