alt_method_summary: Outer purity with earth, water and pure food, and inner washing away of the mind's stains (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: disgust for one's own body, non-contact with others; purity of sattva, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, fitness to see the self (2.40–41)

name: Recitation of the Saundaryalaharī
method_summary: Recitation of the hundred verses as praise and worship; popular manuals attach to each verse a yantra, a method of recitation and a fruit.
notes: The verse-by-verse prayoga tradition is recorded from memory; source manuals not identified.

name: Sautrāmaṇī
method_summary: A rite to Indra the good protector (sutrāman) with offerings including surā, performed for healing and restoration.

queries: local VS 19.1
checks.note: VS 19.1 'svādvīṃ tvā svādunā … indrāya sutrāmṇe pacyasva' opens the sautrāmaṇī — 'VS 19–21' confirmed.

name: Practice seated on a corpse (śava-sādhana)
method_summary: A vīra rite of winning the Goddess's vision seated on a corpse in the cremation ground, as in the account of Sarvānanda. Restricted: named only.

warnings.text: The wilful, the uninitiated, one who drinks the unconsecrated substance, takes a woman by force or kills for his own pleasure, and the addict without Kaula instruction go to hell; the intoxicated Kaula knows neither meditation nor God nor guru and falls.

Aghora practice is given only by the guru and kept secret; the recent teacher Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām is reported to have taught that it is naturalness and service, not spectacle (the lineage's oral rule as reported; no text located — to be sourced).

alt_method_summary: A rite seated upon a corpse in the cremation ground, attributed to Aghora and Śākta adepts; recorded only as named.

name: Śavāsana (the corpse; mṛtāsana)
method_summary: Lying supine on the ground like a corpse (HYP 1.32; GS 2.19); the Dattātreyayogaśāstra counts lying like a corpse, relaxed in solitude, among the 'signals' of laya-yoga (DYŚ 22-23).
signs_of_progress: removes fatigue and brings rest to the mind (HYP 1.32; GS 2.19)
notes: Later 'yoga-nidrā' teachings built on this posture belong to recent lineages (U52).

name: Savikalpa samādhi (Vedānta)
method_summary: Absorption with the mental mode resting in Brahman while the distinction of knower and known remains; with inner and outer forms, attended by objects or by words (Dṛg-Dṛśya Viveka).

warnings.text: Relishing its bliss (rasāsvāda) obstructs nirvikalpa samādhi.

name: Seeing the Lord in all beings and bowing to all
method_summary: Regarding every being as the Lord, with equal vision toward brāhmaṇa and outcaste, prostrating even to dog, outcaste, cow and donkey, ignoring others' laughter, until the vision of the Lord in all arises; images are worshipped only until the Lord is known in one's own heart and in all beings.

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:seeing-the-lord-in-all-beings
checks.note: Rests on tea:uddhava-gita:11.29.12-19, tea:kapila-gita:3.29.21-25; each was located in the local text and matches this entry's statement.

alt_method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.28–29: seeing the supreme lord standing the same in all beings, not perishing among the perishing; seeing the lord equally present everywhere one does not harm oneself and goes to the highest goal. (The Gītā here speaks of seeing, not of bowing.)

name: The self-introspection diary
method_summary: Daily written record of failures in non-violence, truthfulness, chastity, love for all and selfless service, and of time given to meditation, introduced by Kirpal Singh.

name: Holding the mind (sems 'dzin)
method_summary: A set of Heart-essence exercises (traditionally twenty-one) using posture, sound, breath and visualization to produce experiences in which awareness can be recognized.

name: Serving one's parents as dharma
method_summary: The meat-seller serves his aged parents as gods and sends Kauśika home to serve his own (MBh 3.204–206).

name: Seeking and serving the spiritual friend
method_summary: Seeking out good friends without weariness and honoring them — Sudhana's pilgrimage and Sadāprarudita's sacrifice are the models; the buddhas and perfections are the bodhisattva's true friends.

warnings.text: New bodhisattvas in the hands of bad friends become frightened of the profound teaching.

name: Sesshin (intensive retreat)
method_summary: Periods (usually seven days) of intensive zazen, interviews and talks in silence, e.g. the rōhatsu sesshin ending on 8 December for the Buddha's awakening.

name: The seven attentions (sapta manaskārāḥ)
method_summary: The yogin frees himself from desire for sense-pleasures by (1) discerning the coarseness of the lower and the peace of the higher level, (2) resolve, (3) seclusion (abandoning the stronger afflictions), (4) gathering delight, (5) examination (checking for remaining desire), (6) the completion of practice, (7) its fruit — the absorption.

sources.ref: fourth part of the third yogasthāna

name: The sevenfold (seven-branch) worship
method_summary: Homage, offering, confession, rejoicing, requesting the teaching, requesting the buddhas to remain, dedication — from the Bhadracarī; the frame of Tibetan and Newar liturgies.

name: Recitation of the Seven-line prayer
method_summary: Recitation of the seven-line invocation of Padmasambhava, alone or at the start of guru yoga and other practices.

name: The seven-point cause-and-effect meditation for bodhicitta
method_summary: Establishing equanimity toward friends, enemies and strangers, then meditating in sequence: all beings have been one's mother; their kindness as mothers; the wish to repay it; affectionate love; great compassion; the extraordinary resolve to free them oneself; and bodhicitta.

equivalents.note: the other lamrim method for bodhicitta; Gelug teachers often combine the two

name: The seven-point meditation posture

names.name: lus gnad bdun (the seven key points of body)

method_summary: Legs crossed, spine straight, hands in the meditation gesture below the navel, shoulders open, neck straightened, tongue and gaze settled; 'straighten like a plantain stem, cross like a lattice' (bka' dpe phyi ma).
notes: Usually called 'the seven points of Vairocana' in Tibetan manuals; the enumeration here is the common one (from memory), the bka' dpe phyi ma gives its own images.

name: The sevenfold reasoning (chariot analysis)
method_summary: The self is sought as a chariot is sought: is it other than its parts, identical with them, possessing them, in them, containing them, their collection or their shape? Not found in any of the seven ways, it is understood as a designation dependent on the aggregates, cutting the view of the transitory collection.
signs_of_progress: the view of a real self weakens; afflictions rooted in it lessen (MA 6.120)

name: The seven-limb practice
method_summary: The sevenfold worship of the Samantabhadra prayer (prostration, offering, confession, rejoicing, requesting teaching, requesting the teachers to remain, dedication), done before refuge (Atiśa) and in every lamrim session.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).
alt_method_summary: Worship of the Buddhas, the Dharma and the bodhisattvas with offerings (actual and imagined), praise and prostration, refuge, confession of faults, rejoicing in merit, requesting teaching, requesting the Buddhas to remain, and dedication — as the preparation for adopting the awakening mind.
alt_notes: The seven-limbed form follows the Bhadracarī (src:bhadracaripranidhana); its exact division in BCA 2–3 is from memory.

name: Closing the senses (ṣaṇmukhī)
method_summary: Closing ears, eyes and other openings with the fingers so that the inner sounds are heard.
signs_of_progress: sounds like bells (Yogacūḍāmaṇi 114–115)

queries: e-text refs of prc:shanmukhi-mudra
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 1 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

name: Abandoning the body to go to birth (sheshen wangsheng) — restricted
method_summary: Summary only: the rebirth biographies record people who ended their lives (for example by leaping from a tree) out of longing for the Pure Land; Daoxuan's early account attributes such a leap to a man who questioned Shandao, the later Fozu tongji to Shandao himself. Recorded as narrative, not as a practice to be taught.

warnings.text: Shandao's prayer in the account itself asks to die 'without losing right mindfulness'; the tradition's general teaching places birth in the Buddha's vow and recitation, not in the manner of death.

notes: Body-harming: restricted. No method recorded. Explicit warnings by later Pure Land teachers against the act were not verified and are listed as a gap.

name: Pacification practice (zhi byed)
method_summary: Instructions of Padampa Sangye for pacifying suffering: renunciation and devotion, resting the mind in the emptiness taught by the Perfection of Wisdom, and sūtra and mantra methods arranged along the five paths (details of the individual instructions not recalled).

name: Shikantaza (just sitting)
method_summary: Sitting wholeheartedly with no object, method or goal beyond the sitting itself — 'thinking of not-thinking: non-thinking'; understood as the enactment of original realization rather than a means to it.

warnings.text: Do not seek realization apart from practice (Bendōwa).

name: Calm abiding in the Great Perfection (zhi gnas)
method_summary: Calm abiding with a support (a letter A, an object, the breath), without support, and natural calm, as a foundation for recognizing awareness; in Bön the fixation on the white A of the A-tri.

name: Shinshū morning and evening service (gongyō)
method_summary: Recitation of the Shōshinge with the nenbutsu and six wasan before the enshrined image or name of Amida, as arranged by Rennyo; an act of gratitude, not a practice for birth.
notes: Arrangement attributed to Rennyo (1473), recalled.

name: Shouts and blows (he, bang)
method_summary: The teacher's shout or strike used to cut off conceptual thinking and test the student in encounter; Linji's four kinds of shout.

warnings.text: Dahui warns against imitating dramatic acts as 'wondrous function' without insight.

name: Guarding the mind (shouxin)
method_summary: Guarding the original true mind so that deluded thoughts do not arise and the sense of 'mine' ceases; with Daoxin's 'guarding the one without moving'.

warnings.text: The Platform Sūtra rejects 'viewing the mind' and 'viewing purity' as binding oneself with purity.

name: The sick bodhisattva's contemplation
method_summary: When ill, seeing the illness as arising from clinging to 'I' and 'mine', removing the illness but not the dharmas, and extending the insight that all beings' illness is likewise unreal into compassion.

name: Siddhar alchemy (iracavātam: mercury, pāṣāṇam, muppu)
method_summary: Summary only: the Siddhar art of 'binding' mercury, purifying and calcining poisonous minerals and using the secret salt (muppu), both to transmute metals and to make the body deathless; Bogar's Palani image of nine pāṣāṇams is its emblem. No substances, quantities or processes are recorded.

warnings.text: The knowledge is veiled in code language and given only to a proven disciple; unpurified mercury and pāṣāṇam are deadly poison.
All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).

notes: Restricted (metals/mercury).

name: Siddha daily regimen (nōy aṇukā viti)
method_summary: Rules by which disease does not approach: eat only after the previous meal is digested and in measure (Kuṟaḷ 942, 946); regular oil-baths, moderate sleep, restraint and seasonal adjustment as taught in the verses ascribed to Tēraiyar.
notes: Tēraiyar's specific rules recalled only in outline (low).

name: Seeking and worshipping the guru
method_summary: Seeking the master (āriyaṉ) and bowing at his feet (Pattirakiriyār 26); gazing daily on the guru as the flame of grace and seeing the Lord as the guru (Tirumūla ñāṉam 5–6).

name: Siddhar rites against enemies
method_summary: Summary only: some Siddhar worship-manuals (Rāmatēvar's Pūjāviti 5–7) include rites for striking down an enemy. No procedure recorded.

warnings.text: Is one to curse? Do no cruel deeds.

notes: Restricted (harmful rite).

name: Worship of the Siddhacakra
method_summary: Worship of a diagram (yantra) of nine stations — Arhat, Siddha, Ācārya, Upādhyāya, Sādhu, and right faith, knowledge, conduct and austerity — especially during the Navapada Olī; its legend is the story of Śrīpāla and Mayaṇāsundarī.

name: Siddhāsana (the adept's seat)
method_summary: Seated with the heel of one foot pressing the perineum (yonisthāna) and the other foot placed above the genitals, body straight, chin on the chest (a form of jālandhara), senses restrained and the gaze fixed between the brows (HYP 1.35; GS 2.7; ŚS 3.85; GŚ 8). A second arrangement with the left ankle above the genitals is given 'by another view' (HYP 1.36). The texts call it the chief of postures, the one to sit in always.

names.name: vajrāsana / muktāsana / guptāsana (other names reported in HYP 1.37)

signs_of_progress: purifies the 72,000 channels (HYP 1.39)
with it kevala kumbhaka, unmanī and the three locks arise spontaneously (HYP 1.41-42)
practised with moderate diet and meditation on the self for twelve years it brings completion (HYP 1.40)
breaks open the door of liberation (HYP 1.35; GS 2.7)
duration: the HYP (1.40) speaks of twelve years of practice for completion

equivalents.note: HYP 1.37 reports that some call siddhāsana vajrāsana; GS 2.12 describes vajrāsana as a distinct posture.
HYP 1.37 reports the name muktāsana for it; GS 2.11 describes muktāsana separately.
HYP 1.37 reports the name guptāsana for it; GS 2.20 describes guptāsana separately.

notes: Brahmānanda (Jyotsnā on HYP 1.36) calls the first form Matsyendra's and the second that of another school. GŚ numbering per the GRETIL e-text (Kuvalayananda–Shukla).
alt_method_summary: One heel pressed at the perineum, the other foot above the genitals, body straight, senses restrained, gaze fixed between the brows; with the lotus one of the two pre-eminent postures, 'opening the door of liberation'.

name: Concentrations yielding the siddhis (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Kṛṣṇa describes, for each of the eighteen powers, a concentration of the mind on a particular aspect of the Lord; summarized here without the individual procedures.

warnings.text: The siddhis are obstacles and a waste of time for one practising the highest yoga; the goal of yoga is not reached by them.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:siddhi-dharanas-bhagavata
checks.note: BhP 11.15.10 (the first concentration, for aṇimā) to 11.15.31 (the powers come to the one practising these dhāraṇās) verified; procedures not reproduced.

name: Recollection of one's virtue
method_summary: Recollecting one's own virtue as unbroken, untorn, liberating, praised by the wise (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)
faith and gladness
access concentration
alt_method_summary: Recollecting one's own virtue as unbroken and untarnished; reaches access.

name: Silent illumination (mozhao)
method_summary: Sitting in silence in which words are forgotten while the mind's illumination remains clear, 'knowing without touching things, illumining without facing objects'; silence and illumination must be kept together.

warnings.text: If illumination loses silence, aggression appears; if silence loses illumination, it becomes murky superfluous dharma (Hongzhi).
Dahui warns that 'silent illumination' taught as becoming cold ash and dead wood cuts off buddha-wisdom.

name: Sīmantonnayana (parting of the hair)
method_summary: A rite in the later months of pregnancy in which the husband parts the wife's hair for her and the child's protection.

queries: local text at the cited refs
evidence: text:sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/gretil_devanAgarI/1_sanskr/6_sastra/4_dharma/smrti/manu-smrti_plain_text.md (GRETIL, Kullūka vulgate numbering; M = Medhātithi numbering)
checks.note: ĀśGS 1.14.1 has 'caturthe garbhamāse sīmantonnayanam'. Note that ĀśGS puts it in the fourth month, which is earlier than the entry's 'later months'; other Gṛhyasūtras differ. Manu names it only generically ('gārbhair homaiḥ', 2.27). This rests on confirmed teaching checks: tea:manusmrti:2.26-28.

name: Siṃhāsana (the lion seat)
method_summary: The ankles placed under the scrotum at the sides of the perineum, crossed (left to the right side, right to the left), the hands on the knees with fingers spread, the mouth open, gazing at the nose-tip (HYP 1.50-52); in the Gheraṇḍa the knees rest on the ground and jālandhara is applied (GS 2.14-15).
signs_of_progress: brings about the three locks (HYP 1.52)
destroys all diseases (GS 2.15)
notes: Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra.

name: Simran (Sant Mat)
method_summary: Mental repetition of the five (or other) names given at initiation, with attention at the eye centre, to still the mind and gather the attention.
notes: The names are confidential and not recorded.

name: The head-vow (śirovrata)
method_summary: A vow whose performance, 'according to rule', qualifies one to be taught the knowledge of brahman (MuU 3.2.10-11); the text does not describe it.
notes: Commentators differ on its nature; not reconstructed here.

queries: prepared segments: MuU 3.2.10-11
checks.note: All 1 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (MuU 3.2.10-11). It rests on 1 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Śītalī ('the cooling')
method_summary: The breath is drawn in with the tongue (protruded), held, and released slowly through the nostrils (HYP 2.57-58; GS 5.74-75).
signs_of_progress: destroys gulma, spleen disorders, fever, bile, hunger, thirst and poisons (HYP 2.58)
no indigestion, phlegm or bile (GS 5.75)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.

name: Sītkārī ('the hissing')
method_summary: The breath is drawn in through the mouth with the sound 'sīt' and released only through the nose (HYP 2.54-56).
signs_of_progress: one becomes a second god of love, honoured by the circle of yoginīs; no hunger, thirst, sleep or sloth; strength of body (HYP 2.54-56)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.

name: Śītkrama bhālabhāti (water through the mouth)
method_summary: Water is sucked in through the mouth with a hissing sound and expelled through the nose (GS 1.59-60).
signs_of_progress: one becomes like the god of love; no old age or fever; the body free; phlegm disorders removed (GS 1.59-60)

name: Recitation of Śiva mantras
method_summary: Recitation of Śiva's five- or six-syllable mantra and of Dakṣiṇāmūrti's mantras (Pañcabrahma; Bhasmajābāla; Dakṣiṇāmūrti).

queries: e-text refs of prc:siva-mantra-japa
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 3 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text. Some rest on teachings whose ref was corrected or only partly confirmed; the content is located, only the numbering changes: tea:pancabrahma-upanisad:11-40 (corrected).

name: Recitation of the thousand names of Śiva (Mahābhārata)
method_summary: Reciting the thousand names of Śiva that Upamanyu taught Kṛṣṇa (MBh 13.14–17).

name: Śivānubhava — shared discourse on experience
method_summary: Devotees gather to speak from and test their experience of Śiva in dialogue, as the śaraṇas did in the Anubhava Maṇṭapa; continued in modern maṭhas as 'śivānubhava' gatherings.

name: The Śivarātri vow
method_summary: Fast and night-long vigil with worship of the liṅga on Śiva's night; the hunter who kept it unknowingly was saved.

queries: rests_on teachings and cited refs located
checks.note: Koṭirudra Saṃhitā not local; web confirms the Śivarātri glory and the hunter Gurudruha in Koṭirudra ch. 40. Stays saṃhitā-level. The teachings it rests on were located; tea:siva-purana:4 has a partial or corrected result (see its check).

name: Śivayoga-samādhi
method_summary: Through inner worship, meditation on Śiva as one's self: the supreme self is contemplated in the haṃsa form with the feeling 'I am He' until attention is undivided; the six centres are contemplated from the base to the brows and Śambhu in the aperture called Kailāsa within the thousand-petalled lotus.

warnings.text: The breath element (meeting of prāṇa and apāna) is done on the teacher's instruction (commentary on 12.6); no method is recorded here.

name: The six essential duties
method_summary: Daily performance of sāmāyika, praise of the twenty-four Jinas, salutation of the teacher, pratikramaṇa, kāyotsarga and a vow of renunciation (pratyākhyāna); for Digambara householders also the six daily duties of worship, attendance on the teacher, study, restraint, austerity and giving.

name: The six equal tastes (Drukpa)
method_summary: Meeting thoughts, afflictions, gods and demons, suffering, illness and death as one taste with the nature of mind, often in solitary or charnel places.

name: Practice of the six perfections
method_summary: Giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation and wisdom practiced together, each 'perfected' by the perfection of wisdom (not apprehending giver, gift or recipient).

name: The six preparatory practices of a lamrim session
method_summary: Cleaning the room and setting up representations of body, speech and mind; arranging offerings; sitting in the proper posture and taking refuge and generating bodhicitta; visualising the field of merit; offering the seven limbs and the maṇḍala; making requests to the lineage.

name: The Six Yogas of Nāropa
method_summary: A graded set of completion-stage practices received after empowerment: inner heat as foundation, then illusory body, dream, clear light, intermediate state and transference (with 'entering another's body'). Summary only: this ontology does not record methods.
prerequisites: the preliminaries
Cakrasaṃvara/Vajravārāhī (or Hevajra) empowerment
generation-stage practice
a qualified guru's oral instruction

warnings.text: If the fourfold application is not known, qualities may turn into faults; without the equal taste of the elements there is no progress; the armour of inner heat is essential.
Given to unfit vessels the instruction breaks the pledge and leads to hell.
The heedless, craving and intoxicated fall to lower realms.

name: The sixteen contemplations of the Contemplation Sūtra

names.name: shiliu guan 十六觀; dingshan (1-13) and sanshan (14-16)

method_summary: Successive visualizations of the setting sun, water and ice, the jewelled ground, trees, ponds, towers, the lotus throne, the images, Amitāyus' body, the two bodhisattvas, one's own birth there, and the nine grades of birth.

warnings.text: Beings' hindrances are heavy, the object subtle and the mind coarse; contemplation is hard to achieve, hence the Buddha urged calling the name.

name: The sixty-four limbs of devotional practice
method_summary: Rūpa's list of practices: the first ten (taking shelter of a guru, initiation and instruction, serving the guru with trust, following the saints, inquiring into true dharma, renouncing enjoyment for Kṛṣṇa, residence at holy places, accepting only what is needed, honouring Ekādaśī, honouring the sacred trees, cows and brāhmaṇas) and ten avoidances (of non-devotees' company, many disciples, great undertakings, many books for argument, miserliness, grief, disrespect of other gods, harming beings, offences in worship and to the name, tolerating blasphemy) are the gateway; then hearing, chanting, remembering, worship, bowing, prayer, service, friendship, self-offering, wearing Vaiṣṇava marks, honouring prasāda, tulasī, festivals and more, ending with the five most potent limbs.
notes: The full list of sixty-four is recalled only in part; verse-by-verse list to be extracted in Phase D.

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 8.7–8, 8.14; 9.22, 9.34: remember the Lord at all times while doing one's duty ('remember me and fight'); with thought (cetas) yoked by the yoga of repeated practice (abhyāsa-yoga), going nowhere else, continually contemplate the supreme Person; remember him constantly, day after day, with thought on nothing else (ananya-cetas) — for such an ever-yoked yogin he is easy to reach; think of him with no other; 'be one whose mind is on me'.
signs_of_progress: the Lord becomes 'easy to attain' (sulabha) for the constantly remembering yogin (8.14)
held by the Lord to be 'the most yoked' (12.2)
'you will dwell in me alone thereafter' (12.8)

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch07-09): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; corrections logged in interpretation_log.jsonl.
Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch10-12): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

alt_method_summary: Remember the Lord at all times, with mind and intellect fixed on him, even while acting (8.7); the yogin who remembers him constantly with undivided mind finds him easily attained (8.14).

Lineage contribution (Bhakti Sūtras; Āḻvārs; Gīta Govinda): worshipping the Lord at all times with one's whole being (NBS 79); forgetting him is supreme anguish (NBS 19); remembrance is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82). Because at death remembrance may fail, the Āḻvārs place the mind at the Lord's feet now and entrust the hour of death to him (Mukundamālā; PAT 4.10.1). The Gīta Govinda is offered to minds that delight in remembering Hari (GG 1.3).

Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: the wise have their thought (citta) on the Lord and their life-breaths gone into him (10.9); the most yoked fix (āveśya) their mind (manas) on him and worship him, ever yoked, with supreme faith (12.2); 'place your mind on me alone, let your understanding (buddhi) enter into me; you will dwell in me thereafter' (12.8) — the first and highest of the graded means of 12.8–11; the devotee dear to him has mind and understanding offered to him (12.14).
notes: Chs. 10–12 contribution, combining extractor A's prc:smarana and extractor B's prc:fixing-manas-and-buddhi-on-the-lord (12.2, 12.8, 12.14), as the ch07-09 merge recorded 'mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ' (8.7) under prc:smarana.

name: Cremation-ground practice (śmaśāna-sādhana)
method_summary: Night worship of Kālī/Tārā by the vīra in the cremation ground, praised in the Karpūrādistotra and practised at Tārāpīṭh. Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: Kaula texts reserve such rites for the initiated vīra and condemn the wilful (Kulārṇava 5.96-105).

equivalents.note: the Pāśupata dwelling in the cremation ground (U17)

name: Dwelling in the cremation ground
method_summary: In the fourth stage he lives in the cremation ground, in the open or at the foot of a tree, not leaving it until the body falls, living on what comes unasked, practising remembrance.
signs_of_progress: union with Rudra (the stated gain)

name: The four applications of mindfulness (Kośa method)
method_summary: After calm is achieved: examining body, feeling, mind and dharmas first by their particular characteristics, then — in the application to dharmas with all as object — seeing them all as impermanent, suffering, empty and non-self; this leads into 'heat'.
prerequisites: calm (śamatha) through aśubhā or ānāpānasmṛti

equivalents.note: Same fourfold object; the Kośa adds the two-characteristic method and places it before the roots of penetration.

name: The four applications of mindfulness (Yogācāra)
method_summary: Mindfulness of body, feeling, mind and dharmas, cultivated for entry into the four truths: body because of badness, feeling as the cause of craving, mind as the basis (of the self-notion), dharmas for non-delusion about defilement and purification.

name: The bathing rite (snātra-pūjā)
method_summary: A congregational re-enactment of Indra's bathing of the newborn Tīrthaṅkara on Mount Meru: a small image is bathed with water and other substances to hymns, recalling the birth-kalyāṇaka.

name: Satyakāma's meditation on the four quarters of brahman
method_summary: Venerate brahman as having four quarters of four parts each — the quarters of space ('shining'), earth, mid-space, sky and ocean ('endless'), fire, sun, moon and lightning ('luminous'), breath, sight, hearing and mind ('having an abode') — as taught to Satyakāma by a bull, fire, a goose and a diver-bird.
notes: Names of the quarters from memory (moderate). Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

queries: prepared segments: ChU 4.5-4.9
checks.note: The four quarter names (marked 'from memory') are confirmed: prakāśavān ChU 4.5.2, anantavān 4.6.3, jyotiṣmān 4.7.3 and āyatanavān 4.8.3. The members of each quarter are as the entry says. All 1 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ChU 4.5-4.9). It rests on 1 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Solitude and contemplation of the body
method_summary: To settle the mind in concentration one withdraws from worldly company and discursive thought into solitude, reflects on the impermanence of loved ones and the impurity of the body to cut attachment, and on the pleasures of the forest.

name: Sopāśraya (sitting with a support)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: The charnel-ground dweller's practice (sosanikaṅga)
method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the charnel-ground dweller's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

name: Daily, seasonal and occasional conduct (spyod lam)
method_summary: Regular sleep, oil massage and moderate exercise; moral conduct and gentle speech as part of health; adjusting diet and activity to the six seasons; not suppressing the natural urges.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic daily regimen
Āyurvedic seasonal regimen
not suppressing urges

name: Dietary regimen by nyepa and season
method_summary: Choosing foods by taste and potency to balance rlung, mkhris pa and bad kan; eating in measure (half food, a quarter drink, a quarter empty); avoiding incompatible foods.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic rules of eating

name: External therapies (bloodletting, moxibustion, compresses, baths)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted: includes bloodletting). 'Rough' and 'gentle' external therapies used when medicines do not suffice — bloodletting for hot and blood disorders, moxibustion for cold and rlung, hot and cold compresses, medicinal and mineral baths, minor surgery. Sites, instruments and procedures are not recorded.

warnings.text: To be applied only by trained physicians after diagnosis; the wrong therapy aggravates the disorder (the texts' general teaching).

equivalents.note: bloodletting in Āyurveda

name: Spanda awareness
method_summary: Being constantly intent on discerning the spanda principle, one attains one's own nature even while awake; spanda is to be grasped in intense states (great anger, joy, perplexity, running) and in the opening (unmeṣa) from which a new thought arises in one absorbed in a single thought (SK 1.21-22, 3.9).

warnings.text: Light, sound, form and taste that arise from the unmeṣa agitate the embodied (read as a caution against distraction by them).
A void, sleep-like absorption is artificial and not the principle (SK 1.12-13).

name: Feigned trembling (spandana)
method_summary: He deliberately shakes his limbs as if struck by a wind-disorder.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Śrāddha
method_summary: Rites of faith for the dead and the ancestors - ekoddiṣṭa for the preta, the sixteen śrāddhas, monthly and annual rites, pārvaṇa for the three ancestors - with feeding of brahmins; they feed the dead on Yama's road and satisfy the ancestors.

queries: rests_on teachings and cited refs located
checks.note: GP 2.5.49-55, 2.5.85-154 located; MkP 30-33 confirmed by colophons (30 naimittikādi-śrāddhakalpa, 31 pārvaṇa-śrāddhakalpa, 32 śrāddhakalpa, 33 kāmya-śrāddha). All teachings it rests on were located in the local e-texts (see their checks).

name: Śrāddha (offering to the ancestors)
method_summary: Qualified brāhmaṇas are invited and fed as the ancestors' representatives, rice-balls (piṇḍa) are offered to the father, grandfather and great-grandfather, and water and sesame given; performed monthly at the new moon and on death-anniversaries and other occasions (MDh 3.122–286).

queries: local text at the cited refs
evidence: text:sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/gretil_devanAgarI/1_sanskr/6_sastra/4_dharma/smrti/manu-smrti_plain_text.md (GRETIL, Kullūka vulgate numbering; M = Medhātithi numbering)
checks.note: MDh 3.122–286 is the śrāddha section; 3.122–123 and 3.267–272 were read. This rests on confirmed teaching checks: tea:manusmrti:3.122-123, tea:manusmrti:3.267-272.

name: Going forth into homelessness (pabbajjā)
method_summary: Leaving household and family, shaving, taking the mendicant's life of alms and wandering under a teacher who leads an order; common to all the śramaṇa orders.
signs_of_progress: honour from the king himself, even for one who was a slave (DN 2)

warnings.text: Going forth does not make a śramaṇa: 'not by shaving', but by equanimity.

name: Public debate among the orders (vāda)
method_summary: Wanderers and teachers questioning one another in debating halls and parks; a teacher's standing rested on answering the standard questions (the other world, fruit of deeds, the perfected one after death).

warnings.text: Some refuse to answer from fear of being cross-examined by clever debaters (the third eel-wriggler).
Praising one's own sect and disparaging another's harms one's own sect.

name: The śrauta sacrifice (in general)
method_summary: Solemn rites performed in three fires (gārhapatya, āhavanīya, dakṣiṇāgni) by priests of the Vedas — hotṛ (Ṛgveda), adhvaryu (Yajurveda), udgātṛ (Sāmaveda) and brahmán (overseer), up to sixteen in the great soma rites — for a patron (yajamāna) and his wife, with oblations, recitations, chants and gifts (dakṣiṇā).
prerequisites: initiated householder, married, who has established the fires

name: Hearing the scriptures (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Study of scripture and its right interpretation under a teacher. In Dvaita: hearing the true scriptures (Vedas, Mahābhārata, Pañcarātra, Purāṇas) with Madhva's commentaries so as to know Viṣṇu's supremacy, the five differences and gradation; the first principal means to knowledge, never to be curtailed.
stage: all (the lowest adhikārin qualifies by study and devotion)
prerequisites: devotion to Viṣṇu
a qualified teacher
eligibility by class and qualities (adhikāra)
sādhana-catuṣṭaya
a teacher (śrotriya, brahmaniṣṭha)

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch13-15): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

queries: prepared segments: BĀU 2.4.5, BĀU 4.5.6
checks.note: All 2 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (BĀU 2.4.5; BĀU 4.5.6). It rests on 2 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

alt_method_summary: Systematic study of the Upaniṣads (with the Gītā and Brahma Sūtras) under a qualified teacher, determining by the six marks of purport that their meaning is the non-dual Brahman; for the Vivaraṇa the principal means, for one of sharp understanding sufficient by itself.
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be seen, heard, reflected upon and meditated upon'; hearing is the second of the four verbs (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).

Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Those who do not know the self by meditation, sāṃkhya or the yoga of action worship having heard from others; holding to what they have heard, they too cross beyond death (13.26).
signs_of_progress: doubt about what scripture teaches is removed (pramāṇa-saṃśaya)

name: Hearing the Lord's names, qualities and deeds (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Listening to the names, qualities, deeds and stories of the Lord — from the Bhāgavata and the epics, from devotees and in kathā — with love. First of the Bhāgavata's nine forms (BhP 7.5.23); with singing, a means to devotion even for those living in the world (NBS 37); Garga defines devotion as attachment to hearing his stories (NBS 17); the love of Rāma's stories is the second of the nine in the Rāmāyaṇa tradition.
stage: all; the first of the nine
signs_of_progress: the inauspicious in the heart is shaken off and steady devotion arises (BhP 1.2.16–21)

warnings.text: Stories of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies are not to be listened to.

equivalents.note: hearing the Purāṇa recited is the chief form of bhakti-hearing
Vedāntic śravaṇa is study of the Upaniṣads for knowledge of Brahman; bhakti śravaṇa is hearing of the Lord's deeds and names out of love — same word, different object and purpose

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar in the tradition's list: Parīkṣit (cpt:nine-exemplars-of-devotion).

name: Offering to the deity's attendants (śrībhūtabali)
method_summary: Offering of cooked rice on the stones of the deity's attendant beings and guardians placed around the shrine, with the festival image carried in procession.

name: Contemplation of the body as the Śrīcakra
method_summary: The body's openings, channels, winds and faculties contemplated as the enclosures and deities of the Śrīcakra; worship as contemplation of non-difference (Bhāvanā; Tripurā).

queries: e-text refs of prc:sricakra-bhavana
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 3 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text. Some rest on teachings whose ref was corrected or only partly confirmed; the content is located, only the numbering changes: tea:bhavana-upanisad:1-5 (partially-confirmed).

name: Worship of the nine enclosures of the Śrīcakra (navāvaraṇa-pūjā)
method_summary: After the preliminaries (Gaṇapati worship, purification, placements on the body, preparation of the special water), the Goddess is invoked into the central point and the deities of the nine enclosures are worshipped from the outer square inward — each enclosure with its presiding goddess, class of yoginīs, attendant deities and mudrā — followed by the sixty-four services, libations into the bindu, japa and the offering of all to the Goddess. The Yoginīhṛdaya calls this cakra-worship 'aparā', performed even by Śiva; the Samaya school performs it only inwardly. (Summary; no mantras recorded.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.
The Kaula worship is to be done in secret; making it public leads to hell.
Outer worship on a physical support is rejected by the Samayins, who worship only in the heart-space.

equivalents.note: outer and inner forms of the same worship

name: Śrīvidyā initiation (śāktī, śāmbhavī, māntrī)
method_summary: The guru, after his own worship, purifies the blindfolded disciple with the special water, contemplates the red and white feet on his head and a wave of light burning away his bonds, bathes him from a consecrated vessel, places the letters on his body, whispers the Bālā mantra and then the chosen mantra, gives his own pādukā and a name ending in '-ānandanātha', teaches the rules of conduct and makes the disciple his own self (PKS 1.34-43). Summary only.

name: Fire offering in Śrīvidyā
method_summary: The fire rite: preparation of the fire and offerings to the Goddess and her retinue. Taught in section 9 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

equivalents.note: tantric fire offering in Śākta and Buddhist forms

notes: U49 contribution: cross-family equivalents only (other fields copied unchanged).

name: Japa of the Śrīvidyā mantra
method_summary: Repetition of the fifteen- or sixteen-syllable mantra received at initiation, with attention to its subtle final phases and its meanings; the Varivasyārahasya insists that japa without knowledge of meaning bears no fruit. (No syllables recorded.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

warnings.text: Recitation without knowing the meaning bears no fruit and may do harm.
Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.

name: The ten mudrās of Śrīvidyā worship
method_summary: Ten hand-seals shown in the worship of the Śrīcakra, one for each enclosure (sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī to sarvayoni) and the tenth, trikhaṇḍā. (Names only; forms not described.)

name: The daily routine of the Śrīvidyā initiate
method_summary: Rising before dawn, contemplating the guru's feet in the crown with nectar flooding the body, meditating on Gaṇapati in the heart, the morning ablutions and offerings, libations, and the day's worship (PKS 2.2); constant holding of the vidyā and immersion in Śiva-hood (PKS 1.17-18).

name: Placements on the body (nyāsa) in Śrīvidyā
method_summary: Placing of mantras and deities on the body before worship: the purification of the hands, the eight goddesses of speech on head, forehead, brows, throat, heart, navel, genitals and base, the mātṛkā, the great sixfold placement and others, by which the worshipper becomes the deity's body. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Keeping the initiate's conduct (samaya)
method_summary: Observing the rules of the Kalpasūtra: no censure of other schools or persons, secrecy, constant remembrance of the vidyā, avoidance of the six passions, unsanctioned violence and theft, one guru, non-possessiveness, action without regard to fruit, fearlessness; outwardly Śaiva and among people Vaiṣṇava (Kaula Upaniṣad).

warnings.text: Those without the succession of teachers, proud of mere knowledge, are harmed by the mantra's rays through their breach of the samaya.

name: Feigned amorous gestures (śṛṅgāraṇa)
method_summary: Standing at a distance from a group of women, he looks at one young woman and makes signs of desire such as arranging his hair, so as to be called unchaste; the act is a pretence.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Śruta Pañcamī (Digambara)
method_summary: The Digambara festival of scripture on the fifth of bright Jyeṣṭha, commemorating the completion of the Ṣaṭkhaṇḍāgama by Puṣpadanta and Bhūtabali and the saṅgha's worship of the book.

equivalents.note: the Śvetāmbara scripture festival on another date

name: Sthānakalpanā: positing places (breath, body, outer)
method_summary: The lowest āṇava support: positing the divine in 'places' - in the breath and its time-cycles (TĀ 6), in the body, and in outer supports such as the liṅga or maṇḍala.

name: Veneration of sanctified places
method_summary: Visiting and worshipping at places the incarnations visited and venerating objects associated with them.

name: Sthirasukha (the steady-and-comfortable)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Recitation of the tradition's hymns
method_summary: Daily recitation of Madhva's Dvādaśastotra and Narasiṃhanakhastuti and Trivikrama's Vāyustuti (framed by the Narasiṃha verses); in the Rāghavendra tradition, the Rāghavendra hymn.
alt_method_summary: Rāmānandī and wider north Indian practice: daily recitation of the Hanumān Cālīsā and passages of the Mānas.

name: Recitation of hymns (Bhaktāmara, Uvasaggaharaṃ, Kalyāṇamandira and others)
method_summary: Daily or occasional recitation of hymns to the Jinas, especially the Bhaktāmara (44/48 verses) and the protective Uvasaggaharaṃ to Pārśva; a later tradition attaches a mantra, yantra and benefit to each Bhaktāmara verse.

name: Worship at stūpas (caitya)
method_summary: Offerings and honour at shrines holding relics; merit arises from the renunciation itself even though no one receives it (Kośa); the Dharmaguptakas held such offerings to bring great fruit.

warnings.text: Destroying a stūpa is one of the acts resembling the deadly acts.

name: Holding the mind on the auspicious support (VP 6.7)
method_summary: With breath and senses mastered, fix the mind on Viṣṇu's form as the ground of all powers, simplifying it stage by stage, until dhyāna (a single continuous flow) and samādhi (grasping the object's own nature free of imagination) arise.

queries: rests_on teachings and cited refs located
checks.note: All teachings it rests on were located in the local e-texts (see their checks).

name: Suizen (blowing Zen)
method_summary: Playing the shakuhachi as meditation by Fuke-school komusō.

name: Sukhāsana (the comfortable seat)
method_summary: A comfortable seated posture: in the Śivasaṃhitā the name is given to svastika (ŚS 3.97); the Gheraṇḍa has sagarbha breath-control done 'seated in sukhāsana' (GS 5.49); the Darśana and Triśikhibrāhmaṇa Upaniṣads list sukha among their postures.

name: Sukhasiddhi's six dharmas (Shangpa)
method_summary: Instructions from Sukhasiddhi transmitted in the Shangpa alongside Niguma's; summary only.

name: Śukla-dhyāna (pure meditation)
method_summary: Four stages: scripture-based meditation shifting among aspects, words and activities; fixed on one aspect without shifting (which yields omniscience); the omniscient's meditation in which only subtle activity remains; and the stopping of all activity before liberation.
prerequisites: best bodily frame
knowledge of the Pūrvas (first two stages)

warnings.text: The tradition holds that the first two stages require the best bodily frame and knowledge of the lost Pūrvas, and so are not attainable in the present age in Bharata.

name: The Sunlun method
method_summary: A sitting begins with strong, deliberate breathing to build concentration, after which the breathing is released and attention is fixed on the touch sensation at the nostrils and then on all bodily sensations, especially pain, which is watched without moving until it dissolves — summary only.

warnings.text: Taught under a teacher's supervision; the forceful breathing is not to be improvised (general statement; the tradition's own wording not available here).

notes: No breath counts or durations recorded.

name: Dwelling in emptiness (suññatāvihāra)
method_summary: Attending to a single perception (forest, earth, the formless spheres, the signless), seeing what is absent as empty and what remains as present, until the mind is freed (MN 121); dwelling in emptiness internally by not attending to signs (MN 122).

name: Dwelling in an empty house or cave
method_summary: In the stage of conquest he lives in an empty house or cave free from distraction, constantly with the god, senses conquered, studying and meditating.
duration: six months of constant yoga are named for the powers to arise (PS 5.12-13)
signs_of_progress: powers such as distant sight arise gradually

name: Worship of the deity in a pot of liquor (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas set up a pot of liquor and worship the deity placed in it.

name: The Śūraṅgama mantra
method_summary: Reciting the long Śūraṅgama mantra (in Chinese monasteries in the morning service); the sūtra's altar-rite for the latter age.

name: Surat-śabd yoga (the yoga of the sound current)
method_summary: Given only at initiation by a living master: the attention is withdrawn from the body and gathered at the eye centre by simran, held there by dhyān of the master's form, and joined to the inner sound (bhajan), which draws the soul up through the inner regions; practised daily (two and a half hours in the Beas line) with the vows.
prerequisites: initiation (nām-dān)
the four vows
signs_of_progress: attention gathering at the eye centre
inner light (stars, moon, sun) and the radiant form of the master
sounds of the regions (bell and conch first)

warnings.text: Without a living master and initiation the practice is not to be attempted; the lower centres and kuṇḍalinī are not to be worked on.
Inner lights and sounds are not to be sought for their own sake or spoken of; the disciple should not display powers.

equivalents.note: Both are absorption in the inner sound; surat-śabd yoga adds the master's form, the names and the regional cosmology.

name: Practice of the Sūrimantra
method_summary: A Śvetāmbara ācārya, receiving the secret Sūrimantra from his teacher at installation, periodically practises it in its five sections with fasting, silence and worship of the presiding deities; the practice is transmitted orally.
notes: Restricted and secret: summary only.

name: Sūryabhedana ('piercing the sun')
method_summary: RESTRICTED (extreme retention) — summary only: breath drawn in slowly through the right (sun) channel, held with the locks, and released through the left (HYP 2.48-50; GS 5.59-69). The texts set the limit of the retention at an extreme point, which is not reproduced. The Gheraṇḍa sets the practice in the context of the ten breaths and their seats (GS 5.61-65).
signs_of_progress: cleanses the skull, destroys disorders of wind and of worms (HYP 2.50)
destroys old age and death, awakens kuṇḍalinī, increases the bodily fire (GS 5.68-69)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
Breath-control is to be practised by the path the guru teaches, once posture is firm and the diet wholesome and moderate.

name: Śuṣka-basti (the dry basti)
method_summary: Done on the ground in paścimatāna, moving (the belly) slowly and contracting and expanding the anus with aśvinī mudrā (GS 1.48-49).
signs_of_progress: no bowel disorders; increased digestive fire; destroys āmavāta (GS 1.49)

name: Susokukan (counting the breath)
method_summary: Counting exhalations from one to ten as a beginner's method of settling in zazen.
notes: Common in modern Zen instruction; classical sources not identified in this pass.

name: Sūtra and dhāraṇī chanting in Zen liturgy
method_summary: Daily chanting of the Heart Sūtra, dhāraṇīs (e.g. the Great Compassion Dhāraṇī), the Sandōkai and Hōkyō zanmai (Sōtō), Hakuin's Zazen wasan (Rinzai), and dedications of merit; Ōbaku chants in Ming Chinese pronunciation.

name: Copying and honoring sūtras
method_summary: Writing out the sūtra and honoring the book with flowers, incense, banners and parasols; the book is kept as a shrine.

name: Reciting, memorizing and teaching sūtras
method_summary: Taking up, keeping, reading, reciting, explaining and teaching a sūtra or even one four-line verse of it.

name: Worship of married women (suvāsinī-pūjā)
method_summary: Married women are honoured as the Goddess, who 'is pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs' (LSN 178).

name: Performing one's own dharma (svadharma)
method_summary: Look to one's own dharma and do not waver: for a kṣatriya, fight a battle that accords with dharma (2.31); perform one's own dharma even if imperfectly rather than another's well (3.35).

warnings.text: Abandoning one's own dharma incurs sin and disgrace (2.33–36); another's dharma brings fear (3.35).

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Study of the scriptures of liberation or repetition of the praṇava and the other purifying syllables (YBh 2.1, 2.32); from it, union with the chosen deity (YS 2.44), and gods, sages and perfected ones come into view (YBh 2.44).

name: Performing one's own duty (svakarma)

name: Support in the knowledge of dream and sleep (YS 1.38)
method_summary: The mind taking on the form of the knowledge of dream or sleep as its support gains a footing of steadiness (YBh 1.38).

name: Svara practice: attending to the flow of breath in the nostrils (svarodaya)
method_summary: The practice of the Śiva Svarodaya: noting which channel the breath is flowing in — iḍā (left, moon), piṅgalā (right, sun) or suṣumnā (both) — as the flows alternate through the day, and timing actions accordingly: steady and auspicious acts when the moon flows, active and harsh acts when the sun flows, and only meditation and yoga when the suṣumnā flows, since worldly acts then fail. The text treats this knowledge as most secret and also teaches ways of changing the flow (not detailed here).
notes: Verse numbers of the Śiva Svarodaya not recalled; sources cite U28's topic-level teachings.

name: Discerning the elements in the breath (tattva in svara)
method_summary: Within each nostril-flow the five elements (earth, water, fire, air, space) arise in turn; the Śiva Svarodaya teaches how to recognise the element present by the length, direction, colour and taste (and shape) of the breath, and uses this knowledge, with the flows, to foretell outcomes, illness and the approach of death.
notes: Specific lengths and correspondences are not reproduced; recalled only in outline.

name: Svastikāsana (the auspicious-mark seat)
method_summary: Both soles placed between the knees and thighs, sitting with the body straight (HYP 1.19; GS 2.13; ŚS 3.95). The Śivasaṃhitā calls it the comfortable posture (sukhāsana).
signs_of_progress: no disease enters the body and the breath is mastered (ŚS 3.96)

equivalents.note: ŚS 3.97 calls svastika sukhāsana; the Darśana and Triśikhibrāhmaṇa list sukha separately.

notes: Yoga Yājñavalkya ch. 3 is recalled (low confidence) to describe eight postures: svastika, gomukha, padma, vīra, siṃha, bhadra, mukta, mayūra.

name: Dwelling on one's own nature (svasvarūpānusandhāna) as devotion
method_summary: Devotion understood as continuous attention to one's own true nature (VC 31), the chief among the means to liberation.

name: The yoga of the Śvetāśvatara (posture, breath, place)
method_summary: Hold the body steady with chest, neck and head erect; draw the senses with the mind into the heart; restrain the breaths, with movements controlled, and breathe out gently through the nose when the breath is diminished; hold the mind attentively like a chariot yoked to unruly horses; practise in a level, clean place free of pebbles, fire, sand, noise and damp, pleasing to the mind and sheltered from wind.
prerequisites: the invocations of Savitṛ to yoke the mind (ŚU 2.1-7)
signs_of_progress: forms like fog, smoke, sun, wind, fire, fireflies, lightning, crystal and moon precede brahman's manifestation; lightness, health, freedom from craving, clear complexion, pleasant voice and smell, scant excreta (ŚU 2.11-13)

warnings.text: The place must be free of disturbances (pebbles, fire, sand, noise, water-places) and not offend the eye (ŚU 2.10).
The breath is to be let out gently through the nose when diminished (ŚU 2.9).

name: Worship of Śyāmā (Mantriṇī)
method_summary: Worship of Śyāmā/Rājamātaṅgī, Lalitā's minister, with her own cakra and enclosures. Taught in section 6 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: Singing Śyāmā-saṅgīt
method_summary: Devotional singing of the songs of Rāmprasād, Kamalākānta and their successors to Kālī and Umā, alone or in gatherings, as a way of relating to the Mother.

name: Śyena (a sorcery rite)
method_summary: A rite the Veda states as the means for one who wishes to harm an enemy. Mīmāṃsā records it only to show that the Veda does not enjoin harming: the rite is described as a means, not as a duty.

warnings.text: The Śyena and similar rites (Vajra, Iṣu) are harmful (anartha): their aim is violence, violence is prohibited, and they lead to sin (pratyavāya); they are not dharma.

notes: Summary only (abhicāra rite).

name: Taḍāgī mudrā ('the tank')
method_summary: In paścimatāna, the belly is drawn back and hollowed so that it is shaped like a tank (GS 3.61).
signs_of_progress: destroys old age and death (GS 3.61)

name: Offering all conduct to the Lord (tad-arpitākhilācāratā)
method_summary: Dedicating every action to the Lord (Nārada's own definition of devotion, NBS 19); having so offered all conduct, even desire, anger and pride are to be turned toward him alone (NBS 65); until love is attained, action continues with its fruit given up (NBS 62).

equivalents.note: the Gītā's offering of all acts to the Lord (BhG 9.27)

name: Taking adversity as the path
method_summary: When harmed or in bad circumstances, blaming self-cherishing rather than others, contemplating the harmer's kindness as a teacher of patience, seeing the situation as empty and like a dream, and doing the four practices — so that illness, enemies and loss become aids to bodhicitta.

name: Takuhatsu (alms round)
method_summary: Mendicant alms-rounds in which monks receive offerings, practising humility and giving donors merit.

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: In kriyā-yoga and as an observance (niyama): the means without which the impurity variegated by karma, afflictions and tendencies cannot be broken up (YBh 2.1). Vyāsa: bearing the pairs of opposites — hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, silence of wood and of gesture; he names vows (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, sāṃtapana and the like) without describing them (YBh 2.32). It destroys impurity and the covering, and perfection of body and senses follows (YS 2.43). Fasting-type vows are named only; no method is recorded here.

Lopāmudrā's complaint that many autumns of toil wear away the body, and the resolution that tapas and married life together bear fruit, are the Saṃhitā's own counterweight to one-sided austerity.
Austerity is to be done 'according to one's capacity' (śaktitaḥ).
Austerity done for worldly or heavenly reward is 'poison' or 'venom'; only austerity with understanding and longing for release counts.
Austerity of the ignorant (bāla-tapas) binds divine rebirth, not liberation.
Rites and austerities performed without knowing the imperishable come to an end (BAU 3.8.10).

Summary only: the fasting vows the bhāṣya names (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, sāntapana) are not described here.

Ascetic exertion that 'heats' the practitioner: by it the ancients reached heaven, the seers were born, the student fills the worlds; the Vrātya stands upright for a year; the unheated cannot attain soma.

Jain contribution: six external austerities (fasting, eating less, limiting alms, giving up tasty food, lonely lodging, bodily hardship) and six internal (expiation, humility, service, study, abandonment, meditation), practised according to one's capacity to stop and shed karma.

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): Bhṛgu seeks brahman by tapas (TU 3.1-6); a year of austerity, celibacy and faith before questioning (PrU 1.2); the self is found by truth and austerity (MuU 3.1.5; ŚU 1.15); austerity as a branch of dharma (ChU 2.23.1).

Sacrifice of austerity is one of the kinds of sacrifice (4.28); many purified by the austerity of knowledge reached the Lord's state (4.10); the Lord is the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities (5.29); the yogin is held greater than the ascetics (6.46).
Enduring pain and harming none (Kuṟaḷ ch. 27).

name: Seeking brahman by tapas (Bhṛgu and Varuṇa, Taittirīya 3)
method_summary: Varuṇa gives Bhṛgu the mark of brahman (that from which beings are born, live and into which they enter) and tells him to seek it by tapas; Bhṛgu performs tapas and then knows the next identification; the text does not say what the tapas consists of.

name: Guru yoga of Tapihritsa
method_summary: Visualizing Tapihritsa, naked and crystal-clear, as the embodiment of the lineage, supplicating and uniting one's mind with his.
notes: Optional (Bön).

name: Wearing Viṣṇu's heated emblems (tapta-mudrā-dhāraṇa)
method_summary: Summary only: the Mādhva tradition marks the body with Viṣṇu's discus and conch emblems, either heated or in clay; heated emblems are received at set times of the year and at the thread ceremony in the presence of the maṭha's head.

name: Tāraka-yoga
method_summary: Meditation on the 'crossing' light between the brows through the three targets and the voids, proceeding from tāraka with form to tāraka without form and to the mind-less (amanaska) state.
prerequisites: renouncer endowed with the six qualities (Advayatāraka)

name: Discriminating the principles (Sāṃkhya in the Mokṣadharma)
method_summary: Enumerating the twenty-four principles of prakṛti and knowing the twenty-fifth as other than them, the knower awakens and becomes alone (MBh 12.294); knowing the faults of body, senses and guṇas, the Sāṃkhya follower is freed (12.290).

name: Repeated practice of the principles (tattvābhyāsa)
method_summary: After hearing the principles (manifest, unmanifest, knower) from scripture and teacher and establishing them by reasoning, one contemplates them repeatedly — long, reverently and without interruption — discriminating puruṣa from each principle and renouncing identification with each ('not this, not this'), until the knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' arises.
prerequisites: hearing and reasoning about the twenty-five principles; dispassion
duration: long and uninterrupted; Vācaspati speaks of many births of practice
signs_of_progress: the complete, pure, single knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' (SK 64); prakṛti seen as by a spectator, having ceased (SK 65–66)

warnings.text: Liberation is not attained by mere hearing, because beginningless latent tendencies are strong.
Dispassion without discrimination leads only to absorption in prakṛti, from which one rises again.

equivalents.note: long uninterrupted contemplation after hearing and reflection, as in Advaita's nididhyāsana; content and goal differ (discrimination vs identity)

name: The triple-robe wearer's practice (tecivarikaṅga)
method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the triple-robe wearer's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

name: Gaining the fiery power (tejoleśyā)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted: severe fasting with exposure). In the Jain account Mahāvīra, at Gosāla's request, described a course of extreme fasting and exposure to the sun by which the fiery power is gained; Gosāla gained it after leaving him.

warnings.text: In the narrative the power is used to kill two monks and, turned on Mahāvīra, returns and destroys Gosāla himself within seven days.
It left Mahāvīra ill for six months.

notes: No steps, quantities or durations are recorded, by design.

name: Temple-building rites from ploughing to installation (karṣaṇādi)
method_summary: Examination and taking possession of the site, ploughing (karṣaṇa), sprouting seeds, laying out the ground-plan (vāstu-maṇḍala), offerings to the site deities, deposit of the foundation (garbhanyāsa), and rites at each stage of construction up to installation; the Kāmika's Pūrvabhāga devotes many chapters to them.
notes: U58 owns Vāstu/Śilpa; here the ritual frame.

name: The ten-day Vipassana course (Goenka)
method_summary: A residential course in noble silence: taking refuge and the five precepts, surrender to the teacher and the technique; mindfulness of respiration at the nostrils for three and a half days; body scanning from the fourth day; loving-kindness on the last day; recorded evening discourses; given free on donation.
duration: ten full days

name: The ten practices of the Dharma (daśa dharmacaritāni)
method_summary: Copying the teaching, worshipping it, giving it, listening to it, reading it, memorizing it, explaining it, reciting it, reflecting on it and meditating on it — an immeasurable mass of merit.
alt_method_summary: Atiśa's advice to practise day and night the ten dharma practices taught by Maitreya (copying, offering, giving, listening, reading, memorising, explaining, reciting, reflecting, meditating).
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).

name: The ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana)
method_summary: Earth, water, fire, wind, blue, yellow, red, white, space and consciousness contemplated as all-pervading; the first eight in the fourth dhyāna with desire-realm objects, the last two formless.
