Kośa: the formless totality of space; Visuddhimagga: the limited-space kasiṇa.

name: Ten methods of practising no-mind
method_summary: Ten alternative methods (awareness, resting, extinguishing mind or objects or both, keeping both, whole substance, whole function, substance-is-function, transcending both) of which one suffices, chosen by affinity.

name: The three gifts (sopādhi, nirupādhi, sahaja dāna)
method_summary: Giving with a purpose, giving without a purpose, and innate (natural) giving — the last three sub-sthalas of the bhakta-sthala; skill in pure, innate giving marks the passage to māheśvara.

name: The three integrations (Shangpa)
method_summary: In every activity the guru, the deity and illusion are carried onto the path.

name: The three meritorious acts (sanfu)
method_summary: Filial care, service of teachers, non-killing and the ten good deeds; taking refuge, keeping the precepts and deportment; arousing bodhicitta, believing in cause and effect, reciting the Mahāyāna sūtras and encouraging others — 'the right cause of the pure acts of the buddhas of the three times'.

name: Contemplation of the three natures
method_summary: The dependent is entered first as the absence of duality, then as mere imagination with non-existent duality, then the perfected as the being of that absence; the magical elephant is the model: seeing no elephant, the shape vanishing and the wood seen, all at once — understanding, abandonment and attainment of the three natures are simultaneous.

name: Keeping the three supports of life
method_summary: Right use of food, sleep and continence, by which the body is upheld as a house by its pillars.

name: The three concentrations (doors of liberation)
method_summary: Concentration on emptiness (aspects empty, non-self), on the wishless (the remaining aspects of suffering, origin and path) and on the signless (the four aspects of cessation).

name: Hearing, reflection and meditation
method_summary: Wisdom from hearing grasps the meaning of scripture; wisdom from reflection discerns definitive from provisional meaning; wisdom from meditation cultivates what has been ascertained as real — so that doubt is removed and correct knowledge arises.

name: The three-year retreat
method_summary: A closed group retreat of three years and about six weeks following a set curriculum (preliminaries, Mahāmudrā, six yogas of Nāropa and Niguma, deity practices), systematized by Jamgön Kongtrul and spread internationally by Kalu Rinpoche.
duration: three years and about six weeks

name: The three-year retreat in Kongtrul's system
method_summary: A closed retreat of about three years under strict rules, in which retreatants complete the preliminaries and then the practices of several lineages in sequence (among them the Shangpa instructions and the Kālacakra six-branch yoga), as set out in Kongtrul's retreat manual.
duration: about three years (three years and three fortnights)
notes: Duration formula and curriculum order recalled with low confidence.

name: Austerity of body, speech and mind
method_summary: Bodily austerity: worship of gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy, non-harm. Verbal: speech that does not agitate, true, pleasant and beneficial, and recitation of scripture. Mental: serenity, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, purity of being — practised with faith and without desire for fruit (17.14–17).

warnings.text: Terrible austerities not enjoined by scripture, done with hypocrisy and egoism, tormenting the elements of the body and the Lord within, are demonic.
Austerity done with foolish obstinacy, by torturing oneself or to harm another, is tāmasic.

name: Pilgrimage (tīrthāṭana)
method_summary: Visiting sacred places: the Goddess's seats listed in the Devī Gītā, and pilgrimage among the Uddhava Gītā's niyamas; the Avadhūta Gītā's apology notes that pilgrimage presupposes a limit to the all-pervading.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by prc:tirthatana
checks.note: DBhP 7.38.1-7 (seats of the Goddess), BhP 11.19.34 (tīrthāṭana among the niyamas) and Avadhūta Gītā 8.1 ('tvadyātrayā vyāpakatā hatā te') verified.

name: Pilgrimage to tīrthas
method_summary: Journeying to holy places, bathing, worship, gifts and śrāddha there; seven cities give liberation; the inner meaning is purity of mind and the company of the holy, who themselves make places holy.

warnings.text: The greedy, cruel and hypocritical remain impure though they bathe in every tīrtha.

queries: rests_on teachings and cited refs located
checks.note: SkP 4.1.6.28-45 (4.1.6.34 the greedy remain impure), GP 2.38.5-6, BhP 1.13.10 located. All teachings it rests on were located in the local e-texts (see their checks).

alt_method_summary: The Āraṇyakaparvan's pilgrimage to the tīrthas; Vidura's inner reading: the self is a river whose fords are sacred, whose water is truth, banks steadfastness and waves self-restraint — bathing in it purifies (MBh 5.40.19).
Vārkarī: pilgrimage is valued, but the saints' company and Viṭṭhala's feet are the true tīrtha (Nāmdev's Tīrthāvaḷī).
notes: U05's contribution; the Āraṇyaka's tīrtha lists are not itemized here.

name: Tirumūlar's eightfold yoga
method_summary: The eight limbs (iyamam, niyamam, ātaṉam, pirāṇāyāmam, pirattiyākāram, tāraṇai, tiyāṉam, camāti — TM 552), commended by the Siddhar poets (Kaṭuveḷi 31).
notes: U22 contribution (lineage) to U18's entry.
alt_method_summary: Tirumūlar's eight limbs — restraints, observances, posture, breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, absorption — taught to preserve the body as the vessel of realization and to reach Śiva within; summary only.

warnings.text: Breath retention and advanced practices are to be learned only from a guru (general teaching of the text; specific verses not recorded here).

name: Recitation and contemplation of the tirumantra
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āḻvārs): Tirumaṅkai, given the eight-syllable mantra by the Lord himself (the tradition's account), sang that he had searched and found the name 'Nārāyaṇa', which gives every good (PTM 1.1).
alt_method_summary: Repetition of 'oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', received at initiation, with contemplation of its meaning: the soul belongs to the Lord alone, not to itself, and seeks only his service.

name: Singing the Tirumuṟai (paṇṇicai)
method_summary: Singing the Tēvāram and other Tirumuṟai hymns in their melodic modes during temple worship and at home; the ōtuvār's office.

name: Awakening the Lord at dawn (tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci)
method_summary: At dawn the Lord in the temple is roused with song — the sun has risen, the gods and sages wait at his door — and the singer asks to be made servant of his servants. Toṇṭaraṭippoṭi's ten verses are sung daily at Śrīraṅgam and other Śrīvaiṣṇava temples.
notes: Cf. the Sanskrit suprabhātam (src:venkatesa-suprabhatam, U14) and the Śaiva Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci of Māṇikkavācakar (U18).

name: The Mārkaḻi vow of the Tiruppāvai (pāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi the girls rise before dawn, wake one another, bathe, and go singing the Lord's names to his house; during the vow they take no ghee or milk, wear no kohl or flowers, do nothing forbidden, speak no evil, and give alms; they worship with pure flowers, singing and meditation. In the tradition the Tiruppāvai's thirty verses are sung daily throughout Mārkaḻi, one for each day, in temples and homes.
duration: the month of Mārkaḻi (mid-December to mid-January)

equivalents.note: the Śaiva Mārkaḻi dawn vow of Māṇikkavācakar's Tiruvempāvai

notes: The dietary abstentions are a vow of restraint, not a prolonged fast.

name: Daily home worship of the Lord (tiruvārādhanam)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord's image (arcā) at home each day, with purification, meditation on the teachers, offerings of water, flowers, food, recitation and prostration, done as service and not for any fruit.

name: The Mārkaḻi dawn vow (Tiruvempāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi, rising before dawn, bathing and singing the Tiruvempāvai and Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci.

name: Worship of the Nityā of the lunar day
method_summary: Worship of the Nityā presiding over the current lunar day, the Nityās being the phases of time (Tantrarāja; Bhāvanā Upaniṣad). Summary only.

name: Enduring the sense-contacts (titikṣā)
method_summary: The contacts of the senses give cold and heat, pleasure and pain; they come and go and are impermanent — endure them (2.14). The one they do not disturb is fit for immortality (2.15).
prerequisites: seeing that the sense-contacts are impermanent (2.14)
signs_of_progress: not being disturbed by them; sameness in pleasure and pain (2.15)

name: Direct crossing (thod rgal)
method_summary: The instruction-series practice of spontaneous presence: relying on key points of body and gaze given orally by the master, the lamps bring forth the four visions, culminating in the exhaustion of phenomena and possibly the rainbow body. Summary only.
prerequisites: stability in cutting through
oral instruction from a qualified master

warnings.text: Taught only to those stable in cutting through and only orally by a qualified master; practised without that foundation the visions become mere experiences.
The Heart-essence tantras restrict the instruction to fit vessels; teaching it to the unfit brings harm to both.

notes: RESTRICTED: no method recorded.

name: Tokkaṇam (Siddha therapeutic massage)
method_summary: Therapeutic massage and manipulation, one of the external treatments of Siddha medicine, practised in several named kinds. No techniques recorded.

name: Sending and taking (gtong len)
method_summary: Visualising the suffering of others (beginning with one's own future suffering) and its causes, one takes it in on the in-breath, dissolving it into one's own self-cherishing; on the out-breath one sends one's body, happiness and virtue to them, imagining them satisfied; applied to the three objects and three poisons, and used when suffering or witnessing suffering.
stage: intermediate (after love and compassion are developed)
prerequisites: equalizing self and other
love and compassion

warnings.text: Begin the sequence of taking with yourself.
Do the taking secretly, without display (Eight Verses 7: 'secretly take upon myself').

equivalents.note: tonglen is the meditative technique of the exchange

name: Torma offering
method_summary: Offering sculpted ritual cakes to deities, protectors and spirits, or using them as supports of the deity.

name: Transference of consciousness (and entering another body)
method_summary: Summary only: at the time of death consciousness is sent upward with deity and seed syllable into the heart of the deity and guru, or into another body (Tilopa, from Sukhasiddhi). No method details recorded.
prerequisites: consecration
guru's oral instruction

warnings.text: Taught only as oral instruction within the six dharmas; the text itself gives it to one prepared by the preceding yogas.

name: Trāṭaka (the fixed gaze)
method_summary: With steady eyes and concentrated mind, one gazes without blinking at a small target until tears fall (HYP 2.31; GS 1.53). Listed by the texts among the six acts, it is also a practice of concentration: in the Gheraṇḍa it leads to śāmbhavī (GS 1.54).
signs_of_progress: frees from eye diseases and bars sloth (HYP 2.32)
śāmbhavī arises; no eye disease; divine sight (GS 1.54)

warnings.text: To be guarded as carefully as a golden casket.
One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.

notes: The texts name only a 'small target' (sūkṣma-lakṣya); gazing at a candle flame is later usage (recent teachers).

name: Cutting through (khregs chod)
method_summary: After direct introduction, resting in fresh, unfabricated awareness, recognizing whatever arises as its display so that it self-liberates, without meditating on an object; view, meditation and conduct are 'left as they are'; the practice of primordial purity.
prerequisites: preliminaries
direct introduction by a qualified master
signs_of_progress: thoughts self-liberate as they arise
no division between session and post-session

warnings.text: Mistaking a blank, indifferent state (the all-base) or meditative experiences for awareness is the chief deviation.

name: Tripuṇḍra (three lines of ash)
method_summary: Ash taken with the five brahma-mantras and applied in three horizontal lines, each line standing for a fire, a letter of Oṃ, a guṇa, a world, a power, a Veda and a deity (Kālāgnirudra); for all four stages of life.

queries: e-text refs of prc:tripundra
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 6 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text. Some rest on teachings whose ref was corrected or only partly confirmed; the content is located, only the numbering changes: tea:jabali-upanisad:3-4 (partially-confirmed); tea:kalagnirudra-upanisad:1-2 (partially-confirmed); tea:kalagnirudra-upanisad:2-three-lines (partially-confirmed); tea:kalagnirudra-upanisad:3 (partially-confirmed).

name: Worship with the Triśatī
method_summary: Worship offering vermilion with each of the three hundred names of the Triśatī, which together unfold the fifteen syllables of the mantra.

name: Entering another's body (grong 'jug)
method_summary: Summary: the transference of one's consciousness into a dead body, which it revives — 'casting off and taking up like a snake's skin'; by the tradition's account practised by Marpa's son Darma Dode and thereafter lost in Tibet. No method details are recorded.

equivalents.note: the Hindu yogic power of entering another body (the Śaṅkara legend, YS 3.38); the Kagyu presents it as a transference practice for others' benefit

warnings.text: Requires mastery over wind and mind and stability in both stages; a companion keeping the pledges is to be cherished.

name: Yantra exercises ('khrul 'khor)
method_summary: Summary: sets of physical movements combined with breath holding (in the Karṇatantravajrapada six root and thirty-nine branch exercises) used with inner heat to clear obstacles in the channels. No method details are recorded.

warnings.text: Improper practice of the wind yogas is taught to cause wind disorders; the exercises are learned only from a teacher (tradition's teaching; see obs:wind-disorder-from-practice).
Taught only orally in retreat settings; not to be learned from books.

alt_method_summary: Sequences of movements combined with breath holding, practised in retreat with the completion stage and in Dzogchen (in Bön the trulkhor of the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü). Summary only.

name: Channels and winds (rtsa rlung)
method_summary: Yogic exercises of the channels and winds (visualization of the channels, breath and movement) that prepare for the completion stage and Dzogchen; in Bön from the Mother Tantra and the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü. Summary only.
prerequisites: preliminaries
transmission from a teacher

warnings.text: Forcing the breath or visualization causes wind disorders (srog rlung): practise only as taught and gently.

name: Monastic debate on valid cognition (bsdus grwa / rtsod pa)
method_summary: The Tibetan monastic training in epistemology through formal debate: a defender answers a challenger's consequences about definitions, divisions and pervasions, beginning with the Collected Topics and proceeding to the Pramāṇavārttika.

equivalents.note: the Nyāya practice of debate; both aim at truth and codify defeat

alt_method_summary: In the Gelug curriculum debate extends beyond epistemology to all five great texts; the challenger's clap and the defender's formal answers train precise analysis, and debate is regarded as a form of analytical meditation.
notes: Contribution of U47 (Sakya/Kadam/Gelug presentation).

name: Feast offering (tshogs 'khor, gaṇacakra)
method_summary: A gathering in which food and drink are consecrated as nectar and offered to the deities and guests, with confession and restoration of samaya; held on the tenth and twenty-fifth days of the lunar month.

name: Dhutaṅga wandering (tudong)
method_summary: Wandering alone or in small groups through forests and mountains, dwelling under a klot (umbrella tent) in forests, caves and charnel grounds, living on alms and practising meditation, facing fear and hardship.

equivalents.note: the Thai forest form of the ascetic practices

name: Taking the tuḷsī necklace (Vārkarī initiation)
method_summary: A senior Vārkarī places the tuḷsī-bead necklace (māḷ) on the new member, who vows to keep the vārī, to be vegetarian and abstain from intoxicants, to observe ekādaśī and to remember the name.

name: Service of tulasī
method_summary: Watering, circumambulating and worshipping the tulasī plant, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, and wearing and chanting on tulasī beads.

name: Inner heat (gtum mo, caṇḍālī)
method_summary: Summary: a completion-stage yoga of the channels, winds and drops in which inner heat is kindled and the drops melt, giving rise to the four joys, bliss-warmth and non-conceptuality; the root ('main trunk') of the six yogas. No method details are recorded here.

equivalents.note: both raise an inner fire/energy through a central channel; the Buddhist practice aims at clear light and bliss-emptiness, not the union of Kuṇḍalinī and Śiva — the traditions keep them distinct

prerequisites: empowerment
preliminaries
a teacher's direct guidance
signs_of_progress: signs like warmth, smoke, fireflies, a lamp, and the sky; bliss; thoughts ceasing; hot and cold mixing (bka' dpe phyi ma)

warnings.text: If one does not know the fourfold application there is danger that qualities turn into faults; the remedies are countless; the armour of inner heat is important.
The breath-and-wind practice must be learned from the guru's mouth.

name: Sleeping without sleeping (Śiva-yoga sleep)
method_summary: Remaining in the unceasing 'sleep of Śiva-yoga', senses withdrawn and awareness awake (Pattirakiriyār 1–2; Kuṭampai 6).

equivalents.note: sleep-like state kept aware; different texts and methods

name: Turning the hearing back (Avalokiteśvara's perfect penetration)
method_summary: Reversing the hearing to hear the self-nature: entering the stream of hearing, forgetting sound and hearing, until the self-nature becomes the supreme way (Śūraṅgama juan 6).

warnings.text: The fifty demonic states arising in meditation are not to be taken as sagehood.

name: Uccāra: contemplation of the breath (āṇava means)
method_summary: Āṇava contemplation of the vital breath in its five forms as it moves between the heart, the object and the dvādaśānta, recognizing seven successive blisses - one's own, the bliss-less, supreme, Brahman's, great, of consciousness and of the world (TĀ 5.43-52).
signs_of_progress: the seven ānandas; the five signs (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇi) of TĀ 5.101-111

name: Udakakarma (water-offerings for the dead)
method_summary: Relatives offer water (with sesame) to the deceased after the cremation and during the days of impurity; not done for infants under two (YS 3.1).

queries: local YS 3.1-5
checks.note: The cited YS 3.1–2 contains only the rule for infants ('ūnadvivarṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ') and the cremation. The water-offering itself is at YS 3.3–5: kinsmen enter the water on the seventh or tenth day, 'apa naḥ śośucad agham' facing the south; the udakakriyā for the maternal grandfather and teacher; the offering once with name and gotra. Correction: ref widened to 3.1-5; rests_on unchanged.

correction_log.reason: The cited YS 3.1–2 contains only the rule for infants ('ūnadvivarṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ') and the cremation. The water-offering itself is at YS 3.3–5: kinsmen enter the water on the seventh or tenth day, 'apa naḥ śośucad agham' facing the south; the udakakriyā for the maternal grandfather and teacher; the offering once with name and gotra. Correction: ref widened to 3.1-5; rests_on unchanged.

name: Uḍḍīyānabandha (the flying-up lock)
method_summary: Drawing the belly back (paścimatāna) above and below the navel, so that the breath, bound, 'flies up' in the suṣumnā like a great bird (HYP 3.55-59; GS 3.10-11; ŚS 4.48; DYŚ 129-130; GŚ 35 places it above the penis and below the navel). In breath-control it is applied at the end of retention and the beginning of exhalation (HYP 2.45); the Gheraṇḍa applies it at the end of inhalation in sagarbha retention (GS 5.50).
signs_of_progress: the lion to the elephant of death; even the old become young; practised six months it conquers death (HYP 3.57-59; DYŚ 129-130)
the best of locks; when firm, liberation comes naturally (HYP 3.60; GS 3.11)
the navel purified, the belly-fire blazes (ŚS 4.49-50)

warnings.text: It is to be received from the guru and practised in a solitary, settled place.

name: Meditation on the udgītha
method_summary: Venerate the syllable Om as the udgītha, the highest essence, and the udgītha as the breath in the mouth untouched by evil; what is done with knowledge, faith and the upaniṣad is more powerful (ChU 1.1-1.12; BAU 1.3).

queries: prepared segments: ChU 1.1-1.12, BĀU 1.3
checks.note: All 2 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ChU 1.1-1.12; BĀU 1.3). It rests on 4 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Ujjāyī ('the victorious')
method_summary: With the mouth closed, the breath is drawn slowly through both nostrils so that it sounds from throat to heart, held, and released through the left nostril (HYP 2.51-53); in the Gheraṇḍa the breath is drawn in through the nostrils and held in the mouth with jālandhara, as far as one is able without strain (GS 5.70-73). It may be done walking or standing (HYP 2.53).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm in the throat, increases the bodily fire, destroys disorders of the channels, dropsy and the tissues (HYP 2.52-53)
no phlegm disease, indigestion, āmavāta, consumption, cough, fever or spleen disease (GS 5.72-73)

warnings.text: As a lion, an elephant or a tiger is tamed only slowly, so the breath must be brought under control gradually; otherwise it kills the practitioner.
Proper breath-control destroys all disease; improper practice produces all disease — hiccup, asthma, cough and pains in the head, ears and eyes arise from the disturbed breath.
Draw the breath in slowly and release it slowly; do not hold it excessively nor release it quickly.
The breath is held 'as far as one is able, without opposition' (āśakti … avirodhataḥ).

name: Living by gleaning (uñchavṛtti)
method_summary: The ascetic livelihood of gleaning grain left in the fields, praised in the Mokṣadharma and in the mongoose's story, where the gleaner's gift of his last food outweighs a great sacrifice (MBh 14.92–93; 12.184.18; 12.340–353).

name: Entering the mind-less state (unmanī-bhāva)
method_summary: Thinking of no element, no above or below, being like wood, making the mind 'void of void', free of thought and motionless, until the jīva is dissolved and not roused by any sound.
signs_of_progress: insensibility to outer sound; freedom from decay (KJN 14.85–86)

name: Wandering alone like a madman
method_summary: Having closed the doors of the senses with the intellect, he wanders alone as if mad, taking discarded food; people call him mad and foolish. Kauṇḍinya: the madness is a feint to delude worldly examiners.

name: Giving without support
method_summary: Giving without resting on the notion of any object, sign, giver or recipient; its merit is immeasurable like space.

name: Upadhāna
method_summary: A period of several weeks during which laypeople live like mendicants under a teacher, fasting on alternate days and studying the liturgical sūtras, after which they are formally entitled to recite them (restricted in its fasting component: summary only).

name: Upakosala's meditation (upakosala-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate breath, joy (ka) and space (kha) as brahman, the fires as its forms, and the person seen in the eye as the self, the immortal, the fearless, brahman; the knower goes by the path of light and does not return.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

queries: prepared segments: ChU 4.10-4.15
checks.note: All 1 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ChU 4.10-4.15). It rests on 3 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: Whispered repetition — upāṃśu japa
method_summary: Uttering the mantra slowly, the lips moving slightly, barely audible even to oneself; a hundred times better than ritual sacrifice.

equivalents.note: one of the three modes

name: Upanayana (initiation into Vedic study)
method_summary: The boy asks to become a student; the teacher takes his hand, invests him with girdle (of muñja grass for a brāhmaṇa), staff, deerskin and (later) sacred thread, and teaches him the Sāvitrī; he is now 'twice-born' with the Sāvitrī as mother and teacher as father. Due at eight, eleven or twelve years for the three classes (ŚB 11.5.4; ĀśGS 1.19–22; MDh 2.36–40; 2.169–171).

queries: local text at the cited refs
evidence: text:sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/gretil_devanAgarI/1_sanskr/6_sastra/4_dharma/smrti/manu-smrti_plain_text.md (GRETIL, Kullūka vulgate numbering; M = Medhātithi numbering)
checks.note: ŚB 11.5.4, ĀśGS 1.19–22 ('aṣṭame varṣe brāhmaṇam upanayet', 1.19.1) and MDh 2.36–40 and 2.169–171 were found. This rests on confirmed teaching checks: tea:satapatha-brahmana:11.5.4.1-12, tea:asvalayana-grhyasutra:1.19.1-7, tea:manusmrti:2.36-39, tea:manusmrti:2.169-171.

name: Recollection of peace (upasamānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting the qualities of nibbāna — the disillusionment of vanity, elimination of thirst, termination of the round, cessation; reaches access and suits the intelligent.
signs_of_progress: faith and gladness
access concentration

name: Full ordination (upasaṃpadā)
method_summary: Ordination as bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī by a formal act (motion and three proclamations) before a quorum, after going forth; for bhikṣuṇīs, dual ordination by both orders after two years as probationer.
notes: Common to all the Vinayas; details and counts differ by school.
prerequisites: pravrajyā
age of twenty
robes and bowl
freedom from impediments
alt_method_summary: Admission to the Saṅgha: first 'Come, monk', then by the three refuges, then by a formal act of the Saṅgha; for nuns by both Saṅghas (Vin Mv 1; Cv 10).

name: The eight-limbed fast-day vow (upavāsa)
method_summary: A lay person takes eight precepts from another in the morning, in a humble posture, repeating the formula, without ornaments, for one day and night: four limbs of morality (not killing, stealing, unchastity, lying), one of heedfulness (no intoxicants), three of the vow (no high beds, no ornaments/entertainment, no food after noon).
duration: until the next sunrise

name: Development of equanimity (upekkhā)
method_summary: Pervading the directions with a mind of equanimity; abandons aversion (MN 62; DN 13).
alt_method_summary: Developed after the third jhāna of the other three, looking on beings as owners of their kamma; reaches the fourth jhāna; near enemy the equanimity of unknowing, far enemies greed and resentment.

warnings.text: Guard against the near enemy, which resembles the virtue, and the far enemy, its opposite.

equivalents.note: YS 1.33's maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā as attitudes for calming the mind; the Visuddhimagga develops them to absorption

name: Uposatha observance
method_summary: On the eighth, fourteenth and fifteenth of the fortnight lay followers keep the eight precepts and monks assemble to recite the Pātimokkha (AN 8.41; Vin Mv 2).

name: Ūrdhvapuṇḍra (vertical Vaiṣṇava mark)
method_summary: Vertical marks of gopīcandana clay applied with mantras at twelve places (householder) or fewer (students, forest-dwellers, ascetics; the paramahaṃsa one on the forehead) (Vāsudeva).

queries: e-text refs of prc:urdhvapundra
checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 2 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text. Some rest on teachings whose ref was corrected or only partly confirmed; the content is located, only the numbering changes: tea:vasudeva-upanisad:1-3 (partially-confirmed).

name: Wearing the upright mark (tirumaṇ)
method_summary: Daily application of the vertical white clay mark with the central line for Śrī on the forehead and body, a sign of belonging to the Lord.

name: The upright mark in gopīcandana
method_summary: Marking the forehead (and body) with the upright Vaiṣṇava mark in gopīcandana clay, praised as purifying and required for rites to bear fruit.

name: Uṣṭra-niṣadana (sitting like a camel)
method_summary: Named among the examples of posture in Vyāsa's bhāṣya on YS 2.46 ('posture is steady and comfortable'). The bhāṣya gives only the name; its form is explained by the commentators (Vācaspati Miśra, Vijñānabhikṣu and others), whose descriptions are not reproduced here.
notes: Name certain; form per commentators not recalled with confidence.

name: Uṣṭrāsana (the camel)
method_summary: Lying face down, the feet turned up behind and held with the hands, the mouth and belly firmly contracted (GS 2.41).
notes: The Gheraṇḍa's form is prone, unlike the modern kneeling posture of this name.

name: Utkaṭāsana (the squat on the toes)
method_summary: The ground supported by the toes, the heels raised, the anus set upon the heels (GS 2.27). It is the posture taken in water for basti (HYP 2.26; GS 1.46).

name: Yogic departure from the body (utkrānti)
method_summary: The Kubjikāmata's chapter 23 teaches the yogin's voluntary departure from the body at death. Restricted: title only.

name: Yogic departure from the body (utkrānti) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The perfected yogin is said to be able to leave the body at will and merge in Brahman (DYŚ 115); the Haṭhatattvakaumudī has a chapter on a breath practice for it. No method is recorded.

name: Forced departure through the skull (utkrānti)
method_summary: A practice for leaving the body by driving the breath upward so that the skull splits and the jīva goes to the spotless; recorded only as the text's claim, without method.

warnings.text: Presented as a 'proof of liberation' for the adept; the texts keep such teachings secret from the untested.

name: Yogic departure at death
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: Summary of the Gītā's account only: at the time of departure, with unmoving mind, devotion and the power of yoga, the breath is settled between the brows (8.10); the gates (of the body) are restrained, the mind confined in the heart, the breath placed in the head, and, established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā), one utters Oṃ, remembers the Lord and leaves the body, going to the supreme goal (8.12–13). The Gītā gives no further method.
prerequisites: a mind trained by repeated practice (8.8)
the power of yoga (yoga-bala) (8.10)
devotion (bhakti) (8.10)

alt_method_summary: The yogin, choosing the time of death, withdraws the mind, restrains the breaths and leaves the body through the crown, either for immediate liberation or for the gradual ascent (BhP 2.2.15-31). Summary only.

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): at death one goes up through the channel to the crown and reaches immortality (KU 2.3.16; ChU 8.6.6); saying 'Om' one rises by the sun's rays (ChU 8.6.5); the person made of mind goes out through the indrayoni (TU 1.6); through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind one goes upward (MaiU 6.21). Summary only.

warnings.text: Addressed to the accomplished yati; the Vāyavīya asks how the practiser who dies before completing yoga avoids becoming a self-killer (ātmahā).

name: Pacification of portents (utpāta-śānti)
method_summary: When portents of sky, atmosphere or earth appear, the king has pacification performed in the realm: rites and gifts calm the earthly, soften the atmospheric, and — with abundant gifts of gold, food, cows and land, cow-milking at a Rudra shrine and the ten-million oblation — calm even the heavenly.

warnings.text: Some teachers hold that heavenly portents are not calmed by pacification.

name: Uttānakūrmāsana (the supine tortoise)
method_summary: From the bound kukkuṭa position the neck is clasped with the arms and one lies back like a tortoise on its back (HYP 1.24; GS 2.33).
prerequisites: kukkuṭāsana

name: Uttānamaṇḍūkāsana (the supine frog)
method_summary: From the frog posture, holding the head with the elbows and lying back like a frog (GS 2.35).
prerequisites: maṇḍūkāsana

name: Spoken (audible) repetition — vācika japa
method_summary: Uttering the mantra aloud with its proper high, low and circumflex tones and clear words and syllables; ten times better than ritual sacrifice.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in tone or letter does not convey the meaning intended; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer.

equivalents.note: one of the three modes

name: Discussion for truth (vāda)
method_summary: Examining a question with a partner by thesis and counter-thesis, proving and refuting only with the means of knowledge and tarka, within accepted tenets, in the five-membered form, aiming at ascertainment rather than victory.
prerequisites: knowledge of the means of knowledge and of the members
signs_of_progress: ascertainment (nirṇaya)
cutting of doubts

name: Debate for determining the truth (vāda)
method_summary: Debate aimed only at ascertaining the truth, as between teacher and disciple, following the rules of the Kathālakṣaṇa; the maṭhas continue the practice in scholarly disputations.
notes: The maṭha disputations (e.g. during the Cāturmāsya) are recalled, not verified.

name: Cutting the flows (vāhaccheda)
method_summary: Arresting the left and right currents of breath at the heart, as taught by Kṣemarāja, by the silent utterance of vowelless sounds, so that the centre opens (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary, no method given here).

name: Rule-based devotional practice (vaidhī sādhana)
method_summary: Performing the limbs of devotion — hearing, chanting, worship, fasts, vows — because scripture commands them, under a guru, until spontaneous attraction arises.

name: Initiation of the medical student
method_summary: At an auspicious time the fasting, bathed, ochre-clad student brings the requisites; the teacher kindles the fire, offers to Brahmā, Agni, Dhanvantari, Prajāpati, the Aśvins, Indra and the sages, and before fire, brahmins and physicians instructs him in the vows (celibacy, truth, no meat, no weapons, obedience, service of all beings, never harming the sick); the student assents. Mantras not recorded.
prerequisites: examination of the student's qualities (Vi 8.8)

name: Veneration as the whole path (vinaya)
method_summary: (Jain report) The vainayikas venerate gods, the king, ascetics, kin, elders, the lowly, mother and father, by mind, speech, body and gifts, holding this discipline alone to lead to the good.

warnings.text: They call the true untrue and the bad good.

notes: Lineage recorded as the reporting tradition; no vainayika school is otherwise known.

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Lower: the consciousness of mastery (vaśīkāra-saṃjñā) of one free of thirst for seen and scripture-taught objects; by the power of discerning insight the mind sees the faults of objects, and has a consciousness of mastery without engagement and empty of rejecting and taking (YS 1.15, YBh 1.15). Higher: freedom from thirst for the guṇas themselves, from knowing the puruṣa (YS 1.16); Vyāsa: 'only the clearness of knowledge', of which kaivalya is inseparable (YBh 1.16). Dispassion makes the stream toward objects barren (YBh 1.12).

signs_of_progress: The yogin's own thought at the higher dispassion: 'What was to be attained is attained; the afflictions to be destroyed are destroyed; the linked chain of becoming is cut' (YBh 1.16).

warnings.text: Through dispassion (alone) comes absorption into prakṛti, not liberation.
External contentment from abstaining from objects, without knowledge of the principles, does not liberate.

alt_method_summary: Turning away from objects by seeing the faults of acquiring, guarding, losing, attachment and harm (external dispassion), and seeing even pradhāna as like a dream or magic show (internal dispassion); with practice, a support of meditation.

Cultivating freedom from thirst for objects seen and heard of in scripture, by seeing their faults through reflection (1.15, YBh 1.15); higher dispassion, from discernment of the puruṣa, is freedom from thirst for the guṇas (1.16); dispassion even toward the highest powers yields kaivalya (3.50).
Living without attachment to the world, knowing the body a bubble (Kaṭuveḷi 3), like a lotus leaf on water (Pattirakiriyār 54).
With practice, the means by which the restless, hard-to-restrain mind is held (6.35).
Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses is among the items called knowledge (13.9); non-attachment is the weapon that cuts the aśvattha (15.3).

name: Observances for the unseen (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Ablution, fasting, celibacy, residence in the teacher's household, forest-dwelling, sacrifice, giving, sprinkling, and observances regarding directions, lunar mansions, mantras and times — undertaken for the unseen result (adṛṣṭa).

warnings.text: Fasting is listed without further prescription; no durations are given in the sūtra (prolonged fasting is not described here).

name: Yoga: the mind abiding in the self (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Withdrawing the mind from contact with the senses so that it abides in the self, where the embodied one has neither pleasure nor pain; through a particular conjunction of self and mind the yogin perceives the self.
signs_of_progress: absence of pleasure and pain while embodied
perception of the self

name: Vaiṣṇavī mudrā
method_summary: The inner target held while the gaze is outward and unblinking (Śāṇḍilya 1.31); in the Nādabindu, the seal held while listening to the inner sound in the right ear.

name: Meditation on the self common to all men (vaiśvānara-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate the vaiśvānara self as the whole — sky as head, sun as eye, wind as breath, space as trunk, water as bladder, earth as feet — 'a span in size and beyond measure', not as any one of its parts; the first morsels of food are then offered into it as an agnihotra.

warnings.text: Each partial meditation is incomplete, and the king says each would have come to harm (losing head, sight, breath...) without the whole teaching (ChU 5.12-17).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Vaiyāvṛttya (service)
method_summary: Serving teachers, ascetics, novices, the sick and the community with food, medicine, care and help — an internal austerity.

name: Vājapeya
method_summary: A soma rite of 'the drink of strength', with a chariot race, granting pre-eminence.

queries: local VS 9.1

name: Virilization (vājīkaraṇa)
method_summary: The branch that restores potency and fertility for the continuity of lineage. Summary only: no formulations recorded.

warnings.text: Virilization applied to an unpurified body is fruitless.

prerequisites: purification of the body (AHS Utt 39.4 extends the dirty-cloth warning to it)

name: The Vajra Guru mantra
method_summary: Recitation of oṃ āḥ hūṃ vajra guru padma siddhi hūṃ, the mantra of Padmasambhava, in guru yoga and as a continuous devotional practice.

name: Vajra recitation (vajrajāpa)
method_summary: Joining the three syllables OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ with the natural movement of the wind (entering, abiding, leaving), after recognizing the wind's five-coloured nature at the nose tip; the first stage (speech isolation) of the Pañcakrama.
prerequisites: consecration
stable generation stage

warnings.text: This reality is sealed in the Samāja and must be understood through the explanatory tantras and the guru's mouth.

name: Singing songs of realization (mgur)
method_summary: Spontaneous or traditional vajra songs sung by teachers and practitioners, often at gaṇacakra feasts, as teaching and as expression of realization.

name: Vajrakīla practice
method_summary: Sādhana of the wrathful Vajrakīla, embodiment of enlightened activity, to remove obstacles, practised in major Nyingma cycles and in annual monastic ceremonies.

name: Vajrāsana (the thunderbolt seat)
method_summary: The thighs made firm like a thunderbolt and the feet placed by the sides of the anus (GS 2.12); it is the seat for khecarī in the Śivasaṃhitā (4.31) and for śakticālana in the Haṭhapradīpikā (3.114-115). HYP 1.37 records vajrāsana as another name for siddhāsana.
signs_of_progress: gives success to yogins (GS 2.12)

name: Vajrasattva meditation and recitation (the hundred-syllable mantra)
method_summary: Vajrasattva is visualized above the head; with the four powers (support, regret, resolution, antidote) one recites the hundred-syllable mantra while nectar flows down, washing out wrongdoing and obscurations; Vajrasattva declares them purified and dissolves into oneself.
signs_of_progress: dreams of bathing, vomiting impurities, wearing white, flying (purification signs)
alt_method_summary: Visualizing Vajrasattva above the head and reciting his hundred-syllable mantra while nectar washes away negative karma and broken pledges, with the four powers of confession.
Recitation of the hundred-syllable mantra of Vajrasattva with visualization, to purify faults and repair broken pledges.
notes: The mantra's occurrence in the Tattvasaṃgraha is recalled, not checked; the preliminary-practice use is chiefly documented in Tibetan sources.

name: Vajravārāhī practice
method_summary: The consort of Cakrasaṃvara as yidam (Vajrayoginī / Vajravārāhī, often in Nāropa's form); her fifteen-goddess empowerment 'indicated by symbol' ripens for the six dharmas.

name: Making the body adamantine (vajrīkaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhairava's own practice by which he survived dissolution: meditation on the innate centre in the bone-circle and on nested lotuses flooded with milk-white nectar, so that the body stands 'like a thunderbolt'. Summary only.

warnings.text: 'This most secret teaching is to be guarded with effort.'

name: Vajrolī, amarolī and sahajolī
method_summary: RESTRICTED — summary only: practices for the retention and 'drawing back' of bindu (semen, and in women rajas) through upward contraction, which the texts say let even one living as he pleases, outside the yogic rules, succeed; amarolī is ascribed to the Kāpālikas of the Khaṇḍa school and sahajolī involves smearing with ash (HYP 3.83-103; DYŚ 137-145). The Dattātreyayogaśāstra places them in the haṭha of Kapila and his followers (DYŚ 29). No procedure, material or quantity is reproduced. The Gheraṇḍa's 'vajrolī' is a different, posture-like practice (see prc:vajroli-gheranda).

warnings.text: Most secret; not to be given to anyone, only to one as dear as one's own life.
It succeeds only for the meritorious, steadfast, seers of truth and the unenvious — not for the envious.
Death comes from the fall of bindu, life from holding it; semen and mind are to be guarded with effort.
At the start of practice women, fire and travel are to be avoided.
Union with women causes loss of bindu; the yogin should avoid their company.
When women desire the yogin at the beginning stage, union destroys his bindu, shortens life and weakens him — a great obstacle.

alt_method_summary: Named in the Yogatattva among haṭha practices concerned with retaining bindu; recorded by name only.

name: Vajrolī in the Gheraṇḍasaṃhitā (the arm-supported lift)
method_summary: Supporting the ground with both hands, both legs and the head are thrown up into the air; the sages call it vajrolī, for awakening the power and for long life (GS 3.45-48).
signs_of_progress: mastery of bindu; the cause of liberation; success even for one given to enjoyment (GS 3.46-48)
notes: A different practice from the Haṭhapradīpikā's vajrolī sharing only the name and the aim of mastering bindu; not restricted.

name: Vajrolī mudrā
method_summary: U21 contribution: a practice for drawing up and preserving bindu, in the context of which the Haṭhapradīpikā says death comes by the fall of bindu and life by its retention. Summary only.

warnings.text: A restricted practice concerning sexual fluids; only its purpose (retention of bindu) is recorded.

name: Restraining speech in the mind, and the mind in ever finer selves (Kaṭha 1.3.13)
method_summary: The discerning one restrains speech in the mind, that in the self that is knowledge, that in the great self, and that in the peaceful self; the text states the sequence only.

checks.note: Entity read against the teachings it rests on and their segments: faithful; level not raised by J.

name: Worship of Vālai / Maṉōṉmaṇi at the root and on the Meru
method_summary: The Siddhars' Śākta worship: the goddess Vālai (Bālā), mother Maṉōṉmaṇi, is worshipped at the root centre with her three syllables and on the Meru of forty-three triangles (the Śrīcakra), with the syllables of Tripurā, Bhuvanā and Yāmaḷā, after the five initiations (Rāmatēvar; Caṭṭaimuṉi). Mantras and procedure not recorded.

equivalents.note: the Meru of 43 triangles is the Śrīcakra

prerequisites: initiation (tīṭcai)

warnings.text: Worship done 'by the deluded' becomes waste; the Meru needs initiation, 'a small child cannot touch it'.

name: Vāmakrama bhālabhāti (alternate-nostril form)
method_summary: Breathing in through iḍā and out through piṅgalā, then in through piṅgalā and out through iḍā, without force (GS 1.56-57).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm disorders (GS 1.57)

warnings.text: One should not do it forcefully.

name: Vamana-dhauti (washing by vomiting)
method_summary: After a meal water is drunk to the throat, the gaze turned upward for a moment, and the water vomited (GS 1.39).
signs_of_progress: removes phlegm and bile (GS 1.39)
notes: Recent teaching calls a comparable practice kuñjala; that name is not in the Gheraṇḍa.

equivalents.note: Both empty the stomach upward; gajakaraṇī does it by raising apāna to the throat, vamana-dhauti after drinking water.

name: Obeisance and adoration (vandana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna bows his head to the Lord with joined palms (11.14); does homage trembling and bowing low (11.35); offers homage a thousand times, in front, behind and on every side (11.39–40); and, bowing and prostrating his body, seeks the Lord's grace and forgiveness (11.44).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch10-12): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; no change needed.

alt_method_summary: Bowing, prostrating and adoring the Lord with joined palms. Sixth of the Bhāgavata's nine forms. Tamil toḻutal: 'O my mind, worship his radiant feet and rise' (TVM 1.1.1); the Gītā's 'bow to me' (BhG 9.34).
Formal veneration of the teacher (guru-vandana) and of the Jina (caitya-vandana) with bows and recitations.

equivalents.note: Pāśupata prostration as an offering to Rudra

notes: One of the Bhāgavata's nine forms of devotion (prc:navadha-bhakti, U07). Exemplar: Akrūra.

name: Recitation and veneration of the Vāṇī
method_summary: Reading and singing the saint's collected utterances (Dādū Vāṇī; Amritbāṇī of Ravidās) in the panth's seats and gatherings, the book itself being honoured.

name: Day-wise breath (vāra caram)
method_summary: The Tirumantiram's third tantra has sections on the breath flowing through the left or right nostril by weekday (vāra caram, vāra cūlam), read by the Siddhas; summary only.

equivalents.note: svara lore of the nostril breath

notes: Section titles checked in the local TM e-text; contents not summarized.

name: Worship of Vārāhī (Daṇḍinī)
method_summary: Worship of Vārāhī, Lalitā's general, with her own cakra and enclosures. Taught in section 7 of the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra. (Summary; no mantras.)
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā) from a qualified guru into the relevant vidyā

name: The vārī: walking pilgrimage to Paṇḍharpūr
method_summary: Twice a year (above all for Āṣāḍhī ekādaśī, again for Kārtikī) Vārkarīs walk to Paṇḍharpūr in singing companies (diṇḍī) behind the palanquins bearing the sandals of Jñāneśvar from Āḷandī and Tukārām from Dehu, singing abhaṅgas and the name by day, holding kīrtan and bhajan at the halts, keeping the ekādaśī fast, bathing in the Candrabhāgā and taking darśan of Viṭṭhala (or of the temple's pinnacle when the crowds are too great). Those who keep it for life are Vārkarīs.
prerequisites: wearing the tuḷsī necklace (for Vārkarīs proper)
vegetarian diet and abstinence on the road
duration: about three weeks on foot for the Āṣāḍhī vārī from Āḷandī/Dehu; lifelong observance
signs_of_progress: the saints' company experienced as the tīrtha
longing for Paṇḍharpūr as for a mother's home

equivalents.note: a specific, recurring, congregational pilgrimage with its own inner meaning

name: Vārisāra (inner washing with water)
method_summary: Water is drunk slowly until the body is filled to the throat, moved through the belly and expelled downward (GS 1.17-19).
signs_of_progress: cleans the body; one who practises it with effort gains a divine body (GS 1.18-19)

warnings.text: Vārisāra is most secret.

notes: Later (recent) teaching calls a comparable practice śaṅkhaprakṣālana; that name is not in the Gheraṇḍa.

name: Vārkarī kīrtan
method_summary: A kīrtankār takes an abhaṅga as text and expounds it in song and speech, illustrated by the saints' lives, while a chorus with cymbals (ṭāḷ) and drum repeats the refrain and the name ('Jñānobā Tukārām', 'Rāma Kṛṣṇa Hari'); it ends with the name and the Pasāydān. Nāmdev is remembered as its founder.

name: Varṇa: the letters and resonance in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through the 'letter' (varṇa) - the unstruck resonance and seed-syllables contemplated with the breath (TĀ 5).

name: Placing the letters and forms of Viṣṇu (nyāsa)
method_summary: Placing on one's body the fifty letters as the fifty forms of Viṣṇu (Aja, Ānanda, Indra ...) and the parts of the mantras, as part of worship.

equivalents.note: Dvaita's nyāsa places forms of Viṣṇu, not Śākta or Śaiva deities.

prerequisites: dīkṣā

name: The rains retreat (varṣā)
method_summary: Three months of residence in one place during the monsoon, a time of intensified practice and study.
notes: Common to all the Vinayas; details and counts differ by school.

name: The year-long fast (varṣī-tapa)
method_summary: In memory of Ṛṣabha's long fast, a practitioner alternates fasting days and eating days for about a year, ending on Akṣaya Tṛtīyā with sugarcane juice (restricted: prolonged fasting — summary and warnings only).

warnings.text: Austerity is to be undertaken according to one's strength; fasting for fame or reward (nidāna) is faulty.

name: Cessation of vāsanās and saṃskāras as the text states it
method_summary: The text states that vāsanās are held together by cause, fruit, support and object and cease when these are absent (4.11); that the earlier saṃskāra whose seed is burnt by the fire of knowledge no longer yields cognition (bhāṣya 4.28); and that with the destruction of the seeds of saṃskāra no other cognitions arise and dharma-megha follows (4.29). It gives no separate method here.

name: Vase breathing (bum pa can)
method_summary: A gentle retention in which the breath is drawn down and held below the navel in the shape of a vase, used in tsa-lung, inner heat and as the basis of other yogas. Summary only: no counts or durations.
prerequisites: instruction from a teacher
the nine-round purification breath

notes: Owned by U45 (brief). Also a Kagyu and Gelug practice (other units).

name: Vāci yoga (the Siddhar breath-yoga)
method_summary: Summary only: the Siddhars' mastery of the breath, imaged as binding the 'horse of twelve feet' (TM 722), placing the prāṇa in vāci after initiation (Caṭṭaimuṉi 4), so that the body becomes firm and long-lived and the breath is turned inward towards the root and crown. No counts, ratios or retention times are recorded.
