prerequisites: initiation (tīṭcai) and a guru
signs_of_progress: the texts claim an undecaying body and long life (TM 722)

warnings.text: Kāya-citti and vāci are joined to initiation (tīṭcai) and the guru; 'the Siddhars' worship' requires initiation.
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).

notes: Restricted as a retention-based practice; the texts' claims are recorded as claims.

name: Vastra-dhauti (washing with a cloth; vāso-dhauti)
method_summary: A moistened strip of fine cloth is slowly swallowed as the guru teaches and then drawn out again (HYP 2.24; GS 1.40). The measurements the texts give are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: cough, asthma, spleen disorders, skin disease and the twenty diseases of phlegm vanish (HYP 2.25)
gulma, fever, spleen disorders, skin disease, phlegm and bile destroyed; health, strength and nourishment increase (GS 1.41)

warnings.text: One with excess fat or phlegm should first practise the six acts; others should not do them, their doṣas being in balance.
Some teachers hold that all impurities are dried up by breath-control alone and do not approve of the other acts.
The six acts, which purify the body, are to be kept secret.
Dhauti is done 'by the way the guru teaches'.

name: Vātasāra (inner washing with air)
method_summary: With the mouth shaped like a crow's beak (kākī) air is slowly drunk, moved in the belly and released slowly by the lower passage (GS 1.15-16).
signs_of_progress: cleans the body, destroys all diseases, increases the bodily fire (GS 1.16)

warnings.text: Vātasāra is most secret.

name: Vāyavī dhāraṇā (air-concentration)
method_summary: The breath held with the mind in the air-principle, like a heap of collyrium, smoky, with ya and Īśvara (GS 3.77); between the brows, 'whirling' (GŚ 72, 74). Durations are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: gives the power of moving in the sky; destroys old age and death; one does not die by wind (GS 3.77-78)
notes: One of the five dhāraṇās counted among the Gheraṇḍa's twenty-five mudrās; see prc:element-dharanas.

name: Drinking the breath (vāyu-pāna)
method_summary: A group of practices in the Śivasaṃhitā for removing afflictions: drinking the breath with the tongue at the root of the palate; drinking cool air through the crow's-beak mouth; drinking with the tongue pressed at the cavity of the front teeth while contemplating kuṇḍalinī; drinking with the teeth pressed together and the tongue turned up (ŚS 3.68-83); the Gorakṣaśataka similarly has the yogin press the tongue-tip at the cavity of the front teeth and contemplate the goddess of nectar (GŚ 63-64).
signs_of_progress: destroys fatigue, burning, old age and disease; claims of conquering death, becoming a poet, becoming like Bhairava with the powers (ŚS 3.71-78; GŚ 64)
notes: Where these practices merge into khecarī (the tongue turned up into the cavity) the restrictions of prc:khecari-mudra apply.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 1: Fullness at the two points where the breath arises
method_summary: The supreme [Goddess], whose nature is emission (visarga), sounds forth as prāṇa above and as jīva (the in-breath) below; by dwelling on and filling the two places where they arise, the state of fullness (bharitā sthiti) comes about.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 24 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Commentators identify the two places as the heart and the dvādaśānta (Kaumudī: 'utpattau dvādaśānte dvitīye hṛdi'). First dhāraṇā in Ānandabhaṭṭa's count as well.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 10: The same method on a void, a wall or a worthy vessel
method_summary: By this very method, contemplation on anything whatever - on a void, on a wall, on an excellent person (pātra) - dissolves of itself and grants the boon.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 33 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 100: Neither attachment nor aversion
method_summary: One should not cultivate aversion anywhere, nor attachment anywhere; in the middle, free of attachment and aversion, Brahman spreads.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 126 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 101: The unknowable and the void as Bhairava
method_summary: What is unknowable, ungraspable, void, what lies in non-being - all that is to be contemplated as Bhairava; at its end, awakening arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 127 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 102: The mind in outer space
method_summary: Placing the mind in outer space - eternal, supportless, void, pervasive, free of limitation - one enters the spaceless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 128 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 103: Letting go of each object the moment the mind goes to it
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, abandoning that very thing at that very moment, by not letting it settle, one becomes waveless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 129 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 104: Continuous utterance of the word 'Bhairava'
method_summary: 'He makes all resound through fear (bhayā ... ravayati), he gives all, he pervades the whole' - by continuously uttering the word 'Bhairava' [with this sense], one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 130 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 105: At the thought 'I' and 'mine'
method_summary: When notions such as 'I', 'this is mine' arise, the mind goes to the supportless; impelled by meditation on that, one becomes calm.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 131 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 106: Contemplating the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless'
method_summary: Meditating at every moment on the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless', 'pervasive', 'lord of all', according to their meaning, one attains one's aim.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 132 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 107: 'What reality has a magic show?'
method_summary: 'All this, without reality, stands like a magic show; what reality has a magic show?' - by firmness in this, one goes to peace.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 133 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Illusion imagery used as a contemplation; relevant to the Advaita/Śaiva dispute on the world.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 108: The unchanging self: the world as void
method_summary: For the unchanging self, where is knowledge, where is action? External things depend on knowledge; therefore this world is void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 134 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 109: 'No bondage, no liberation for me'
method_summary: 'For me there is no bondage, no liberation; these are bugbears for the frightened; this [world] is a reflection in the intellect, like the sun in waters.'
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 135 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The Kaumudī reads 'bālasyaitā vibhīṣikāḥ' (bugbears for a child).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 11: The mind within the skull, eyes closed
method_summary: Placing the mind within the skull and remaining with eyes closed, gradually, through the mind's steadiness, one discerns the highest object.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 34 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 110: Withdrawing from the senses into the self
method_summary: All contact with pleasure, pain and the like comes through the doors of the senses; so, abandoning the senses, one abides in oneself, established in one's own self.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 136 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 111: Knowledge and the known as one
method_summary: Knowledge reveals everything, and the self is the revealer through everything; because they have a single nature, knowledge and the known are to be contemplated as one.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 137 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 112: Dissolution of mind, awareness, power and self
method_summary: When the four - mind, awareness (cetanā), power (śakti) and self (ātman) - have dissolved, beloved, then there is Bhairava's form.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 138 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī glosses: mind = manas, cetanā = intellect (buddhi), śakti = the breath-power, ātman = the limited individual.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 12: The central channel like a lotus fibre
method_summary: The central channel (madhyanāḍī), situated in the middle, [is to be meditated on] in the form of a lotus fibre; by that goddess, meditated as inner space, the God shines forth.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 35 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 13: Closing the sense-doors: the bindu between the brows
method_summary: Blocking the eyes with the 'weapon' of the hands, piercing at the brows and closing the doors [of the senses]: when the point (bindu) is seen and gradually dissolves, in its midst is the supreme state.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 36 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Resembles the haṭha ṣaṇmukhī mudrā (see equivalents).

equivalents.note: Closing the sense-openings with the hands; the VBT adds the seen bindu

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 14: The bindu like a subtle spark, at the crest or in the heart
method_summary: For one who meditates on the point (bindu) - shaped like a subtle fiery mark arising from agitation within the light-abode (dhāma) - at the end of the crest (śikhānta) or in the heart, at the end of dissolution there is absorption.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 37 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 15: The unstruck sound (anāhata)
method_summary: One who is immersed in the Sound-Brahman - the unstruck (anāhata), unbroken sound, [heard] in the ear as a vessel, rushing like a river - attains the supreme Brahman.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 38 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). 'pātrakarṇe' is read differently in the recensions.

equivalents.note: Absorption in the inner unstruck sound

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 16: Uttering Oṃ and resting in the void at its end
method_summary: By uttering the praṇava (Oṃ) and the like, and contemplating the void at the end of its prolonged (pluta) sound, one goes to voidness by the supreme void power, O Bhairavī.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 39 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī: the sixteenth (ṣoḍaśī) dhāraṇā - agrees with this count.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 17: The void before and after any sound
method_summary: One should contemplate the beginning and the end of any sound (varṇa) whatever; by the void [power] such a person becomes void, of the form of the void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 40 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 18: The fading sounds of stringed instruments
method_summary: In the long, successive sounds of stringed and other instruments, one whose mind is on nothing else becomes, at the end of each, of the form of the supreme space.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 41 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 19: A seed-mantra dissolved into its subtle phases and the void
method_summary: Of any compound seed-mantra (piṇḍamantra), by [uttering] its gross letters in order and then, through the half-moon (ardhendu), the point (bindu), the resonance (nāda) and its end, by uttering the void, one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 42 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 2: The two voids at the turning points of the breath
method_summary: When the breath, moving inward or outward, does not turn back from the two spaces [at its ends], thus, O Bhairavī, the form of Bhairava is revealed through Bhairavī.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 25 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī counts this 'the second' (dvitīyā).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 20: The body as space in all directions at once
method_summary: One should contemplate space in all directions simultaneously in one's own body; for one whose mind is free of thought-constructs, everything becomes space.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 43 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī: 'now he states the twentieth (viṃśatitamī) dhāraṇā'.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 21: The voids above, at the root and in the heart
method_summary: Whoever contemplates simultaneously the void 'behind/above' (pṛṣṭha) and the void at the root becomes void-minded through the power independent of the body (44). One should contemplate steadily the void above, the void at the root and the void in the heart; from this simultaneous freedom from thought, the thought-free state arises (45).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 44-45 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Grouped: the Kaumudī recension (KSTS 9) has one verse combining 44a and 45b.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 22: Voidness in a part of the body, for a moment
method_summary: One should contemplate voidness in [any] part of the body even for a moment; free of thought-constructs, one comes to share the nature of the thought-free.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 46 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 23: The body's substance pervaded by space
method_summary: O doe-eyed one, one should contemplate all the substance within the body as pervaded by space; then that contemplation of his becomes steady.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 47 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 24: The skin as a wall with nothing within
method_summary: One should contemplate the skin as a wall enclosing the body, with nothing inside it; meditating thus, one comes to partake of what cannot be meditated upon.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 48 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 25: The space of the heart-lotus
method_summary: One whose senses are dissolved in the space of the heart, dwelling in the middle of the closed lotus, with mind on nothing else, O fortunate one, attains the supreme fortune.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 49 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 26: Dissolving the mind in the dvādaśānta
method_summary: By dissolving the mind in the dvādaśānta of one's own body on all sides, for one of firm understanding the mark of reality becomes firm.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 50 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 27: Casting the mind into the dvādaśānta at any time
method_summary: However and wherever [one may be], one should cast the mind into the dvādaśānta; for one whose mental activity wanes moment by moment, an extraordinary state arises within days.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 51 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).
signs_of_progress: an extraordinary state 'within days' (v. 51)

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 28: One's own body burnt by the fire of time
method_summary: One should contemplate one's own 'city' (the body) as burnt by the fire of Kālāgni rising from the place of time (kālapada); at the end, the appearance of peace arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 52 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Commentators take 'the place of time' as the right big toe (interpretation).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 29: The whole world burnt
method_summary: In the same way, having meditated, by imagination, on the whole world as burnt, a person whose mind is on nothing else attains the supreme state of the person (pumbhāva).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 53 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 3: Suspension of the breath-power in the centre
method_summary: When the power (śakti) in the form of breath neither goes out nor enters and [the centre] has expanded, through the absence of thought-constructs in the middle, by that [power] there is the state of Bhairava.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 26 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 30: Dissolving the tattvas into the subtler
method_summary: Having meditated on the tattvas of one's own body or of the world as dissolving into the subtle and the still subtler, at the end the Supreme (Parā) is revealed.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 54 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 31: The power, thick then thin, in the twelve and in the heart
method_summary: Having meditated on the power (śakti), [first] thick and [then] feeble, in the field of the twelve (dvādaśa), and entering and meditating in the heart, one is liberated and attains freedom (svātantrya).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 55 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 32: The paths of the cosmos, gross to supreme
method_summary: One should contemplate the whole in the form of the path of worlds (bhuvanādhvan) and the other paths, step by step, in its gross, subtle and supreme condition, until at the end the mind dissolves.

name: Vedic study (vedādhyayana / svādhyāya)
method_summary: Learning one's own Vedic recension by recitation from a teacher, as enjoined by 'one's own Veda is to be studied'; in the Mīmāṃsā account it precedes, and makes possible, the inquiry into the meaning of Vedic sentences.
prerequisites: initiation into Vedic study (upanayana), per Dharmaśāstra

name: Contemplation of feelings (vedanānupassanā)
method_summary: Knowing each pleasant, painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as such, and as worldly (sāmisa) or unworldly (nirāmisa) (MN 10:32-33).

checks.note: Level not raised (entities are not promoted by the spot-check). By code: every linked id resolves in data/ or these shards; no restricted flag; no modern/psychological/health wording found. Content not read line by line by J.

alt_method_summary: Knowing pleasant, painful and neutral feelings as they are, worldly or unworldly (MN 10); feeling only the first dart (SN 36.6).

name: Vedic recitation (vedapāṭha, svādhyāya of the Saṃhitā)
method_summary: Learning and reciting one's śākhā's Saṃhitā orally from the teacher's mouth, phrase by phrase, with exact accents marked by hand movements, first in the continuous form, then word by word and in the interwoven recitations; daily recitation of the Veda is itself counted a sacrifice (brahmayajña). The Soma book says whoever studies the purifying verses eats purified food (RV 9.67.31).
prerequisites: upanayana (initiation) by a teacher of the śākhā
duration: years of daily study; the complete Saṃhitā with its modified recitations traditionally takes a decade or more (as reported; low confidence)
signs_of_progress: mastery of the Saṃhitā, then pada, krama and the vikṛtis
the six virtues of a reciter (sweetness, distinctness, word-division, accent, composure, tempo)

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
One who recites the Veda without understanding its meaning is a post bearing a load; what is repeated without understanding never blazes, like dry fuel without fire.
Studying without the hand-gestures, lacking accent and letters, one is 'burned' by the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman.

name: Initiation by piercing (vedha-dīkṣā)
method_summary: The rarest initiation, in which the guru's power pierces the disciple's centres; given only to a rare, fit disciple (Kulārṇava 13.79; 14.66). Summary only.

warnings.text: It is not to be given to anyone at all; such a guru and such a disciple are both rare.

name: Breath-control with Oṃ, the utterances and the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Breath-control performed while mentally reciting the Gāyatrī with its 'head', preceded by the utterances and with Oṃ, as part of the twilight worship and as the renouncer's austerity; it burns away the faults of the senses (MDh 6.70–72; YS 1.23; VDh 10.5).
notes: No retention counts or durations are recorded here.

name: Not suppressing the natural urges
method_summary: Do not hold back the arisen urges of urine, faeces, semen, flatus, vomiting, sneezing, belching, yawning, hunger, thirst, tears, sleep and breath after exertion; nor force them.

warnings.text: All diseases arise from forcing or suppressing the urges.

name: Abstaining from meat (Mahāyāna)
method_summary: Not eating meat, fish or (in some texts) the five pungent plants, out of compassion for beings seen as one's relatives in past lives; prescribed by the Laṅkāvatāra (ch. 8), the Mahāparinirvāṇa and the Brahmajāla precepts.
notes: Not required in the Pali Vinaya (see dsp:is-meat-eating-permitted); Tibetan practice varies.

name: Night rite in the great cremation ground (literary)
method_summary: Summary only: in Bāṇa's Harṣacarita the Śaiva adept Bhairavācārya performs a mantra-rite at night in the great cremation ground, guarded by the king and disciples.
notes: Named 'vetāla-sādhana' in scholarship; the text's details were not checked in this run.

name: Contemplating the Lord in his manifestations (vibhūti)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Asking how he may know the Lord while constantly contemplating him, Arjuna asks in which beings and states the Lord is to be thought of (10.17). The Lord names himself as the self in all beings and as the chief of each class of gods, seers, beings, things, sounds, times and qualities (10.20–39), and gives a rule for all else: whatever being is glorious or mighty is to be known as sprung from a portion of his splendour (10.41). Whoever knows his manifestation and yoga in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7).
notes: New practice for 10.17–41, combining extractor A's prc:vibhuti-cintana and extractor B's prc:contemplating-the-lord-in-his-vibhutis. The text does not name it as a technique; it is implied by Arjuna's question (cintya, paricintayan, 10.17) and the rule of 10.41, and the text gives no further procedure.

signs_of_progress: One who knows this vibhūti and yoga of his in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7).

name: Wearing sacred ash (vibhūti) and tripuṇḍra
method_summary: Applying ash consecrated with 'namaḥ śivāya' as three horizontal lines on the forehead and fifteen places of the body; one of the eight shields.

name: Inquiry (vicāra) as the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha teaches
method_summary: Reflecting, with scripture and the wise, on 'who am I? what is this world?', discriminating the Self from body, senses and mind until the seen is known not to exist apart from consciousness; Cūḍālā's daily self-questioning is the model.

method_summary: Renunciation by one who has attained knowledge, as the natural expression and protection of liberation while living (the paramahaṃsa life).

name: Wandering on foot (vihāra)
method_summary: Outside the rains, mendicants travel on foot only, never in vehicles, staying a limited time in any place, watching the ground to avoid harming beings (the carefulness in walking).

name: Dissolution of thought-constructs (vikalpakṣaya)
method_summary: Letting thought-constructs subside by fixing awareness at the heart and not thinking of anything, one comes to rest in the thought-free centre (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary).

name: The eight modified recitations (vikṛti)
method_summary: Jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha and ghana: permutations built on the krama that lock the order of every word of the text.
notes: List as traditionally given; the source ascription is low-confidence.

name: Vinaya (reverence)
method_summary: Reverence toward knowledge, right view, conduct and the worthy, expressed in respectful conduct toward teachers.

name: The base of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatana)
method_summary: Attending to the consciousness that pervaded the space as 'infinite consciousness'. Preceded by mastery of the fourth jhāna on a kasiṇa.
prerequisites: fourth (fifth) jhāna on a kasiṇa with mastery

name: Viparītakaraṇī (the inverting technique)
method_summary: Because the sun at the navel swallows the nectar that drips from the moon at the palate, causing old age, the body is inverted — 'navel above, palate below; sun above, moon below' — the head on the ground (with the hands supporting) and the legs raised (HYP 3.77-79; GS 3.33-35; ŚS 4.45; DYŚ 133-135; GŚ 55-59). It is begun for a moment and lengthened a little day by day (HYP 3.81-82; DYŚ 135). In the Gorakṣaśataka and Vivekamārtaṇḍa it is taught as pratyāhāra, the 'withdrawal' of the nectar from the sun.

warnings.text: It increases the digestive fire, so ample food must be provided; if food is scanty the fire burns the body at once.

It is to be learned from the guru's instruction, not from millions of treatises.
To be learned from the guru's mouth.
The practitioner must eat plenty, otherwise the fire quickly consumes the body.

alt_method_summary: Inverting the relation of sun (navel) and moon (palate) — navel above, palate below — so that the nectar is not consumed by the sun.
An inverted posture-seal named in the Yogatattva; the text warns that the practitioner must then eat sufficiently or the fire consumes the body.

name: The rites of the royal expedition (yātrā)
method_summary: For a king's march: choosing the day, asterism, moment and rising sign; examining the purity of the planets and bodily omens; worship of the guhyakas; observing dreams; the bathing rite; the sacrifice to the planets; the departure; and the omens on the way (BJ 28.4–5 listing the Yātrā's contents).

name: Drawn-out recitation of the Buddha's name (Jingzhong)

name: One-practice samādhi (yixing sanmei)

name: The practice-hut (maṭha, kuṭīra) and the place of practice
method_summary: The haṭha yogin lives and practises alone in a small hut with a small door and no windows or holes, neither too high nor too low, smeared with cow-dung, clean and free of creatures, walled, with water nearby, in a righteous, well-governed and prosperous land free of trouble (HYP 1.12-14; GS 5.5-7; DYŚ 49-54; ŚS 3.20, 3.35). Practice is not to be begun in a far country, a forest, a capital or a crowd (GS 5.3-4).

warnings.text: In a far country there is no trust, in a forest no food, in a crowd one is exposed — so begin yoga in none of them.

name: The eight limbs of yoga as a practice (yogāṅga-anuṣṭhāna)
method_summary: The practice of the eight limbs (YS 2.29) destroys impurity, and the light of knowledge rises up to discriminative discernment (YS 2.28); it is the cause of separation from impurity and of attaining discernment (YBh 2.28).

name: Yogāsana (the yoga seat)
method_summary: The feet, turned up, placed on the knees and the hands, turned up, on the seat, drawing in the breath and gazing at the nose-tip — a posture for yoga-practice (GS 2.44-45); also listed in the Triśikhibrāhmaṇa.

name: Installing the raptures in the body (borān kammaṭṭhāna)
method_summary: After preliminary rites and a formal request to the teacher, the meditator induces the five kinds of rapture in order, each fixed at a prescribed place in the body with Pali syllables, before proceeding to further qualities — summary only.

name: Worship of the circle of yoginīs (Kaula cakra rite)
method_summary: Kaula worship of the sixty-four yoginīs and the eight-by-eight circles in a secluded place with food, fish, meat and wine, with a Śakti partner; recorded only in summary.

warnings.text: To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.
One fallen from the pledge (samaya) is a paśu; dualistic attitude in the rite is condemned.

name: Propitiation of yoginīs (yoginī-sādhana)
method_summary: Rites to win the favour of yoginīs for powers, set out in the Kaula and eastern digests (Tantrasāra, third pariccheda). Restricted: named only.

name: Yoni mudrā as a hand-gesture in Śākta worship
method_summary: A gesture of the hands forming the yoni, shown to the goddess after meditation in Śākta worship (named repeatedly in the Śāradātilaka's rites, e.g. with the śaṅkha, cakra and mahāmudrā); distinct from the haṭha yoni mudrā.
notes: The form of the gesture is not described here; its details were not verified.

name: Yoni mudrā (the womb seal)
method_summary: In the Gheraṇḍa: seated in siddhāsana, the ears, eyes, nostrils and mouth are closed with the fingers, prāṇa is drawn in by kākī and joined with apāna, the six centres are contemplated in order with the mantra 'huṃ haṃsa', the sleeping serpent-goddess is roused and led with the jīva to the supreme lotus, and one contemplates union with Śiva — 'I am Brahman' (GS 3.37-42); it is the means to laya-samādhi (GS 7.12-13). In the Śivasaṃhitā it is the contraction of the yoni between anus and genitals with meditation on the flame rising from the brahma-yoni (ŚS 4.1-11), perfected by mūlabandha (ŚS 4.42). The Haṭhapradīpikā mentions it as holding bindu (HYP 3.43).
signs_of_progress: one established in it even once is in samādhi (GS 3.42)
makes defective mantras effective (ŚS 4.6)

warnings.text: Yoni mudrā does not succeed without first practising śakticālana.
It is most secret; it is not to be given to anyone, not even with one's life in one's throat.

equivalents.note: The Gheraṇḍa's yoni mudrā includes the closing of the six openings that is elsewhere the whole of ṣaṇmukhī; the Śivasaṃhitā's yoni mudrā is a perineal contraction.

notes: The texts' claims that it removes even the great sins are arthavāda in their own manner.

name: Wise attention
method_summary: Attending to 'this is suffering … this is the way' rather than to questions about one's existence in past and future (MN 2); attending to the bases of the awakening factors and to the foulness sign to starve the hindrances (SN 46.51).

name: Declining the invitations of the high stations (YS 3.51)
method_summary: As the bhāṣya on 3.51 states it: when gods of high stations invite the yogin who has realised the madhumatī stage, he reflects on the faults of attachment (that he has obtained the lamp of yoga in the darkness of saṃsāra and would be deceived by a mirage of sense-objects), dismisses the offers as dream-like, and cultivates samādhi; having no attachment he also feels no pride, for pride would make him think himself secure, and heedlessness watching for a gap would stir the afflictions again.
prerequisites: realisation of the madhumatī stage (bhāṣya 3.51)

name: Worship of the divine couple (yugala-upāsanā)
method_summary: Worship and meditation on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa together — Rādhā on Kṛṣṇa's left, served by the sakhīs — in the Nimbārka school, with Braj songs of the couple's play (Yugalaśataka, Mahāvāṇī).
alt_method_summary: In the Rādhāvallabha and Haridāsī traditions the pair are worshipped together as inseparable, Rādhā supreme (Rādhāvallabha) or the natural pair in the grove (Haridāsī).

name: Keeping the mind yoked (yukta manas)
method_summary: As stated in the simile only: understanding as charioteer holds the reins of the mind so that the senses obey; the text gives no technique here, only the condition and its result (reaching the highest place, no rebirth).

checks.note: Entity read against the teachings it rests on and their segments: faithful; level not raised by J.

name: Yuthok Nyingthig: guru yoga and practice of the physicians
method_summary: The physician's spiritual path: preliminaries, guru yoga of Yuthok, generation and completion practices, so that medicine and Dharma are practised together.

equivalents.note: guru yoga with Yuthok as the guru

name: Interfusing nenbutsu with the name register
method_summary: Practitioners inscribe their names in a register and pledge a daily number of recitations, whose merit interfuses with that of all others.

name: Zazen / zuochan (seated meditation)
method_summary: Sitting upright in full or half lotus on a cushion, hands in the cosmic mudrā (left on right, thumbs touching), eyes half-open, breathing naturally through the nose, letting go of involvements; in the Platform Sūtra's redefinition, 'sitting' is thoughts not arising toward objects and 'meditation' is seeing the unmoving self-nature. In Sōtō it is just sitting; in Rinzai the seat of kōan work.

warnings.text: Fixing the mind and viewing stillness is a sickness, not meditation; long sitting constrains the body without benefit.
Sitting with an empty mind falls into indeterminate emptiness.
Taking quiet as the ultimate is to be captured by heretical silent-illumination Chan (Dahui).

equivalents.note: Chan redefines seated meditation so as not to be a pursuit of absorption states.

name: Assisted recitation for the dying (zhunian)
method_summary: Companions recite Amitābha's name beside the dying, in turns, voice following voice, to support his recollection until the ten recitations are complete; the body is not moved and no one weeps.

warnings.text: Strictly avoid moving the body or weeping, lest the dying one lose right mindfulness.
